docs.title: HoloDeck - AI Agent Experimentation Platform
docs.text: HoloDeck is an open-source experimentation platform for building, testing, and deploying AI agents through YAML configuration. Define intelligent agents entirely through configuration—no code required.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• No-Code Agent Definition: Define agents, tools, and evaluations in simple YAML files
  • Multi-Provider Support: Anthropic and local Ollama via the Claude backend; OpenAI and Azure OpenAI via the OpenAI Agents backend
  • Flexible Tool Integration: Vector stores, custom functions, MCP servers, and AI-powered tools
  • Built-in Testing & Evaluation: Run evaluations with multiple metrics, customize models per metric
  • Multimodal Test Support: Images, PDFs, Word docs, Excel sheets, and mixed media in test cases
  • Agent Server: Deploy agents as REST APIs or AG-UI endpoints for integration with web apps
  • OpenTelemetry Observability: Built-in tracing, metrics, and logs with OTLP export

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text:
uv tool install holodeck-ai@latest --prerelease allow --python 3.11

Installation Guide | Quickstart Tutorial

docs.title: Project Status
docs.text:
Version: 0.3.0

  • Core configuration schema (Pydantic models)
  • YAML parsing and validation
  • Environment variable support
  • CLI interface (holodeck command with init, test, chat, serve)
  • Agent execution engine (LLM provider integration, tool execution, memory)
  • Interactive chat with spinner, token tracking, and adaptive status display
  • Evaluation framework (AI-powered and NLP metrics with threshold validation)
  • Agent Local Server with REST API and AG-UI endpoints
  • OpenTelemetry instrumentation with OTLP export
  • Multi-agent orchestration (planned for v0.4)

All notable changes to HoloDeck will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Planned Features
docs.text:
• Deployment Engine: Registry push (holodeck deploy push) and cloud deployment (holodeck deploy run)
  • Plugin System: Pre-built plugin packages for common integrations
This section also lists the changes that shipped in 0.7.0 and 0.7.1, which had no section of their own.

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.7.x
docs.text:
This release removes Semantic Kernel and splits the install into feature extras. Read this list before you upgrade. The same steps with commands are in the upgrade guide.

  1. Check your install extras (BREAKING). pip install holodeck-ai no longer installs DeepEval, anthropic, ollama (new eval extra), nltk, rouge-score, sacrebleu (new nlp extra), optuna (new optimizer extra) or opensearch-py (new opensearch extra). MkDocs Material and Twine left the runtime requirements for the dev extra. The new all extra installs every runtime extra. A test run whose configuration selects a metric without its extra stops before any agent or model call and prints the install command (MissingExtraError); holodeck test optimize and an OpenSearch keyword index do the same. Commands that do not use these features still start. The vector store MissingClientError is now a MissingExtraError with the same attributes.
You ran Now run pip install holodeck-ai and use DeepEval or NLP metrics pip install "holodeck-ai[eval,nlp]" pip install holodeck-ai and use holodeck test optimize pip install "holodeck-ai[optimizer]" (add eval,nlp for its metrics) pip install holodeck-ai and use an OpenSearch keyword index pip install "holodeck-ai[opensearch]" pip install holodeck-ai and want everything as before pip install "holodeck-ai[all]"
  1. Update retired metric names (BREAKING). Azure AI evaluation and azure-ai-evaluation are removed (042 T18); DeepEval metrics replace them. An agent.yaml that names a retired metric fails when the configuration loads, before any agent or model call, and the error names the replacement. HoloDeck does not translate old configuration, and scores are not equivalent: re-run the suite and set new thresholds. Stored runs that used these metrics still open in the dashboard. See Removed Azure AI metrics.
Removed metric: Use instead (DeepEval) groundedness type: rag, metric_type: faithfulness relevance type: rag, metric_type: answer_relevancy coherence type: geval with coherence criteria fluency type: geval with fluency criteria similarity type: geval with evaluation_params: [actual_output, expected_output] safety type: geval with safety criteria
  1. Update retired vector store providers (BREAKING). The faiss, sql-server and azure-cosmos-mongo providers had no install extra, sample or live test and could not run from a documented install. An agent.yaml or global config.yaml that names one fails at config load with a migration message, before any backend, embedding or agent call. Stored runs that name a retired provider still open in the dashboard. The published agent.schema.json lists only the eight supported providers.
Removed provider Use instead faiss chromadb (embedded, local files) or in-memory sql-server postgres (pgvector) azure-cosmos-mongo azure-cosmos-nosql

  1. Check your vector collections. Plain text chunking changed (BREAKING for stored chunks): TextChunker is now a HoloDeck splitter (tiktoken cl100k_base) instead of Semantic Kernel's characters/4 estimate. chunk_size is a hard per-chunk token limit, chunk_overlap tokens are repeated at the start of the next chunk, and splits prefer paragraph, line, sentence, then word boundaries. chunk_overlap >= chunk_size and a non-default separator_list now raise ValueError; an unset vectorstore chunk_overlap defaults to 50 capped at a quarter of chunk_size, and an explicit 0 is honored. Collections now record the pipeline that wrote them in a companion holodeck_manifest collection. A tool refuses writes to a collection written by a different pipeline and lists the inputs that differ; searches still work. Collections created before this release stay usable and are marked legacy, with their old chunks until re-ingested. Run holodeck vectorstore inspect for a read-only report, then holodeck vectorstore migrate to rebuild into a new collection (resumable and verified; the old collection is kept until prune). See the vector stores guide.

  2. Download the METEOR data once. METEOR no longer downloads NLTK data on first use. When wordnet, punkt_tab or omw-1.4 is missing it raises NLPMetricsError that names the resource and the command python -m nltk.downloader wordnet punkt_tab omw-1.4. Run that command once on each machine that scores METEOR.

  3. A missing vector store client is an error. A vectorstore or hierarchical_document tool no longer falls back to in-memory storage when the provider's client library is missing or the provider name is retired. The tool fails with the install command or the migration text. A failure while the store adapter is created still falls back to memory. A client that connects on first use (Qdrant, for example) raises its connection error; it does not fall back.

  4. ChromaDB scores changed. Chroma returned a cosine distance that was used as the similarity score, so semantic results ranked worst-first and min_similarity_score kept the least similar chunks. Scores are now 1 - distance, and the best match ranks first. Review any threshold you tuned against the old ranking.

  5. MCP 2 is allowed. The mcp range is >=1.30.0,<3 (was <2) and the lock moves mcp 1.30.0 to 2.3.0. claude-agent-sdk 0.2.179 and openai-agents 0.24 accept it, and both backends pass the offline smoke run and make verify-live on 2.3.0.

  6. Rebuild deployment images. holodeck deploy build and the base image install an exact HoloDeck version with dependency versions constrained to that release's uv.lock. They no longer use --prerelease. See the Changed section for the options and the build manifest.

  7. Semantic Kernel is removed (BREAKING for Python imports). semantic-kernel is no longer a dependency of any install profile. Every vector store provider runs on a native adapter behind holodeck.lib.retrieval, and embeddings and contextual-retrieval chat run on LiteLLM. Existing Qdrant, Chroma and Postgres collections stay readable and writable: their layout is frozen under tests/fixtures/legacy_layout/ and checked against the native adapters. Removed Python surfaces: the holodeck.lib.vector_store module (QueryResult and StructuredQueryResult now live in holodeck.lib.retrieval), the SK bridge adapter, holodeck.lib.observability.enable_semantic_kernel_telemetry with its SK_OTEL_* constants, and holodeck.lib.keyword_search.get_keyword_search_strategy with its provider-name sets (the adapter's capabilities choose the hybrid strategy). HoloDeck no longer sets the SEMANTICKERNEL_EXPERIMENTAL_GENAI_ENABLE_OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS variables. No agent key named Semantic Kernel remains (the last one, metrics.include_semantic_kernel_metrics, went in 0.7.0). The default of observability.logs.filter_namespaces changes from ["semantic_kernel"] to []. The lock no longer allows pre-releases globally (tool.uv.prerelease is removed), the azure-search-documents cap is relaxed from <12.1 to <13, and the lock goes from 378 to 347 entries at this step (376 to 329 over the whole dependency work).

Other breaking changes in this release, not part of the dependency work: Python 3.11 or later is required, the tool_filtering agent field is removed, the Claude backend isolates settings by default, and more built-in Claude tools need a declaration. Each has its own entry below.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Pipeline fingerprint, ingestion completion marker and holodeck vectorstore. Retrieval collections now record the pipeline that wrote them (embedding provider, model and dimensions, parser and chunker policy and settings, record layout, contextual embeddings) in a companion holodeck_manifest collection; the layout of existing collections is unchanged. A tool refuses writes to a collection written by a different pipeline and lists the inputs that differ; searches still work. Collections created before this release stay usable and are marked legacy. Each ingested source is marked incomplete before its chunks are written and complete after, so an interrupted ingestion is redone on the next start. New commands: holodeck vectorstore inspect (read-only dry run with chunk and token estimates), migrate (rebuild into a new collection, resumable, verified, old collection kept), rollback and prune. See the vector stores guide.
  • Native Weaviate adapter. The weaviate provider runs on the asynchronous weaviate-client 4.x with native vector, BM25 and hybrid search, filtered reads, cursor pagination and source replacement. New weaviate extra (weaviate-client>=4.24,<5, also in vectorstores). The lock adds weaviate-client 4.24.1 and validators 0.36.0 and moves grpcio 1.85.1 to 1.78.2 (the client requires grpcio<1.80). The Semantic Kernel path never worked against a server, so no stored collections change; free-text record IDs are now stored as UUIDv5 with the original in a holodeck_id property, collection names are normalized to Weaviate's rules, and unknown database settings are an error. See the vector stores guide.
  • Native Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL adapter. The azure-cosmos-nosql provider no longer goes through Semantic Kernel's connector, which also needed pymongo to import. New extra azure-cosmos (azure-cosmos>=4.17,<5; the lock adds 4.17.1; also in vectorstores). The container layout is unchanged (partition key /id, float32 cosine embedding policy, same index exclusions). New: HoloDeck picks quantizedFlat above 505 dimensions (SK's flat could not create a container for 1536 dimensions); item IDs with / \ ? # are stored encoded (SK's writes failed on them); writes run concurrently; an existing container with other dimensions or partition key is rejected; unknown database settings are an error. Native hybrid search (ORDER BY RANK RRF) is opt-in with full_text_search: true. Verified on the Linux emulator (all operations except hybrid search) and on a test fake; hybrid search and the Cosmos DB service itself are unverified.
  • Native Azure AI Search adapter. New azure-ai-search extra (azure-search-documents 12.0, azure-identity) and an adapter on the asynchronous clients with vector, keyword and native hybrid search, exact-match filters, key-range enumeration and index creation. hierarchical_document tools now work on Azure AI Search (stale chunks are removed on re-ingestion). The index layout follows what Semantic Kernel created, with differences: record IDs that Azure rejects as keys (paths) are stored Base64-encoded, filterable and searchable are set only where needed, and the key is sortable, so an index created by Semantic Kernel is rejected with a clear error. Entra ID signs in when no api_key is set. Verified against an in-memory fake and the SDK's request shapes on a stub transport; not run against the Azure service yet.
  • OpenAI Agents native backend (Feature #035) — model.provider: openai and azure_openai now run on a first-class backend built directly on the OpenAI Agents SDK (Agent + Runner), replacing the former Semantic Kernel agent path. Verified end-to-end against Azure OpenAI with the financial-assistant sample (hierarchical-document RAG over Qdrant + numeric eval).
  • Tools: Python function tools, plus vectorstore and hierarchical_document RAG tools (reusing the same .search()/embedding layer as the Claude backend; surfaced to the model as {name}_search).
  • MCP: stdio / sse / http transports map to the SDK MCP server classes with ${VAR} env/header substitution and per-server allowed_tools static filtering; transport: websocket is skipped with a warning.
  • Structured output: response_format (JSON-schema dict or file path) drives the SDK output type; strict mode auto-enables when the schema qualifies. Note: OpenAI structured outputs reject oneOf — use anyOf (the same schema works on the Claude backend).
  • Reasoning thinking: populated from reasoning-model summaries when effort is set.
  • openai: config block (sibling of claude:): max_turns, effort (low|medium|high|max; max → SDK xhigh), max_budget_usd (per-session cost cap → BackendBudgetExceededError with partial response), fallback_model (one fallback attempt on 429/5xx after primary retries exhaust), disallowed_tools, permissions, and serve-sizing knobs.
  • Tracing: an OTel-mirroring TracingProcessor reflects SDK spans into the HoloDeck OTel pipeline. HoloDeck owns the SDK's process-global processor list through one router with per-backend policies applied per trace, so mixed OpenAI/Azure agents keep their own upload behaviour in either initialization order. provider: openai retains the platform.openai.com upload alongside the mirror; azure_openai never uploads (also with observability disabled); observability.disable_provider_tracing: true forces mirror-only. trace_include_sensitive_data is tied to observability.traces.capture_content (default off) on every run.
  • Subagents / handoffs: openai.agents.<name> entries become SDK handoff targets (transfer_to_<name>), inheriting the parent's tools and MCP servers unless restricted, with model: inherit or an explicit id (Claude aliases rejected) and the SDK's recommended handoff prefix prepended once unless skip_recommended_prefix: true. Handoffs surface on the existing tool-event stream (start/end/parent_link/subagent_message/thinking) so holodeck chat and AG-UI render them like Claude subagents.
  • Skills: new type: skill tool (inline instructions or a path to a SKILL.md directory; YAML-only allowed_tools) validated at config load and, on this backend, translated into a scoped handoff-target sub-agent. claude.setting_sources is accepted for portability and warns that it is ignored on this backend. A runnable full-capability sample lives in sample/openai-agents-full/.
  • Roadmap (not yet shipped on this backend): YAML hooks, hosted tools, default credential-redaction guardrails, and holodeck serve / holodeck deploy (all fully supported on the Claude backend).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Deployment images are pinned and constrained. holodeck deploy build and the base image install an exact HoloDeck version (holodeck-ai[extras]==X.Y.Z, no --prerelease flag), with dependency versions constrained to that release's uv.lock: the wheel now ships holodeck/deploy/constraints.txt and overrides.txt (make constraints; make constraints-check runs in make verify-fast). The base image build needs HOLODECK_VERSION (an exact release) and scripts/build-base-image.sh needs --version; both pin the Python and uv images by digest, and Dockerfile.local no longer pipes the uv installer to a shell. deploy build builds on holodeck-base:<version> of the version it runs. A development version (not on PyPI) needs --wheel or a matching wheel in ./dist; otherwise the build stops before Docker starts. New deploy build options: --wheel, --base-image, --no-pull.
  • Extras in deployment images are chosen from the agent file. One function (holodeck.deploy.extras.required_extras) maps the agent to extras: openai-agents for OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, the vector store extra from the adapter registry (now including weaviate, azure-ai-search, azure-cosmos), opensearch for an OpenSearch keyword index, otel-prometheus and otel-azmon for those exporters, and claude-otel only when Claude-backend tracing is on (before, every Anthropic agent got it and OpenAI agents got no openai-agents). Serving images never get eval, nlp or optimizer.
  • Native Pinecone adapter on client 10. The pinecone provider no longer goes through Semantic Kernel's connector. The pinecone extra is now pinecone>=10,<11 (was pinecone[asyncio,grpc]~=7.0, a dev build); the lock moves pinecone 7.0.2.dev1 → 10.3.0 and drops pinecone-plugin-interface, protoc-gen-openapiv2 and lz4. The index layout is unchanged (serverless, cosine, record ID as the vector ID, data fields as metadata, one namespace). hierarchical_document tools now work on Pinecone: find uses the client's fetch-by-metadata, and stale chunks are removed on re-ingestion. Changes to know: index names are normalized to Pinecone's rules (documents_dim1536 becomes documents-dim1536, which Pinecone rejected before); unknown database settings are an error instead of being passed to the client; use_grpc is ignored (the async client uses HTTP); record IDs must be ASCII. Verified on Pinecone Local with a test-only control plane and on a fake client; no run against the Pinecone service yet. The Dependabot ignore for Pinecone majors is removed.
  • Retrieval tools use HoloDeck's vector store adapter contract. vectorstore and hierarchical_document tools no longer call Semantic Kernel collections directly; collection names and stored layout are unchanged. A changed file's stale chunks are now removed on re-ingestion. A hierarchical_document tool on a provider without filtered reads fails before ingestion instead of re-ingesting silently; every supported provider has filtered reads, so none hits that error today.
  • ROUGE and METEOR run without Hugging Face evaluate. ROUGEEvaluator calls rouge_score directly and METEOREvaluator calls nltk.translate.meteor_score directly, with the same parameters and scores as before (the frozen golden fixtures pass unchanged). Neither metric fetches a script from the Hub. METEOR no longer downloads NLTK data on first use: when wordnet, punkt_tab or omw-1.4 is missing it raises NLPMetricsError naming the resource and the command python -m nltk.downloader wordnet punkt_tab omw-1.4. nltk and rouge-score are in the new nlp extra. CI downloads and caches the data before the tests, the METEOR tests skip with that command as the reason when it is absent, and the evaluation guide documents the one-time download. evaluate, datasets, pyarrow, dill, multiprocess and xxhash leave the lockfile (345 to 339 packages), and the datasets and pyarrow constraints are removed.
  • markitdown[all] replaced by format extras (042 T20): the dependency is now markitdown[pdf,docx,pptx,xlsx], and openpyxl, pandas, pdfminer.six and python-pptx are declared directly. Ten packages leave the lock: azure-ai-documentintelligence, azure-ai-contentunderstanding, youtube-transcript-api, speechrecognition, pydub, olefile, xlrd, audioop-lts, standard-aifc, standard-chunk. Legacy .xls, audio, YouTube and Outlook conversion are not used by FileProcessor. The lock goes from 339 to 329 packages. The explicit azure-ai-contentunderstanding>=1.2.0b1 constraint that the Semantic Kernel removal added (only markitdown[all] needed that pre-release) is dropped, so the lock holds no pre-release outside packages that ship only pre-releases.
  • Fewer direct dependencies. aiofiles, python-dateutil, absl-py, ml-dtypes, requests and the stale sentry-sdk constraint are no longer declared; nothing in src/ imports them. aiofiles and ml-dtypes leave the lockfile (376 to 374 packages). The remote file download and the MCP registry client now use httpx instead of requests (redirects are followed; timeouts are unchanged). anthropic and ollama stay declared because DeepEval's Anthropic and Ollama judge models need them.
  • Remaining major upgrades. temporalio 1.32 → 1.35 (exact pin), opensearch-py 2.8 → 3.2, dash 3.4 → 4.5 and twine 6.2 → 7.0. twine 6.2 could not read wheels with metadata 2.5, so the release twine check was failing.
  • Faster CLI start. Commands now load only their own modules. Every command used to import the evaluation stack (pandas, DeepEval), Semantic Kernel and the agent SDKs at startup: a first holodeck init in a fresh environment drops from about 25 s to 1 s. holodeck test still loads what it needs. This also fixes subprocess tests that timed out on busy CI runners.
  • DeepEval 4 and ChromaDB 1.5. deepeval 3.8.9 → 4.3.3. It needs posthog 7, which chromadb 1.0.x rejects, so the chromadb extras now allow <1.6 (locked 1.5.9). DeepEval 4 also accepts reasoning-model judges such as gpt-6-luna, which 3.8.9 rejected (it sent temperature: 0). The four ignored chromadb advisories are unchanged by 1.5.9.
  • Azure Container Apps SDK 5. azure-mgmt-appcontainers 4.0 → 5.1. SDK 5 returns provisioning_state as an enum, so deploy and status now report its value (Succeeded) instead of ContainerAppProvisioningState.SUCCEEDED. It also stopped sending activeRevisionsMode, allowInsecure and transport by default; the deployer now sets them explicitly, so the request body matches 4.x.
  • OpenAI stack on openai 3. openai 2.54 → 3.48, openai-agents 0.20 → 0.24 and litellm 1.100 → 1.108, moved together: openai-agents 0.21+ requires openai 3, and litellm allows it from 1.108.
  • Agent runtime upgrade. claude-agent-sdk 0.2.121 → 0.2.179 and openai-agents 0.17.4 → 0.20.0. The openai<2.45 cap is lifted. openai-agents 0.21 and later need openai 3, which the next entry covers.
  • Claude tool search is off by default. Claude Code 0.2.17x hides MCP tools behind ToolSearch, so a model must search before it can call an agent's own tools; models behind custom endpoints may never do that. HoloDeck now sets ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false unless the operator exports it.
  • More built-in Claude tools are blocked unless declared. NotebookEdit (writes files) now needs file_system.edit, and WebSearch needs web_search: true. Before, both were available to every agent. The block is session-wide, so a subagent that needs one of these tools still needs it declared at the top level.
  • Breaking: Python 3.11+ required. Python 3.10 reached end of life in October 2026, and the security fixes for Pillow, filelock and dnspython ship only for 3.11+. CI tests 3.11 and 3.13; the base Docker image moves to python:3.13-slim with a pinned uv.
  • Dependency security refresh (2026-11). The lock moves past 155 known advisories in 26 packages (including claude-agent-sdk 0.2.121, mcp 1.30, litellm 1.100, pypdf 7, pillow 13, pyjwt, authlib, aiohttp, urllib3). The NLTK audit exception is retired (3.10.4 fixes it). Two caps added for this refresh (openai below 2.45 and azure-mgmt-appcontainers below 5) were lifted later in this release, by the openai 3 and Azure Container Apps SDK 5 entries.
  • Trace redaction works on OpenTelemetry SDK 1.45+ and covers current GenAI tool attributes. The SDK now freezes span attributes before on_end, which made RedactingSpanProcessor fail open with only a warning. It now unfreezes the shared mapping for the scrub, so processors holding the original span see redacted values too. Byte values are decoded and scrubbed, and a value whose redaction raises is exported as [REDACTED:redaction-failed] instead of the original. gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.tool.call.result (current semconv names used by the Claude Agent SDK instrumentation) were never redacted; they are now.
  • OpenAI Agents backend runs GPT-6 models. Reasoning-model detection only matched o1/o3/o4/gpt-5, so gpt-6* models were sent the default temperature and rejected with HTTP 400. Every gpt-<n> generation from 5 up is now treated as a reasoning model.
  • Verify suite. make verify-fast (all gates and the full test suite), make verify-deps (pip-audit with expiring ignores in security/audit-ignores.toml), make verify-smoke (offline holodeck test + holodeck serve AG-UI on both backends against a local fake provider, including a tool call whose real output is checked) and make verify-live (every supported tool type per backend against real providers, with Qdrant and an Aspire dashboard in Docker and a planted fake secret to confirm trace redaction). The /verify skill picks tiers from the diff. See Reliability.
  • holodeck serve multi-turn on the OpenAI Agents backend. Every serve session now runs its backend inside the session's dedicated actor task (previously only Anthropic did). The OpenAI backend connects stdio MCP servers during initialize(), and that used to happen in the HTTP request task of turn 1, so turn 2 on the same thread failed with ClosedResourceError and an empty reply. Backend errors reported as is_error results are now surfaced by the chat executor (raised when there is no content, logged when a partial response exists) and logged with a traceback by the backend; the AG-UI RUN_ERROR text is backend-neutral.
  • Serve session actor hardening (stack review). A backend that fails during create_session/prepare is now closed and torn down inside the actor task instead of leaking; abandoning close() (for example the session store's 5 s shutdown timeout) cancels the actor, fails the in-flight and queued turns with BackendSessionError, and still runs close/teardown in the actor task; closing from inside the actor no longer raises; concurrent first turns on a fresh session share one backend.
  • Qdrant record IDs: numeric business keys are hashed too. A numeric string such as "42" is not a native Qdrant point ID (only the integer is), so it now maps to the same deterministic UUIDv5 as any other business key; only UUID strings pass through unchanged.
  • Handoff names cannot shadow parent tools. An openai.agents entry or skill whose transfer_to_<name> tool name equals a tool the parent already declares fails config load instead of silently replacing the tool.
  • OpenAI Agents tracing router fails closed on unknown traces. Spans or trace ends whose trace identity the router never saw (or evicted before the span started) are dropped rather than sent to the SDK default exporter.
  • RAG metrics now receive retrieval_context on the OpenAI Agents backend. The test runner only recognised the Semantic Kernel (vectorstore-<name>) and Claude MCP (mcp__holodeck_tools__<name>_search) tool names when collecting retrieval-tool output, so on provider: openai / azure_openai (which report <name>_search) faithfulness and the contextual_* metrics were silently skipped as "requires retrieval_context but none available". Vectorstore and hierarchical-document results are now matched under the OpenAI naming too.
  • vectorstore tools work on Qdrant again. Record IDs are now deterministic UUIDv5 values on provider: qdrant (Qdrant rejects the readable {path}_chunk_{n} keys, which had made ingestion fail with 400 Bad Request), matching what the hierarchical-document tool already did; other providers keep the readable IDs, except where their own entries say otherwise. Plain vector search on Qdrant no longer fails with 'AsyncQdrantClient' object has no attribute 'search': qdrant-client 1.13 removed search, and the native adapter uses query_points.
  • RAG embedding failures now surface instead of degrading silently. A failed embedding call raises EmbeddingServiceError (provider exception chained); vectorstore and hierarchical-document tools no longer fall back to placeholder zero vectors, so a broken provider fails tool initialization or the search with the real cause. Per-tool embedding_dimensions is now sent to the provider as dimensions (one dedicated embedding service per override) rather than only being checked against the returned vector length. LiteLLM's raw-response span attribute, error.* failure attributes, and span-event attributes (the OTel exception event) join the trace redaction, and the emitted embedding/chat span shape (default and OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental) is documented in the Observability guide.
  • Backend routing. openai / azure_openai now route to the OpenAI Agents native backend (previously the Semantic Kernel path); ollama routes to the Claude backend. Selection remains automatic by model.provider.
  • Documentation overhaul. Semantic Kernel is no longer presented as a user-facing backend; a new OpenAI Backend guide is added and the Semantic Kernel Backend guide is removed (Ollama setup migrated into LLM Providers). Every guide now leads with a runnable Quick start section before reference detail.
  • Claude backend now defaults to settings isolation. The spawned claude CLI subprocess no longer inherits plugins, skills, or hooks from ~/.claude or .claude/. HoloDeck passes setting_sources=[] to the SDK unless the agent's YAML opts in via the new claude.setting_sources field. Accepted values: user, project, local, or all. Migration: if your agents relied on host-machine Claude config (e.g. a project CLAUDE.md or a custom skill), add setting_sources: [project] (or the layers you need) to the claude: block. See Claude Backend → Settings isolation.
  • OTel instrumentation bumped to otel-instrumentation-claude-agent-sdk>=0.0.6, which structurally fixes the frozen from claude_agent_sdk import query import path so invoke_agent / execute_tool spans are emitted regardless of how callers reference the SDK's top-level query().

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Semantic Kernel, three vector store providers and the Azure AI evaluation metrics are removed. See "Upgrading from 0.7.x" above (items 2, 3 and 10).
  • Dead Semantic Kernel harness leftovers. Removed SK-coupled surfaces orphaned when the SK agent backend was deleted: the unused holodeck.tools.mcp SK plugin factory (live MCP runs through the Claude SDK bridge), the never-wired holodeck.lib.tool_filter module, the dead to_semantic_kernel_function stub, and the unused metrics.include_semantic_kernel_metrics config field. Semantic Kernel itself is removed (see above).
  • BREAKING: removed the tool_filtering agent-config field. It was parsed but ignored (Claude manages tool selection natively). Because agent configs forbid extra fields, any agent.yaml still setting tool_filtering: will now fail validation — delete the block. No behavior change.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• ChromaDB search results came back worst-first. Chroma returns a cosine distance, which was used as the similarity score, so semantic results were ranked in reverse and min_similarity_score / min_score kept the least similar chunks. Scores are now 1 - distance, so the best match ranks first.
  • Dashboard skipped runs that used a code grader or a file-based skill. Loading a stored run re-validated its agent snapshot, which imported each type: code grader and read each skill's SKILL.md. Those live next to the agent, not the results, so holodeck test view dropped such runs (cannot import grader module, skill path is not a directory). Stored runs now load as snapshots and skip that work; agent.yaml loading still checks both before any agent call.
  • type: code graders now see tool invocations on single-turn test cases. The single-turn path ran evaluations before pairing tool calls with results, so GraderContext.tool_invocations was always empty and any grader that checked tool calls or results scored 0, even though the test result listed the invocations. Calls are now paired once and the same list goes to the grader, the expected-tool arg matcher, and the TestResult. Single-turn graders also receive test_case_name. Multi-turn (turns:) cases were not affected.
  • Code graders get their own copy of tool invocations. A grader that edited ctx.tool_invocations[i].args or .result changed the invocations saved in the TestResult and seen by later graders. Each grader context now holds deep copies.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Evaluation-Runs Dashboard (Feature #031) --Interactive Dash UI for holodeck test run history
  • holodeck test view CLI launches the Dash dashboard as a subprocess with SIGINT forwarding; --seed renders the built-in golden fixture (24 runs, 6 prompt versions) for demos
  • Summary view: pass-rate time series, metric breakdown, sortable/filterable run table, CSV export, prompt-version boundary markers
  • Explorer view: three-column drilldown (runs -> cases -> detail) with full conversation thread, tool-call panels, expected-tools coverage, agent-config snapshot, and metric rows
  • Compare view: side-by-side diff for up to three runs with a persistent floating compare tray (quick-add buttons for 2 or 3 most-recent runs)
  • Dynamic reload: mtime-aware run memo + dcc.Interval polls the results directory every 5 s so new holodeck test output appears without restarting the dashboard
  • Conversation rendering: assistant bubble renders Markdown for prose replies and prettified JSON for structured-output replies (strict {/[ prefix + successful json.loads detection)
  • Optional [dashboard] extra bundling Dash >=3.0, Plotly >=5.20, pandas >=2.0; holodeck test view prints an install hint and exits 2 if the extra is missing
  • Prompt Version Frontmatter (Feature #031 US2) --Optional YAML frontmatter on instructions.file to version and label system prompts
  • Recognised keys: version, author, description, tags; any other keys are preserved under extra on the persisted run record
  • Auto-derives version: auto-<sha256[:8]> from the body hash when no manual version: is supplied, so every run still has a stable identifier
  • Inline instructions (instructions.inline) resolve to source: inline and skip frontmatter parsing entirely
  • Prompt body reaching the LLM is byte-equivalent (frontmatter is stripped); malformed frontmatter fails with a clear ConfigError instead of silently shipping a broken header
  • EvalRun Persistence (Feature #031 US1, US3) --Every holodeck test invocation writes results/<slugify(agent.name)>/<ISO-timestamp>.json
  • EvalRunMetadata snapshot captures prompt version, agent config (redacted via deep-copy), git commit, HoloDeck version, environment, and timing
  • Secrets-bearing fields on the snapshotted Agent are automatically redacted

  • Startup Validators --6 pre-flight checks called during ClaudeBackend.initialize(): Node.js presence, credential validation, embedding provider validation, tool filtering warnings, working directory collision detection, response format schema validation
  • ClaudeSDKContextGenerator --ContextGenerator protocol implementation using Claude Agent SDK query() for contextual embeddings with batch prompts, JSON parsing, single-chunk fallback, retry logic, and concurrency control
  • Shared Tool Initializer (tool_initializer.py) --Provider-agnostic tool initialization used by both SK and Claude backends with 5-tier context generator resolution chain
  • Shared Instruction Resolver (instruction_resolver.py) --Extracted instruction loading (file or inline) from AgentFactory for cross-backend reuse
  • embedding_provider field on Agent model --Required when using provider: anthropic with vectorstore/hierarchical_document tools (Anthropic has no native embedding API)
  • context_model field on HierarchicalDocumentToolConfig --Dedicated LLM for contextual embedding generation, separate from the main agent model
  • embedding_model field on VectorstoreTool and HierarchicalDocumentToolConfig --Explicit embedding model override with cross-tool conflict detection
  • PDF Processor Package (lib/pdf_processor/) --Extracted PDF operations into dedicated package (#265)
  • heading_extractor.py: Dual-strategy heading detection --bookmark-based (preferred) with font-size fallback and fuzzy matching
  • page_extractor.py: Page-range extraction using pypdf with bounds validation

docs.title: Engineering design
docs.text: Start with architecture for code locations and runtime boundaries. Use the design index for decisions and their evidence. The reference index records the external guidance used by this harness.

docs.title: Change contracts
docs.text:
• Preserve declarative agent configuration and published schemas.
  • Keep provider-specific behavior behind backend contracts and adapters.
  • Preserve independent agent execution, evaluation, and deployment engines.
  • Keep deterministic workflow helpers separate from model execution.
  • Validate external values at the boundary before domain logic uses them.
  • Reach vector stores only through holodeck.lib.retrieval: the adapter contract, the registry, and the manifest and fingerprint guard. Do not import a store client in a tool.
  • Keep evaluation on DeepEval, deterministic NLP metrics and code graders. Do not add Microsoft AI evaluation or a retrieval framework.
  • Keep features in install extras. The base install must start without them, and a missing extra must name its install command.
  • Do not depend on Semantic Kernel. A test fails if it becomes importable or named in src/.

The constitution defines product principles. The core beliefs explain engineering tradeoffs.

docs.title: Decision records
docs.text:
For a boundary or contract change, record the problem, alternatives, selected approach, and verification in an execution plan. Use PLANS.md for the plan lifecycle. Link durable decisions from design-docs/index.md. Link requirements from product-specs/index.md. The dependency stack decisions (native adapters, extras, evaluation) are in spec 042 and its selection evidence.

Code and named tests establish current implementation. Specs describe intent and history. When those disagree, record the discrepancy instead of silently assuming that the spec shipped. Update the relevant guide in the same change as its behavior.

docs.title: Mechanical enforcement
docs.text:
make harness-check validates the harness layout, local link targets, document discovery, entry-point size, Claude import, and generated schema inventory. It does not prove that prose matches runtime behavior.

Schema synchronization and Temporal import/sandbox tests enforce selected architecture constraints. See QUALITY_SCORE.md for their locations and remaining enforcement gaps.

docs.title: Frontend and interaction design
docs.text: HoloDeck has a Python Dash dashboard, a Click CLI, and HTTP protocol surfaces. There is no separate JavaScript application in the current architecture.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Start at dashboard/app.py. The views provide summary, explorer, and comparison pages. Data loading reads saved evaluation results. The dashboard does not execute an evaluation when it reads a result file.

Reuse design tokens and component styles. The design-system reference points to the same sources.

For interaction changes, exercise loading, empty results, error states, filters, and comparisons that the change affects. For visual changes, inspect the rendered page at relevant window sizes. Use committed fixtures or synthetic data without credentials. Record the observed result in the task or execution plan.

docs.title: CLI and protocols
docs.text: Use Click output in CLI commands and logging in library code. Keep actionable error messages near the invalid configuration or failed operation. Use typed AG-UI requests and events at the HTTP boundary. See the dashboard guide, server guide, and quality map.

docs.title: Execution plans
docs.text: Small, reversible changes need a brief task-local plan and verification result. For work across boundaries or multiple sessions, create a committed plan in docs/exec-plans/active/. Use YYYY-MM-DD-short-name.md as its filename.

docs.title: Plan contents
docs.text:
Include these sections:

  1. Objective and observable acceptance criteria.
  2. Scope, constraints, and links to the relevant code and product spec.
  3. Ordered steps with verification for each meaningful change.
  4. Progress and decisions, including why an approach changed.
  5. Validation results, blockers, and remaining work.

Keep the plan current as work proceeds. Preserve enough context for another agent to continue. When all acceptance criteria pass, move the plan to completed/ and update this index. Move deferred gaps into technical debt with an owner and exit criterion.

Earlier plans remain historical artifacts. Repository custom commands and their scaffolding have been removed. Maintain specifications, design documents, and execution plans directly in the directories above. Keep AGENTS.md as the knowledge map and CLAUDE.md as its single import.

docs.text: The migration ledger records one destination for each of the 316 original files. When a migrated file moves again, update its destination in the ledger and its index links. Source hashes record the migration baseline. They do not freeze future content edits.

docs.title: Product sense
docs.text: HoloDeck helps users define, test, compare, and deploy agents through YAML. The experiment must expose evidence: responses, tool use, evaluation results, cost, and latency.

docs.title: Product rules
docs.text:
• Keep the ordinary agent authoring path declarative.
  • Make configuration errors actionable before expensive runtime work starts.
  • Preserve evaluation flexibility across global, run, and metric model choices.
  • Support document-heavy, multimodal workflows and expected tool behavior.
  • Keep native Claude capabilities available alongside the OpenAI backend.
  • Let developers compose Temporal workflows in Python while agents remain YAML-defined.

The constitution records the governing principles. VISION.md provides product direction. It is not an implementation inventory. Product specs and source code establish feature scope and status.

docs.title: Evaluate a change
docs.text: Describe the user problem and observable result before choosing an implementation. Prefer a focused addition that fits the existing configuration and execution contracts. For a behavior change, supply a reproducible example and useful acceptance evidence. For dashboard changes, preserve the distinction between saved evidence and live execution.

docs.title: Verification policy
docs.text:
For a behavior change, run its regression tests and affected contracts with -n auto. For shared schema or protocol changes, broaden to their consumers. For Python changes, run focused formatting, lint, and type checks. Keep required commit and CI checks. See Contributing.

The constitution sets an 80% coverage target. Measure it with explicit coverage options. Do not infer coverage from test counts or from the presence of tests. Document environmental blockers and skipped live checks separately from failures.

docs.title: Maintenance loop
docs.text: When a check fails repeatedly, identify the missing contract, fixture, diagnostic, or instruction. Fix that cause with a focused change and a remediation message. Review this map when a module or its test strategy changes. Track unresolved gaps in technical debt.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text: Owner: runtime and deployment maintainers. Review this document when lifecycle or deployment behavior changes.

docs.title: Runtime contracts
docs.text:
Use the backend lifecycle from base.py. Preserve initialization, session preparation, cancellation, streaming, and teardown behavior. Use async clients or thread boundaries for blocking work. For timeout, retry, or session changes, exercise the affected lifecycle tests.

The server provides /health, /health/agent, AG-UI /awp, and REST endpoints. Health probes establish readiness. A representative request establishes useful agent behavior. Temporal retries must preserve the distinction between retryable model failures and configuration errors. See retry classification tests.

docs.title: Local reproduction and evidence
docs.text:
1. Select a committed fixture or a minimal agent configuration that reproduces the problem.
  2. Use separate result directories, ports, and container names for concurrent worktrees.
  3. Capture the command, configuration identity, response, and relevant redacted logs or traces.
  4. Exercise the failed behavior again after the change.
  5. Record the observed result and any unavailable external dependency in the execution plan.

Use the observability guide for configured OpenTelemetry exporters and GenAI signals. Do not assume a collector exists in every checkout. The repository does not provision the article's per-worktree observability stack automatically. That gap is tracked in technical debt.

It does not run profiles, live or providers None fast make verify-fast Harness, lock, Ruff, Black, MyPy, schema and image-constraints checks pass, and the full pytest suite passes None deps make verify-deps The lock is current. No unreviewed pip-audit advisory exists. npm audit of sample/copilotkit passes (skipped when that sample is absent) None (network to the advisory databases) smoke make verify-smoke Both backends complete real holodeck test run and holodeck serve AG-UI turns, including a tool call and thread isolation None profiles make verify-profiles The built wheel installs and works in a clean venv for each extras profile, and unselected packages are absent (details below) None (network to the package index) live make verify-live Every tool type each backend supports, a vector store case on every supported provider, plus serve AG-UI turns, against real providers; traces in a local Aspire dashboard CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (Claude), OPENAI_API_KEY (OpenAI, and embeddings for both); Docker for the vector stores and Aspire; optional PINECONE_API_KEY and AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT + AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY providers make verify-providers Only the vector store matrix of the live tier: the provider table below, with no AG-UI turns Same as live

deps. audit_deps.py audits every locked package (all extras and groups). Accepted advisories live in audit-ignores.toml. Each entry has id, package, reason, owner and expires. An id can be the advisory id or any alias. The audit fails on an unignored advisory, an expired entry, or an entry that matches no current advisory.

smoke. smoke.py starts fake_provider.py. That process implements the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages APIs on a local port. The script points the verify fixtures at it with a scrubbed environment and fake keys. For each backend, it runs holodeck test run, then 2 threads x 2 turns over POST /awp. It asserts RUN_STARTED first, RUN_FINISHED last, no RUN_ERROR, scripted text, and TOOL_CALL_* events on the tool turn. It also asserts that no request for thread B carries thread A's text. Artifacts, including the provider request log, go to .verify/smoke/<UTC timestamp>/. On Linux the Claude backend needs bubblewrap (bwrap): the Claude Code CLI will not start without it while HoloDeck's default subprocess env scrubbing is on. Smoke fails fast with an install hint when it is missing. CI runs this tier on Python 3.11. A weekly scheduled workflow runs verify-deps and verify-smoke.

profiles. profiles.py builds the wheel once, then for each profile creates a throwaway venv on Python 3.11 (the lowest supported; --python overrides it) and installs the wheel with that profile's extras. The versions come from uv.lock (uv export as constraints, plus the [tool.uv] overrides), so a run is reproducible and a new upstream release cannot fail it. Checks run inside the venv from an empty directory (profile_probe.py and holodeck processes), so the source tree cannot be imported by accident. Each profile asserts that the modules its extras provide import, and that every other feature package is absent by import and by installed distribution name. semantic-kernel, azure-ai-evaluation and evaluate are absent in every profile, all included, and uv pip check reports no broken requirements (the pytz override aside).

Profile Extras Feature checks base none --version, --help and every command's --help; holodeck init from the packaged templates; the config loader; an in-memory vectorstore tool round trip with placeholder embeddings; each missing store client names its extra; a DeepEval metric under holodeck test run, test optimize and test view each exit non-zero with the install command and no traceback eval-nlp eval, nlp DeepEval evaluators and judge models construct (no model call); BLEU and ROUGE score offline; METEOR scores or names the NLTK download command; the executor builds every metric optimizer, opensearch the extra An Optuna study suggests a value; the OpenSearch index builds against an unreachable host openai-agents, dashboard, temporal, deploy openai-agents, dashboard, temporal, deploy-all Both backends import; the dashboard app and assets, and test view --help; holodeck worker --help and the Temporal modules; the deploy modules and deploy --help one per store qdrant, chromadb, postgres, pinecone, weaviate, azure-ai-search, azure-cosmos create_adapter builds the store's adapter and never raises MissingClientError; Qdrant (:memory:) and Chroma (a temp directory) also run a real upsert and vector search; every other store client stays absent all all Every module in the wheel imports, with every extra present

--profile NAME (repeatable) and --group base|features|stores|all choose profiles; --keep leaves the venvs for debugging. Run it after any change to pyproject.toml, uv.lock, the extras or a lazy import. It downloads and unpacks hundreds of packages per profile, so it is not in make verify. CI runs it as the profiles job of profiles.yml: four matrix groups on GitHub-hosted runners (so it never queues behind the self-hosted test lane) with Python 3.11 and the uv cache. It runs on pull requests that change pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .gitignore, src/ or the verifier, and on every push to main. A new extra needs a row in EXTRA_MODULES; tests/unit/test_verify_profiles.py fails without one.

live. live.py runs the live validation loop without the CopilotKit browser step. It runs each backend whose credential is set. Put credentials in .verify/live.env (gitignored; copy live.env.example). Shell variables win. Claude uses live-full-claude.yaml and OpenAI uses live-full-openai.yaml.

Tool type Claude OpenAI function (smoke_echo, leak_probe) yes yes mcp stdio (local FastMCP server, started with uvx) yes yes vectorstore on every provider in the table below, hierarchical_document on Qdrant, PostgreSQL and Weaviate needs OPENAI_API_KEY yes subagents (claude.agents / openai.agents handoff) yes yes skill no: the Claude backend does not adapt skills yet yes prompt no: no runtime adapter on any backend no

Each tool type has one multi-turn test case with expected_tools and a type: code grader that checks the tool result or reply for a fixed marker. No case uses an LLM judge. The script reports PASS, FAIL or SKIP for each test case from the results JSON under the run copy's results/. Without OPENAI_API_KEY (embeddings), it removes every vector tool from the run copy. Without a provider's container or credentials, it removes that provider's tools. Each removed tool's cases are reported as SKIP with the reason, never PASS. The other cases still run. Then it starts holodeck serve and sends 2 threads x 2 turns. Thread A turn 2 must emit TOOL_CALL_START for smoke_echo. Thread B turn 2 must contain B's code word and not A's. It also fails when a credential value occurs in any file of the run directory. Each run uses an empty HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so ~/.holodeck/.env and a stored Claude login cannot replace the credential under test.

Vector store providers. Each has one vectorstore tool and case per backend, with its own small corpus under rag/ and a marker string the answer must contain. hierarchical_document runs on three providers over the same handbook corpus, each with its own tool name and collection.

Provider Infrastructure What the case proves qdrant container holodeck-verify-qdrant Document chunks through the native adapter; hierarchical_document with Qdrant vector search plus the in-process BM25 leg chromadb container holodeck-verify-chroma (HTTP client) Document chunks through the server client postgres container holodeck-verify-postgres (pgvector) Document chunks in a pgvector table; hierarchical_document through the BM25 fallback, since the adapter has no hybrid search weaviate container holodeck-verify-weaviate (HTTP 8089, gRPC 50059) Document chunks through the native adapter; hierarchical_document through Weaviate's native hybrid search azure-cosmos-nosql container holodeck-verify-cosmos, the Linux emulator (HTTP, published key). It accepts only the diskANN vector index and has no full-text search, so the tool sets vector_index: diskANN Document chunks in a Cosmos container with a vector policy pinecone Credential-gated: PINECONE_API_KEY (serverless index, aws / us-east-1). No local emulator: Pinecone Local is end-of-life and rejects the v10 control plane Document chunks in a hosted serverless index azure-ai-search Credential-gated: AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT and AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY. Azure has no emulator Document chunks in a hosted search index

The agent YAML is static, so the hosted providers' tools stay in the fixtures. The script drops a provider's tools and cases when its prerequisite is missing, and the SKIP row names the missing variable or the unavailable container. A tool falls back to in-memory storage when its provider cannot be reached (a missing client library or a retired provider name is an error, not a fallback), and a case could then still pass. So each tool gets a collection name unique to the run (verify_<backend><id>_<tool>). After the cases and the AG-UI turns, the script creates the provider's adapter, asks for that collection, and reports provider <name> (<tool>) holds records. The row is FAIL when the collection is missing or empty. Then it deletes every run collection, so a hosted service keeps no data. A failed delete is a FAIL row named cleanup. Pinecone reads can lag a write, so the count is polled for up to 30 seconds.

Docker containers (left running after the run; --no-infra skips them, and local vector store and trace checks then SKIP; hosted providers still run when their credentials are set):

Container Image Host ports holodeck-verify-qdrant qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.1 6333 holodeck-verify-chroma chromadb/chroma:1.5.9 (matches the locked client) 8765 holodeck-verify-postgres pgvector/pgvector:pg17 (throwaway credentials, loopback only) 54329 holodeck-verify-weaviate cr.weaviate.io/semitechnologies/weaviate:1.40.4 (anonymous, no vectorizer) 8089 HTTP, 50059 gRPC holodeck-verify-cosmos mcr.microsoft.com/cosmosdb/linux/azure-cosmos-emulator:vnext-preview (--protocol http; first start takes about a minute) 8081 gateway, 1234 data explorer holodeck-verify-aspire mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire-dashboard:13.5.2 (anonymous) 18888 UI, 4317 OTLP/gRPC, 4318 OTLP/HTTP

If another service of the same kind already serves those ports, the script reuses it and does not stop it. Stop the managed containers with docker rm -f holodeck-verify-qdrant holodeck-verify-chroma holodeck-verify-postgres holodeck-verify-weaviate holodeck-verify-cosmos holodeck-verify-aspire. The run reads its spans back from the Aspire dashboard and fails when a backend's leak_probe span is missing or shows the fake token (collector spans redacted row). The traces are also open for review at http://127.0.0.1:18888/traces. Look for the services holodeck-verify-live-claude and holodeck-verify-live-openai. The leak_probe tool returns a fake ghp_ token. Its span must show [REDACTED:github-token], never the token.

Pass flags through LIVE_ARGS, for example make verify-live LIVE_ARGS="--backend claude --no-infra". --limit N runs only the first N test cases. --only providers (or make verify-providers) runs only the vector store cases: it keeps the test cases for vector tools and skips the AG-UI turns. Cost: each backend makes about 20 small model calls (claude-haiku-5-5, gpt-6-luna) plus a few embedding calls; hosted providers add a serverless index or search index that the run creates and deletes. Artifacts (SSE transcripts, logs, the run copy of the agent) go to .verify/live/<UTC timestamp>/. Exit code 2 means every backend was skipped. Report that as skipped, not passed. A backend with its credential set and no passing case or turn fails.

docs.title: End-to-end deployment validation
docs.text:
Run this loop only when the user explicitly requests deployment validation or authorizes the target deployment. This loop publishes images and changes a live service. Reuse authorization already supplied in the conversation. The deployment guide describes supported configuration and CLI options.

The former local sample, sample/financial-assistant/claude, is git-ignored and may not exist in another checkout. Use the user-selected agent, registry, and target. Do not assume a personal cloud endpoint.

  1. Build the working-tree wheel with uv build --wheel. Keep exactly the intended wheel in the Docker build context.
  2. Build docker/Dockerfile.local with that wheel, using --no-cache and the target platform. Give the image a name that is not a published tag, for example holodeck-base-local:test.
  3. Inspect the installed wheel version inside the image.
  4. Build the agent image with holodeck deploy build --wheel dist/<wheel> --base-image <local base> --no-pull. Without --no-pull, builder.py passes pull=True to Docker.
  5. Publish the verified tag to the authorized registry.
  6. Deploy with holodeck deploy run for the selected agent configuration.
  7. Wait for health with a bounded timeout, then send a deterministic request with a known expected answer.
  8. Record the image digest, target, response, and relevant telemetry. Keep the build manifest (.holodeck/builds/<tag>.json).

By default the build pulls the base image, which can replace a locally tagged base image with its published registry version. Use --no-pull only for a base image you built locally. Azure Container Apps requires a compatible target image, commonly linux/amd64 for this repository's deployment loop. Readiness and cold-start timings vary. Measure them instead of relying on the old sample's timings. Local image builds (steps 1 to 4) need no registry access and are safe to run. Pushing images and holodeck deploy run need the authorization described above.

docs.title: Image pins and manifest
docs.text: Every image installs holodeck-ai[extras]==X.Y.Z with --constraint and --override files shipped in the wheel (src/holodeck/deploy/constraints.txt and overrides.txt, generated from uv.lock). Regenerate them with make constraints; make constraints-check fails when they are stale and runs in make verify-fast. A build that uses --wheel takes the files from that wheel. The Python base image is pinned by digest; update the digest on purpose. holodeck deploy build writes .holodeck/builds/<tag>.json (HoloDeck version, extras, base image reference and digest or image ID, built image ID, package list), and every image keeps its package list in /opt/holodeck/manifest.txt. Serving images carry only the extras the agent needs; they never carry eval, nlp or optimizer. See the deployment guide.

docs.title: Security boundaries
docs.text: Owner: maintainers of configuration, runtime adapters, serving, and deployment. This document records implementation boundaries and verification routes. Read the existing prompt-injection defenses, container hardening, and Azure Container Apps limitations for detailed controls and gaps.

docs.title: Credentials and external data
docs.text:
Environment precedence is shell variables, project .env, then ~/.holodeck/.env. Use the environment loader and typed configuration. Keep credentials out of commits, diagnostics, test artifacts, and examples.

Treat model output, MCP responses, document content, and external URLs as untrusted data. Validate data shapes at the boundary. Do not treat retrieved content as repository instructions. Use narrow typed adapters for SDK data.

Review eval-run redaction and telemetry redaction when changing stored or exported data. For path handling, preserve confinement checks in edge.py and relevant configuration/file-processing boundaries.

docs.title: Runtime and deployment
docs.text:
MCP servers and provider subprocesses execute with their configured permissions and environment. Keep subprocess commands and credential forwarding explicit. Use MCP for external API tools under the constitution's documented exception policy.

Do not assume the HTTP server provides production authentication, TLS termination, or tenant isolation. Inspect the target configuration and serve guide before exposing a service. For deployment validation, use the authorization and evidence procedure in Reliability.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
make security runs pip-audit, Ruff security rules, Bandit, and detect-secrets. security/audit-ignores.toml records accepted vulnerability exceptions with a reason, owner and expiry date; make verify-deps fails when one expires or goes stale. Do not add broad ignores to make a new failure disappear. For an accepted exception, record the affected path, reason, owner, and removal condition.

The pre-commit configuration defines enabled hooks. Security scans also run explicitly in CI. Record unresolved findings in technical debt without including secrets.

docs.title: Contributing to HoloDeck
docs.text: Start at AGENTS.md for repository instructions and the knowledge map. Read architecture before changing a module boundary.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
The package targets Python 3.11+. CI tests Python 3.11 and 3.13; make init uses Python 3.11. Use UV to manage the environment and uv.lock to reproduce dependencies.

git clone https://github.com/justinbarias/holodeck.git
cd holodeck
uv sync --all-extras
make install-hooks
uv run holodeck --version

uv run selects the project environment without shell activation. make init also creates the environment, but requires a discoverable Python 3.11 executable. Use pyproject.toml for supported extras and dependency constraints. Use uv add, uv add --dev, or uv remove for requested dependency changes.

Environment priority is shell variables, project .env, then ~/.holodeck/.env. Keep secrets out of version control and verification output. See Security.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
Run pytest with -n auto. Select the affected test area from Quality score.

uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/backends/test_selector.py -n auto -q
make test-unit-parallel
make test-integration-parallel
make test-parallel
uv run pytest -n auto --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80

The plain make test, make test-unit, and make test-integration targets currently run serially. The constitution sets an 80% coverage target. A focused test run does not establish repository-wide coverage. Integration and slow tests can require external services or credentials. Inspect their fixtures first. Use mocks for unit tests and committed fixtures for reproducible examples.

For bug fixes, first reproduce the failure with a test or an existing deterministic check. For behavior changes, cover meaningful edge cases and changed contracts. For documentation or formatting, use relevant checks without adding implementation-mirroring tests.

docs.title: Verify suite
docs.text: Before a PR, run make verify (static gates, the full test suite, dependency audit, and an offline smoke of both backends). Run make verify-live when backends or serve change and you have credentials. Reliability describes each tier, its proof, and the credentials it needs.

docs.title: Code style guide
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11-compatible syntax, Black at 88 columns, Ruff, and MyPy. pyproject.toml defines exact rules. Use Google-style docstrings for public modules, classes, and functions.

  • Annotate functions and domain values with concrete types.
  • Use protocols, discriminated unions, or TypedDict for known structures.
  • Use RunAgentInput and BaseEvent for AG-UI request/event surfaces.
  • Use backend result and event types at runtime boundaries.
  • Convert untyped SDK values at the adapter boundary. Keep casts narrow.
  • Do not access known model fields through getattr or arbitrary dictionaries.
  • If dynamic SDK compatibility requires a helper, isolate it and document its typed return contract.
  • If no practical alternative exists, use a specific type: ignore code and explain the reason.
  • Use the error hierarchy and preserve exception context.
  • Catch specific exceptions. At process or protocol boundaries, convert failures to the documented error contract.
  • Use Click output for CLI messages and logging for library diagnostics.
  • Keep blocking I/O out of async execution. Use async clients or an appropriate thread boundary.
  • Use Pydantic factories or None sentinels for mutable defaults.
  • Justify new dependencies in the change description.

For touched Python files, run focused checks. Substitute the actual paths:

uv run black --target-version py311 --check scripts/check_harness.py tests/unit/test_harness.py
uv run ruff check scripts/check_harness.py tests/unit/test_harness.py
uv run mypy scripts/check_harness.py

make format mutates all source and test files. Prefer formatting touched files during scoped work. make format-check, make lint, and make type-check provide repository checks. make lint runs Ruff. make security separately runs pip-audit, Ruff security rules, Bandit, and detect-secrets. If a broad check fails for unrelated code or unavailable stubs, report that failure and the focused result.

docs.title: Documentation and schema checks
docs.text:
make harness-check
uv run mkdocs build
make schema
make schema-check

Run schema generation only for changes to the agent schema inputs. make harness-check also detects changes to the generated schema inventory. Use make harness-generate to refresh that inventory after schema changes.

The harness check covers mapped engineering documents and their local link targets. It does not crawl every historical spec, resolve Markdown heading anchors, or fetch external URLs. The docsite build can report separate historical link warnings. Record unresolved warnings as debt. Use uv run mkdocs serve for a local documentation preview.

docs.title: Pull request workflow
docs.text:
1. Define acceptance criteria and inspect the current working tree.
  2. For complex work, maintain an execution plan.
  3. Implement the scoped change and relevant regression coverage.
  4. Run focused checks and review the final diff for unintended edits.
  5. Update affected guides, schemas, design evidence, and spec status.
  6. Report the change, checks, and any unresolved limitations.

Before committing, complete the constitution's formatting, type, test, and security checks. Run configured pre-commit hooks. Do not bypass required hooks to hide a failure. CI runs hooks, parallel tests, and security scanning. make ci is a broad local workflow that also cleans caches and installs dependencies. It is not a required command after every small edit.

Use focused conventional commits, such as fix(config): reject invalid provider. Do not add Claude Code attribution or generated-by trailers. Stage only the intended files. Preserve unrelated user changes.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
make install-hooks
uv run pre-commit run --all-files

The hook configuration is the source of truth for enabled checks. Security scanning also runs through make security in CI.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: For dependency errors, compare the installed environment with uv.lock before changing dependencies. For test failures, reproduce the smallest failing case with -n auto and inspect its fixtures. For runtime failures, use Reliability and capture redacted evidence. For architecture or test gaps, update technical debt.

docs.title: Backend Abstraction Layer
docs.text: The backend abstraction layer provides a provider-agnostic interface for agent execution. Downstream consumers (test runner, chat session, serve endpoint) depend only on the protocols defined in holodeck.lib.backends.base -- no provider-specific types leak through.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
BackendSelector inspects model.provider and instantiates the correct backend automatically:

Provider Backend openai, azure_openai OpenAIAgentsBackend anthropic, ollama ClaudeBackend

docs.title: holodeck.lib.backends.base -- Core Protocols & Data Classes
docs.text: Defines the provider-agnostic contracts that every backend must satisfy and the unified result types returned to callers.

docs.title: ExecutionResult
docs.text: The unified result type returned by every backend. Fields: response, tool_calls, tool_results, token_usage, structured_output, num_turns, is_error, error_reason, and thinking (extended-thinking text, empty when disabled or unsupported by the active backend).

docs.title: ExecutionResult(response, tool_calls=list(), tool_results=list(), token_usage=TokenUsage.zero(), structured_output=None, num_turns=1, is_error=False, error_reason=None, thinking='') dataclass
docs.text:
Provider-agnostic result of a single agent turn.

Attributes:

Name Type Description response str

The text response from the agent.

tool_calls list[dict[str, Any]]

List of tool call records made during execution.

tool_results list[dict[str, Any]]

List of tool result records returned during execution.

token_usage TokenUsage

Token consumption metadata for this turn.

structured_output Any | None

Optional structured output from the agent.

num_turns int

Number of turns taken to produce this result.

is_error bool

Whether the execution ended in an error state.

error_reason str | None

Human-readable reason for the error, if any.

thinking str

Extended-thinking text emitted by the model, concatenated in arrival order. Empty when extended thinking is disabled or unsupported by the backend.

docs.title: ToolEvent(kind, tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input=None, tool_response=None, error=None, parent_tool_use_id=None, text=None) dataclass
docs.text:
Real-time tool execution event from the backend.

Emitted by backends that support hook-based tool observation (e.g. Claude Agent SDK). Events are pushed onto an asyncio.Queue that consumers can drain concurrently during agent execution.

Attributes:

Name Type Description kind Literal['start', 'end', 'error', 'subagent_message', 'parent_link', 'thinking']

Event type — "start" before execution, "end" after success, "error" after failure, "subagent_message" for an assistant text snapshot streamed by an in-flight subagent (Task tool), "parent_link" to declare that a tool invocation was spawned by a subagent (so the panel can annotate it), "thinking" for an extended-thinking block streamed mid-turn (one event per ThinkingBlock, ahead of any tool call the block precedes).

tool_name str

Name of the tool being invoked. Empty for "thinking" (no tool involved).

tool_use_id str

Unique identifier correlating start/end/error for the same invocation. For "subagent_message" events this is the parent Task's tool_use_id so consumers can attach the snapshot to the corresponding active entry. For "parent_link" this is the child tool's id. For "thinking" this is a per-block id callers can thread through any downstream protocol (e.g. AG-UI REASONING_* message_id).

tool_input dict[str, Any] | None

Tool input parameters (present on "start").

tool_response str | None

Tool output (present on "end").

error str | None

Error description (present on "error").

parent_tool_use_id str | None

For nested events, the parent Task's tool_use_id. Present on "subagent_message" and "parent_link".

text str | None

Latest assistant text snapshot from a subagent (present on "subagent_message"), or the thinking-block text (present on "thinking").

docs.title: AgentSession
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Stateful multi-turn conversation session.

Implementations maintain conversation history across multiple send calls. Callers must invoke close when the session is no longer needed to release any held resources (connections, subprocesses, etc.).

docs.title: close() async
docs.text:
Release session resources (connections, subprocesses, etc.).

Source code in src/holodeck/lib/backends/base.py 
async def close(self) -> None:
    """Release session resources (connections, subprocesses, etc.)."""
    ...

docs.title: prepare() async
docs.text:
Connect or otherwise ready the session before the first send.

Called by callers that need the session's underlying transport opened in a specific async task context (e.g. _TaskBoundSession requires the SDK's connect() to run in the actor task so the anyio task group binds correctly).

Default behavior is a no-op. Implementations that have lazy connect semantics — like ClaudeSession — should override this to perform the connect explicitly. Implementations that connect at construction time can leave this as a no-op.

Source code in src/holodeck/lib/backends/base.py 
async def prepare(self) -> None:
    """Connect or otherwise ready the session before the first ``send``.

    Called by callers that need the session's underlying transport
    opened in a specific async task context (e.g.
    ``_TaskBoundSession`` requires the SDK's ``connect()`` to run in
    the actor task so the anyio task group binds correctly).

    Default behavior is a no-op. Implementations that have lazy
    connect semantics — like ``ClaudeSession`` — should override
    this to perform the connect explicitly. Implementations that
    connect at construction time can leave this as a no-op.
    """
    return None

docs.title: AgentBackend
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Provider backend factory.

Each backend encapsulates provider-specific initialisation logic and exposes a uniform surface for single-turn invocations (invoke_once) and stateful sessions (create_session). Callers must call initialize before any other method and teardown when done.

docs.title: create_session(*, eager_connect=True) async
docs.text:
Create a new stateful multi-turn session.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default eager_connect bool

When True (default), the backend may open its underlying transport before returning. When False, the backend must return a session whose transport is opened lazily — typically by AgentSession.prepare() invoked from a specific async task. Used by callers that need connection lifecycle bound to a different task than the one calling create_session (e.g. _TaskBoundSession actor). Backends without lazy connect semantics may accept and ignore this argument.

True

Returns:

Type Description AgentSession

A fresh AgentSession instance bound to this backend.

Raises:

Type Description BackendInitError

If the backend was not initialised before calling.

BackendSessionError

If the session cannot be created.

Source code in src/holodeck/lib/backends/base.py 
async def create_session(self, *, eager_connect: bool = True) -> AgentSession:
    """Create a new stateful multi-turn session.

    Args:
        eager_connect: When True (default), the backend may open its
            underlying transport before returning. When False, the
            backend must return a session whose transport is opened
            lazily — typically by ``AgentSession.prepare()`` invoked
            from a specific async task. Used by callers that need
            connection lifecycle bound to a different task than the
            one calling ``create_session`` (e.g.
            ``_TaskBoundSession`` actor). Backends without lazy
            connect semantics may accept and ignore this argument.

    Returns:

@staticmethod
async def select(
    agent: Agent,
    tool_instances: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    mode: str = "test",
) -> AgentBackend:
    """Select and initialize the appropriate backend for the given agent.

    Args:
        agent: Agent configuration with model provider information.
        tool_instances: Initialized tool instances for Claude backend.
        mode: Execution mode (``"test"`` or ``"chat"``).

    Returns:
        An initialized AgentBackend instance ready for use.

    Raises:
        BackendInitError: If the provider is not supported or initialization fails.
    """
    provider = agent.model.provider

    if provider in (ProviderEnum.OPENAI, ProviderEnum.AZURE_OPENAI):
        # Lazy import keeps the optional openai-agents SDK off the import
        # path for non-OpenAI providers (SC-005).
        from holodeck.lib.backends.openai_agents_backend import OpenAIAgentsBackend

        openai_backend = OpenAIAgentsBackend(agent=agent)
        await openai_backend.initialize()
        return openai_backend

    if provider in (ProviderEnum.ANTHROPIC, ProviderEnum.OLLAMA):
        claude_backend = ClaudeBackend(
            agent=agent,
            tool_instances=tool_instances,
            mode=mode,
        )
        await claude_backend.initialize()
        return claude_backend

    raise BackendInitError(f"Unsupported provider: {provider}")
