docs.title: DMN ↔ HoloDeck YAML Mapping
docs.text:
ARCHIVED (2026-08-29). Part of the archived 036 spec — see the banner in spec.md and the successor docs/product-specs/040-holodeck-temporal/spec.md.

Companion artifact to spec.md / refinements.md / tasks/plan.md. Status: design input for T2 (workflow models) and T3 (table model) — illustrative, not normative until those tasks land. Produced 2026-06-10 from a design discussion on how the native YAML DSL relates to the OMG DMN standard.

Note (2026-07-25): the worked examples below still use the original loan-hardship scenario. They are retained as DMN-mapping illustrations only — the anchor sample has since moved to the Targeted Compliance Framework (spec.md US6). The element-by-element mappings, the DRD semantics, and the source:/input_data rows are all current; only the domain in the examples is stale. The date(..) expression on line ~51 has been corrected in place.

docs.title: The honest claim
docs.text:
The v1 artifacts carry DMN semantics, not the DMN interchange format:

  • Standard-faithful: FEEL expression syntax (refinements §5: FEEL syntax is the contract), hit-policy semantics (UNIQUE/FIRST/PRIORITY), decision-table structure (input expressions, unary-test cells, output values), DRD composition (decisions requiring decisions and input data, acyclic by validation).
  • Not the standard artifact: no DMN 1.x XML import/export, no DMNDI (diagram geometry), no boxed expressions. Spec Out of Scope, by design.
  • Pitch wording: "DMN-semantics policy-as-code" — not "DMN-compatible" and not "bring your existing DMN files" (those need the deferred XML importer; see Migration path).

docs.title: Division of labor
docs.text: File DMN concept it carries workflow.yaml The DRD (logical form): decisions, input data, information requirements tables/*.dmn.yaml One decision table each (<decision> + <decisionTable>) schemas/*.json (gates) <itemDefinition> — the type of each input-data fact

docs.title: Decision table mapping (tables/*.dmn.yaml)
docs.text:
Example — the Level-2 affordability table:

# DMN: <decision> + <decisionTable>
id: affordability
name: Hardship affordability assessment
version: "2026-06-01.1"          # FR-013: required label, snapshotted into the run record
hit_policy: UNIQUE               # DMN: hitPolicy — exactly one rule may match

# DMN: <input>/<inputExpression> — full FEEL expressions live HERE only.
# `income` / `residency` are workflow node ids; dot-paths reach into the
# gated object (edge node) or verdict (policy node).
inputs:
  - name: surplus_ratio
    expression: (income.net_monthly_income - income.monthly_expenses) / income.net_monthly_income
    type: number
  # CORRECTED 2026-07-25 — was `date(application_date) - date(income.statement_date)`,
  # which research.md caveat 6 proved unevaluable: bkflow-feel's `date_func`
  # production accepts only a quoted literal, not a variable. Date-typed gate
  # fields cross the boundary as Python `datetime.date` and subtract bare;
  # caveat 1 requires the wrapper to convert the resulting timedelta to days.
  - name: statement_age
    expression: application_date - income.statement_date
    type: days
  - name: residency_status
    expression: residency.status
    type: string

# DMN: <output>; `values` = outputValues (and the priority order under PRIORITY)
outputs:
  - name: affordability
    type: string
    values: [affordable, marginal, unaffordable]

# DMN: <rule> — each `when` cell is a FEEL unary test, keyed by input name.
# An input omitted from `when` is the irrelevant cell (always matches), which
# is DMN's "-"; an explicit "-" is accepted and means the same thing.
# CORRECTED 2026-07-25 — this example was positional (`when: [">= 0.25", ...]`)
# until T3 landed. Open design point 1 below resolved to keyed cells, so the
# positional form no longer parses. See `models/decision_table.py::Rule`.
rules:
  - when: { surplus_ratio: ">= 0.25", statement_age: "<= 90", residency_status: '"verified"' }
    then: { affordability: affordable }
    annotation: Comfortable surplus, fresh statements, verified residency
  - when: { surplus_ratio: "[0.10..0.25)", statement_age: "<= 90", residency_status: '"verified"' }
    then: { affordability: marginal }
    annotation: Thin surplus — refer for officer review
  - when: { surplus_ratio: "< 0.10" }
    then: { affordability: unaffordable }
    annotation: No realistic repayment capacity
  - when: { statement_age: "> 90" }
    then: { affordability: unaffordable }
    annotation: Statements too stale to assess

# DMN: defaultOutputEntry — without it, no-match fails loudly (FR-012)
# default: { affordability: unaffordable }

Element-by-element:

*.dmn.yaml DMN element Notes id, name <decision id name> version (no direct DMN equivalent) HoloDeck addition; FR-013 snapshot key hit_policy hitPolicy UNIQUE multi-match errors per FR-012; PRIORITY resolves by values order (DMN's output-values-as-priority rule) inputs[].expression <inputExpression> (FEEL) Full FEEL allowed here only inputs[].type typeRef rules[].when[<input name>] <inputEntry> (FEEL unary test) >= 0.25, [0.10..0.25), "verified"; an omitted key (or -) is the irrelevant cell rules[].then <outputEntry> rules[].annotation rule annotation outputs[].values outputValues Doubles as PRIORITY ordering, highest first default defaultOutputEntry Optional; absence ⇒ loud no-match failure

docs.title: Open design points for T3
docs.text:
1. ~~Positional vs keyed when cells.~~ RESOLVED in T3 — keyed only. Positional mirrors DMN's column layout, but keyed cells are diff-friendlier and immune to column-reorder bugs, and a reordered column silently changing every rule's meaning is exactly the class of error this spec exists to prevent. Rule.when is a dict[str, str] keyed by input name; a cell naming an undeclared input is rejected at load. Positional entries do not parse. A future transpiler (spec 039) emits keyed cells.
  2. Expression placement rule. Full FEEL (arithmetic, date math) is valid only in inputs[].expression; rule cells are restricted to unary tests. Faithful to DMN and matches what the FEEL-library research verified best (bkflow-feel). Encode as a T3 validation rule.

docs.title: DRD mapping (workflow.yaml)
docs.text:
The workflow file is the DRD in logical form:

name: loan-hardship-underwriting
version: "2026-06-01.1"

nodes:
  # DMN <inputData> — produced by an agent; the gate schema is the
  # <itemDefinition> (the type of the fact).
  - id: income
    edge: { agent: agents/income-extractor/agent.yaml }
    gate: { schema: schemas/income.json }
  - id: residency
    edge: { agent: agents/residency-verifier/agent.yaml }
    gate: { schema: schemas/residency.json }
  - id: doc_fraud_flag
    edge: { agent: agents/doc-fraud-detector/agent.yaml }
    gate: { schema: schemas/fraud-flag.json }

  # DMN <decision> — `inputs:` is the <informationRequirement> list.
  # CORRECTED 2026-07-25 — `hit_policy:` was shown on each node until the T3
  # refactor moved it onto the referenced table, where DMN puts it (one table,
  # one hit policy, one source of truth). `PolicyNode` has no such field and
  # forbids extras, so the earlier form no longer parses.
  - id: affordability
    decision: tables/affordability.dmn.yaml   # the table declares UNIQUE
    inputs: [income, residency]          # requiredInput ×2
  - id: risk_tier
    decision: tables/risk.dmn.yaml            # the table declares FIRST
    inputs: [doc_fraud_flag, income]

  - id: final_determination
    decision: tables/determination.dmn.yaml   # the table declares PRIORITY
    inputs: [affordability, risk_tier]   # requiredDecision ×2
    requires_human: true
    decided_by: "Hardship Officer"
    draft: { agent: agents/reasons-drafter/agent.yaml }
    ai_may_draft: [reasons]
DMN DRD element HoloDeck equivalent <decision> policy or human node (one table each) <inputData> edge node's gated output <itemDefinition> the gate's JSON Schema <informationRequirement> (requiredInput / requiredDecision) the inputs: list (kind implicit — resolved by what the id names) Acyclic requirements graph (DMN mandate) FR-003 load-time cycle rejection — same constraint <inputData> not agent-produced the workflow-level input_data: block (facts of record — prior state, case facts). Distinct from an edge node's gated output, which is agent-produced. <knowledgeSource> not modeled — see proposal below <businessKnowledgeModel> (reusable invocable logic) not modeled — every table is bound to exactly one node DMNDI (diagram layout) not modeled — logical DRD only; visual modeler is North Star

docs.title: Behavioral deltas from standard DRD
docs.text:
• DMN allows any decision as an evaluation entry point; v1 always evaluates the full DAG to the top. Evaluating one table in isolation is the policy test executor's job (T12).
  • One workflow.yaml holds exactly one DRD; a DMN definitions file may hold several sharing elements.

docs.title: Proposal: source: annotation (knowledgeSource-lite)
docs.text:
<knowledgeSource> is DMN's record of the authority for a decision — "this table implements §72 of the Hardship Policy." For the regulated audience that traceability link is substance, not decoration, and it costs one optional field:

# on a node or table
source: "Hardship Policy v4.2 §72"
  • Non-executable annotation; flows into the run record and OTel span attributes.
  • Recommended for T2/T3 model fields (one-line schema addition now vs. a migration later). A future "draft table from policy document" feature would populate it automatically.

docs.title: Authoring routes (where tables come from)
docs.text:
1. Hand-authored YAML — the only route in v1; guarded by the published JSON schema (T2), load-time FEEL validation with table/rule/cell locators (T3), and policy tests (T12).
  2. Imported from DMN XML — deferred but architecturally preserved: a transpiler walks <decisionTable> and emits exactly the shape above (decision tables only; no DRD-XML, BKM, or boxed expressions). Likely small once T3's model exists, if "bring your existing DMN" becomes a sales requirement.
  3. AI-drafted from a policy document — now specced: docs/product-specs/039-policy-generator (was "not in any spec yet"). Emits tables and the workflow.yaml DRD, with TODO markers where edge nodes go; edge agents stay hand-authored. On-pattern (AI drafts, human reviews/versions/commits — same move as ai_may_draft: reasons; the committed table stays deterministic), and US5 policy tests are exactly how a drafted table is verified.

036 ships only what makes a drafted table safe to run: the provenance block (T3a) and the review gate — holodeck workflow run refuses a table with generated_by and no reviewed_by (FR-030, SC-009). This extends "the LLM is never the spine" to authoring time: without it, a model could be the spine by writing the rules rather than by producing a verdict.

039 is built only after 036's MVP ships. Its golden corpus is pinned at docs/product-specs/039-policy-generator/corpus-manifest.md.

docs.title: Refinement Memo — Deterministic Spine (036)
docs.text:
ARCHIVED (2026-08-29). Part of the archived 036 spec — see the banner in spec.md and the successor docs/product-specs/040-holodeck-temporal/spec.md.

Date: 2026-06-10 · Produced by an idea-refine interview run against spec.md (Draft for review). The spec is not edited by this memo; fold these resolutions in manually (suggested deltas below are precise enough to apply verbatim).

docs.title: Why these six questions
docs.text:
The spec was already sharp, so the refine run skipped re-divergence and interviewed only where (a) the codebase contradicts a spec assumption, or (b) the spec text is genuinely ambiguous. Codebase grounding:

  • ExecutionResult.structured_output exists (src/holodeck/lib/backends/base.py), but only the Claude backend produces and validates it; the SK backend has no structured-output path at all.
  • TestExecutor (src/holodeck/lib/test_runner/executor.py) is hard-wired to agent invocation — there is no seam for asserting a pure function's verdict.
  • No confidence convention exists anywhere in the codebase.
  • workflow is a free CLI verb (resolves spec Open Question 4). No prior FEEL/DMN/SpiffWorkflow dependency — clean slate.
  • Artifact conventions favor .holodeck/ (deployments.json, optimizer output_dir/<run-id>/trials.jsonl) — supports .holodeck/runs/<id>.json for the run record (spec Open Question 2, suggestion only, decide in plan).

docs.title: 1. Edge backends — Claude-only for the POC
docs.text:
SK structured output is a hidden dependency the spec didn't price in. Decision: edge nodes still dispatch via BackendSelector (the protocol contract stands), but the POC validates the Claude backend only. SK structured-output support becomes a named follow-up, not an implicit prerequisite.

  • Delta — FR-006: append: "The POC validates the Claude backend only; SK-backend structured output is a tracked follow-up, not a POC requirement."
  • Delta — Open Question 3: resolved — binding is confirmed for Claude (Agent.response_format → structured_output, already schema-validated in claude_backend.py); SK is out of POC scope.

docs.title: 2. Human node — the table computes a recommendation
docs.text:
The spec left the human node's DMN table semantically dangling (a table with a hit policy that's never evaluated would be dead config). Decision: at a human node the table is evaluated over the composed inputs and produces a recommended verdict. The CLI presents: composed inputs → table recommendation (with matched rule) → AI-drafted reasons (advisory) → prompt. The human accepts or overrides; an override is recorded as an override (recommended vs. decided, both in the run record). The human's choice is the verdict, always.

  • Delta — FR-014: the CLI presents the composed inputs, the table's recommended verdict and matched rule, and (if declared) AI-drafted reasons, then prompts for the human selection.
  • Delta — FR-015: the run record stores both the table's recommendation and the human's decision; when they differ, the verdict is flagged as an override.
  • Delta — US3 acceptance scenarios: add: "Given the table recommends refer and the human selects decline, Then the verdict is decline and the record marks it as an override of the recommendation."
  • Replay note: replay re-evaluates the table (recomputing the recommendation from snapshots) and re-applies the recorded human decision — identical verdict guaranteed, override flag reproduced.

docs.title: 3. Policy tests — a new WorkflowTestExecutor, same shape
docs.text:
TestExecutor won't be refactored inside a POC. Decision: introduce a WorkflowTestExecutor that mirrors the existing executor's shape (TestCaseModel-like YAML cases, TestResult-like outputs, same AAA flow) but evaluates a decision table over given inputs instead of invoking an agent. No agent, no backend, no LLM.

  • Delta — FR-023: "…via a WorkflowTestExecutor that mirrors the existing test/eval framework's case and result shapes" (replaces "via the existing HoloDeck test/eval framework", which implied reusing TestExecutor as-is).
  • Convergence of the two executors is North Star, not POC.

docs.title: 4. Confidence gating — cut from the POC
docs.text:
No convention exists, and inventing one means trusting self-reported LLM confidence. Decision: gates validate schema only (types, required fields, enums, ranges). Confidence-threshold rejection/routing moves to Out of Scope.

  • Delta — Edge Cases: delete the "Low-confidence edge output" bullet.
  • Delta — Out of Scope: add "Confidence-scored gate fields / low-confidence routing (no convention exists; self-reported confidence is unreliable). North Star."
  • Delta — Open Question 3: drop the "low-confidence-field convention" clause.

docs.title: 5. FEEL — the syntax is the contract; the subset may shrink
docs.text:
Decision: decision-table cells must be valid FEEL syntax. If the spike finds no Python evaluator covering the full FR-010 subset, the subset narrows further (e.g. drop date difference before dropping ranges) but stays FEEL-compatible so a fuller evaluator can swap in later. The sample bends to the subset, never the reverse. No pragmatic non-FEEL expression language fallback.

  • Delta — FR-010: keep the NEEDS CLARIFICATION (library choice is still the plan-phase spike) but add the fallback posture: "If no library covers the full subset, the subset narrows (remaining FEEL-syntax-compatible); non-FEEL expression syntaxes are not an acceptable fallback."
  • Delta — SC-005: caveat "…or the documented narrowed subset, with the sample adjusted accordingly."

docs.title: 6. Human identity — declared in workflow.yaml, confirmed at the prompt
docs.text:
Decision: the human node declares decided_by (a role or name) in workflow.yaml. At the prompt, the CLI displays the declared decided_by and asks the operator to confirm or enter their name; the confirmed name is recorded verbatim in the run record with a timestamp. This models accountability ahead of time while staying honest that a CLI POC makes no authentication claim.

  • Delta — FR-002: human node gains optional decided_by.
  • Delta — FR-015: "…attributed to the named human" becomes "…attributed to the decided_by identity declared in the workflow and confirmed (or entered) at the CLI prompt; no authentication is claimed in the POC."
  • Delta — Key Entities (RunRecord): add decided_by (declared + confirmed) alongside the human decision.

docs.title: Still open (unchanged, resolve during implementation planning)
docs.text:
1. Which FEEL evaluator to embed — the spike remains the gating risk (posture now fixed by Decision 5).
  2. Run record JSON shape; location suggestion: .holodeck/runs/<id>.json.

docs.title: Not doing (added by this refinement)
docs.text:
• SK-backend structured output (Decision 1) — follow-up feature.
  • Confidence gating in any form (Decision 4) — North Star.
  • Refactoring TestExecutor (Decision 3) — North Star convergence.
  • Any non-FEEL expression fallback (Decision 5) — the standards claim is the point.

docs.title: Research: FEEL Evaluator Spike (T1, Phase 0)
docs.text:
ARCHIVED as a spec, RETAINED as rationale (2026-08-29). 036 is archived (see spec.md), but the FEEL evaluator and decision-table caveats recorded here still govern the kept primitives in holodeck.lib.workflow and are cited from their docstrings.

Resolves the FR-010 NEEDS CLARIFICATION and refinements §5 ("FEEL syntax is the contract"). Produced 2026-06-11 from a hands-on spike on branch 036-deterministic-spine. Behavior pinned by tests/unit/workflow/test_feel_conformance.py (40 tests, all passing).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Embed bkflow-feel 1.2.0 (pinned). MIT-licensed, lark-grammar FEEL parser from TencentBlueKing. It covers the full FR-010 subset — no subset narrowing needed (the refinements §5 fallback posture goes unused). The core spike risk — FEEL date difference — is retired: date("2026-01-31") - date("2026-01-01") evaluates to timedelta(days=30).

docs.title: Candidates considered
docs.text:
Library Verdict Why bkflow-feel 1.2.0 chosen MIT; full FR-010 coverage verified; active org (TencentBlueKing); lark grammar pySFeel fallback, unused GPLv3 (viral — incompatible with embedding in an MIT-adjacent product without license review); dormant SpiffWorkflow (DMN module) ruled out No real FEEL parser — Python-expression translation; hit policies limited to UNIQUE/COLLECT

License note: bkflow-feel's PyPI metadata has an empty license field, but the repository carries an MIT LICENSE file and the project is published by TencentBlueKing under their standard MIT terms.

docs.title: FR-010 subset verdicts
docs.text:
All verified against bkflow-feel 1.2.0 (the spike initially probed 1.2.1rc2; behavior matched except where noted).

FR-010 feature Verdict Notes Numeric comparisons (< <= > >= = !=) ✅ pass including arithmetic operands: (a - b) / a >= 0.25 Ranges, all four brackets [a..b] [a..b) (a..b] (a..b) ✅ pass endpoint inclusion/exclusion exactly per FEEL and / or / not(..) ✅ pass String equality ✅ pass status = "verified" with context vars List membership x in [..] ✅ pass strings and numbers Date literals date("YYYY-MM-DD") ✅ pass Date comparison ✅ pass including date-in-date-range Date difference ✅ pass* returns datetime.timedelta — see caveat 1 Dot-path context access ✅ pass income.net_monthly_income into nested dicts — how composed node outputs flow into input expressions

docs.title: Caveats (design inputs for T3)
docs.text:
1. Date difference yields a timedelta, which is not number-comparable. (date(..) - date(..)) > 30 raises ValidationError ("Type of both operators must be same"). → The T3 FEEL wrapper must convert timedelta-valued input expressions to days (number) before rule cells compare them. This also matches the type: days column in dmn-yaml-mapping.md.
  2. No duration literals, and unknown functions fail silently. duration("P30D") has no builtin; in 1.2.0 an unknown function call returns None silently (the internal ValueError is caught and logged, not raised). → T3's static validation must reject non-allowlisted function names itself; runtime gives nothing to catch until the None poisons a comparison.
  3. The grammar accepts out-of-subset FEEL — static rejection needs its own allowlist. some x in [1, 2] satisfies x > 1 parses and evaluates fine; for .. return happens to be rejected at parse time. The parser is not a subset gate. → T3 must walk the lark parse tree (or token stream) and enforce an allowlist of node types.
  4. No unknown-variable error. A missing context variable resolves to None and fails later as a type mismatch (ValidationError, NoneType vs int) — there is no dedicated unknown-variable diagnostic. → T3's wrapper must verify required inputs are present before evaluation so failures carry the table/rule/cell locator (FR-012 loud failures). Partly resolved (T3), completed later: the first fix extracted the referenced root names from the parse tree and raised FeelEvaluationError(locator, ..) for any root absent from the context. That covered a typo'd root but not a missing attribute under a bound root, which ContextItem.evaluate also resolves to None — and because NotEqual has no operand validator (it is a bare Python !=), a != rule cell then matched unconditionally and the table emitted a real-looking verdict. feel.evaluate_expression now resolves every full dot-path against the bindings before evaluating, and rejects three distinct cases: an unbound root, an attribute absent from a bound mapping, and an attribute read through a value that is not a dict (which can never resolve). A leaf explicitly bound to None is still a bound fact, as before — presence, not truthiness, is the test.

One route could still defeat the guard: a fact named true, false or null parses as a FEEL literal, never as a variable, so the binding was invisible to both the expression and the check. Those three names are now rejected as fact names when a context is evaluated. That check is at evaluation time, not load time, because the workflow model — not the FEEL wrapper — owns node/fact names. 5. Error taxonomy for the wrapper: syntax errors surface as lark.exceptions.UnexpectedInput (parse time); type/value errors as bkflow_feel.exceptions.ValidationError (eval time). Both must be caught and re-raised through holodeck.lib.errors with locators. Resolved, and wider than stated: those are not the only two channels. bkflow_feel.api.parse_expression re-raises any other exception unchanged, and two are reachable from schema-valid data — a ZeroDivisionError from a ratio expression with a zero denominator, and a bare TypeError from range cells (In/RangeGroup bypass the operand validator and compare with raw Python). The wrapper therefore catches broadly and re-raises everything as FeelEvaluationError with the locator, preserving the cause.

  1. Numeric comparison is exact-typed and asymmetric. BinaryOperationValidator is isinstance(left, type(right)), so a float column value refuses an int cell literal and vice versa — a monetary column with cents against a whole-number threshold (<= 2000) loads fine and fails at runtime on the first fractional value. Ranges bypass the validator entirely, so [0..90] and <= 90 disagreed on the same input. → Unary tests are evaluated with both sides widened to float: the column value in feel.evaluate_unary_test, and every numeric literal via a FEELTransformer subclass. bool is deliberately not widened (it must still compare against true/false) and is rejected outright in number and days columns, where it would otherwise compare silently as 1/0. Full expressions keep stock literal typing — widening there would break arithmetic over int-typed facts for no gain.
  2. date(..) accepts only a quoted literal, not a variable. date(income. statement_date) does not parse — the date_func production wants a string literal (date("2026-01-01")), so the dmn-yaml-mapping.md example date(application_date) - date(income.statement_date) is unevaluable as written. → Date-typed inputs are supplied to the FEEL context as Python datetime.date objects and subtracted directly (application_date - income.statement_date), which yields a timedelta (caveat 1). The gate-schema format: date fields become date objects at the workflow boundary; the table's inputs[].expression does bare subtraction, never date(variable).

docs.title: Static-rejection list (input to T3)
docs.text:
Out-of-subset constructs T3 must reject at load time (grammar does NOT reject them all):

  • Quantified expressions: some/every .. satisfies (grammar accepts)
  • Any function invocation outside the allowlist — initially date(..) only (grammar accepts unknown functions and returns silent None)
  • for .. return (grammar rejects, but reject statically anyway for a uniform locator-bearing error)
  • if .. then .. else, context literals {..}, instance of, between — to be probed/enumerated as T3 builds the allowlist walker; the posture is allowlist, not blocklist, so anything unprobed is rejected by default.

docs.title: Dependency findings
docs.text:
bkflow-feel declares pytz<2024 (and lark>=1.1.7,<2, python-dateutil<3, pydantic<3). The pytz pin is overly conservative — pytz's API is stable — and a naive uv add downgraded repo-wide pytz 2025.2→2023.4 and dragged optuna 4.9.0→4.8.0.

Resolution (applied):

  • Pinned bkflow-feel==1.2.0 (stable; uv had selected pre-release 1.2.1rc2 because the repo allows prereleases for semantic-kernel).
  • Added [tool.uv] override-dependencies = ["pytz>=2024"] to neutralize the pin. Restored: pytz 2026.2, optuna 4.9.0.
  • Compatibility of bkflow-feel 1.2.0 with modern pytz is verified by the conformance suite (date functions exercise the tz-touching code paths).

Risk register: bkflow-feel's release cadence is slow and 1.2.1 has sat in rc since publication. The pin + conformance suite make upgrades deliberate: bump, run tests/unit/workflow/test_feel_conformance.py, read the diff. MIT license permits vendoring if the project goes dormant.

docs.title: Hit-policy evaluation: in-house (T4)
docs.text: bkflow-feel is an expression evaluator only — it has no decision-table or hit-policy layer (its sibling project bkflow-dmn does, but it brings a different table format and more dependency surface). UNIQUE/FIRST/PRIORITY over already-evaluated unary tests is ~50 lines of well-specified logic with SC-004 conformance tests planned in T4. Decision: implement hit policies in-house in T4; use bkflow-feel strictly for expressions and unary tests.

docs.title: Dependency stack selection evidence
docs.text:
Reviewed: 2026-11-10 at 00d1ed4 (second round). First round: 2026-09-06 at 3e59e1d. Owner: Retrieval and packaging maintainers. Product contract: Spec 042.

This record separates inspected implementation from upstream claims and from the proposed selection. Package facts come from the PyPI JSON API and released source archives on 2026-11-10. No candidate was installed, benchmarked or run against a live database for this round.

docs.title: Second-round result
docs.text:
The first round preferred LlamaIndex as the retrieval foundation. The second round does not support that choice. The evidence now favours HoloDeck-owned native adapters, with no retrieval framework. The maintainer accepted this on 2026-11-10 and the spec was revised the same day. See Recommendation and decision.

Three findings drive the change:

  1. LlamaIndex connectors do not provide the operations the spec requires (FR-013, FR-020). See operation coverage.
  2. Every framework lags the store clients. That is the same problem SK causes today. See pin lag.
  3. HoloDeck already owns native code for the stores it documents and tests. See the inventory provider table.

docs.title: Semantic Kernel status and urgency
docs.text:
• Latest release is semantic-kernel 1.47.0 (2026-11-05). It requires Python >=3.11.
  • From 1.44, mcp<2.0 is a core requirement. MCP is at 2.3.0. Both native agent SDKs HoloDeck uses allow mcp<3, so SK is the only package that holds MCP back. HoloDeck pins MCP for security fixes.
  • SK also caps pydantic<2.14, pymongo<4.17, chromadb<1.6 and pinecone~=7.0. Pinecone is at 10.3.0. SK's Pinecone connector fails to import with 8+ (verified locally in #431).
  • The SK repository names Microsoft Agent Framework as its successor. SK 1.x receives critical fixes. No end-of-support date is announced. Microsoft's stated minimum is one year after Agent Framework general availability (agent-framework-core 1.0.0, 2026-04-02), which gives about April 2027 by inference.
  • In HoloDeck's base install SK alone brings 26 packages that nothing else needs.

docs.title: Candidate frameworks
docs.text:
Dated PyPI metadata, 2026-11-10. Package presence is not proof of operation parity.

Candidate Version (date) Python Base weight Finding llama-index-core 0.14.25 (2026-09-21) >=3.10,<4.0 29 required packages, including nltk, sqlalchemy, llama-index-workflows, networkx, pillow No release in 7 weeks. No slim core. SentenceSplitter downloads NLTK data at run time. MIT. agent-framework-core 1.25.0 (2026-11-07) >=3.11 7 required packages New since round one. Has an SK-style vector-store API with precomputed vectors, paged reads without vectors and keyword-hybrid search. The API is marked experimental. It lives in the agent runtime package; no separate vector package exists. langchain-core + store packages current >=3.10 varies langchain-pinecone requires pinecone<8 and Python <3.14. langchain-postgres requires pgvector<0.4. Azure packages pull langgraph. Adds a second document contract. haystack-ai 3.4.1 (2026-10-21) >=3.11 19 required packages, including posthog Pipeline runtime and telemetry. No Cosmos or SQL Server store. Collections created outside Haystack generally need migration. pydantic-ai current >=3.11 n/a No vector-store abstraction.

Not credible for this purpose after review: txtai, cognee, mem0, lancedb, vecs, autogen-ext memory. Each is a store, an application framework, or too immature to be an abstraction over eleven stores.

docs.title: LlamaIndex connector versions
docs.text:
Package Version Change since 2026-09-06 Client requirement qdrant 0.10.4 New release; the Python <3.14 bound is gone qdrant-client>=1.16.0 postgres 0.9.0 None asyncpg, psycopg2-binary, pgvector, sqlalchemy<2.1 pinecone 0.9.0 None pinecone>=7,<10 chroma 0.6.0 None chromadb>=0.5.17 azureaisearch 0.6.0 None azure-search-documents<12 (12.0.0 is released) weaviate 1.7.1, faiss 0.7.0, azurecosmosmongo 0.9.0, azurecosmosnosql 1.6.0 unchanged None no conflict found SQL Server none Five likely package names return HTTP 404 n/a

Conflicts with HoloDeck's lock:

  • The Postgres connector requires sqlalchemy<2.1. HoloDeck locks sqlalchemy 2.1.8 through Optuna. This does not resolve.
  • The Postgres connector imports both asyncpg and psycopg2; HoloDeck uses psycopg 3. It creates its own data_<name> table with a fixed schema, so existing SK tables need migration.
  • The Pinecone connector allows 7–9, not 10.

docs.title: LlamaIndex operation coverage
docs.text:
Read from the released source archives, not from documentation. In llama-index-core 0.14.25 the base class's default async methods call the sync method on the event loop, and get_nodes/delete_nodes raise NotImplementedError unless a connector overrides them.

Connector Get by ID Delete by ID Real async Metadata filters Paged read without vectors qdrant Yes Yes Yes Yes No: scrolls with vectors, limit 9999, no cursor postgres Yes Yes Yes Yes No: selects the embedding, no limit chroma Yes Yes No: blocks the event loop Yes Partial: limit, no offset pinecone No: raises ValueError; filter-only through a zero-vector query Yes No Yes No weaviate No Yes Yes Yes No azureaisearch Yes Yes Yes Yes Not verified azurecosmosnosql No No No No: raw filter strings only; delete() formats the document ID into SQL No azurecosmosmongo No No No No No faiss No No (FaissVectorStore) No No: raises on filters No SimpleVectorStore No Yes No Yes No

No connector provides paged enumeration without vectors. HoloDeck needs it for incremental ingestion, source deletion and cold-start reload (FR-013, FR-016). Every store would still need native code inside the adapter. Qdrant hybrid in LlamaIndex is dense plus sparse and needs FastEmbed or a supplied sparse function; it is not HoloDeck's dense plus full-text path (FR-018).

docs.title: Microsoft Agent Framework connector status
docs.text:
Store Package status (2026-11-07 builds) Limit that matters qdrant Alpha No keyword-hybrid; HoloDeck already does this natively postgres Alpha; uses psycopg 3 and pgvector 0.5 No full-text or hybrid sql-server Alpha; mssql-python on an executor No keyword-hybrid azure-cosmos (NoSQL) Beta /id must be the only partition key azure-ai-search Beta Native hybrid available mongodb / azure-documentdb Alpha Mapping to azure-cosmos-mongo not verified in-memory In core, experimental n/a chroma, weaviate, pinecone 0.0.0a1 placeholders with no code Not usable faiss No package Not usable

Agent Framework is the natural successor to SK's vector API and matches HoloDeck's drivers. It is not ready: connectors are date-stamped alphas, and two of the five stores HoloDeck documents (chroma and pinecone) have no connector.

docs.title: Current storage capability evidence
docs.text:
Sources: collection factory (src/holodeck/lib/vector_store.py, removed in T16), filter helpers (src/holodeck/lib/retrieval/adapters/sk_bridge.py, formerly lib/collection_filter.py; removed in T16), keyword routing, hierarchical tool. “Native” describes inspected routing, not a live test result.

Provider Current collection owner Hybrid route Native filtered enumeration / full scan 2026-09 candidate direction (superseded by the 2026-11 scan below) postgres SK BM25/OpenSearch + application RRF Implemented LlamaIndex Postgres; audit schema, psycopg/asyncpg and enumeration azure-ai-search SK SK native hybrid Unsupported by HoloDeck helper LlamaIndex Azure AI Search plus required operation adapter qdrant SK collection shell + native client HoloDeck dense/full-text RRF Implemented LlamaIndex/native compatibility adapter; preserve existing data weaviate SK SK native hybrid Implemented LlamaIndex Weaviate with native operation coverage chromadb SK + HoloDeck client setup BM25/OpenSearch + application RRF Implemented LlamaIndex Chroma; audit blocking methods faiss SK BM25/OpenSearch + application RRF Unsupported by HoloDeck helper LlamaIndex FAISS plus metadata/persistence support as required azure-cosmos-nosql SK SK native hybrid Unsupported by HoloDeck helper LlamaIndex Cosmos NoSQL plus capability verification azure-cosmos-mongo SK Falls through to BM25 fallback Unsupported by HoloDeck helper LlamaIndex Cosmos MongoDB; resolve routing/name drift sql-server SK BM25/OpenSearch + application RRF Unsupported by HoloDeck helper No verified LlamaIndex candidate; native adapter or evaluated integration required pinecone SK BM25/OpenSearch + application RRF Unsupported by HoloDeck helper LlamaIndex Pinecone; source manifest/enumeration strategy required in-memory SK BM25 + application RRF Implemented LlamaIndex simple store or small typed adapter; same behavior contract

There is naming drift: mongodb appears in native-hybrid capability sets but is not a collection-factory provider. azure-cosmos-mongo is absent from both explicit native/fallback sets and reaches fallback through the selector default.

Unsupported reads affect incremental ingestion, source deletion, and cold-start reload. Some callers catch errors into reingest or empty results. These are existing gaps to resolve or reject clearly, not behavior to preserve as successful parity. The new matrix must include existence/create, all record families, upsert, ID read/delete, metadata predicates, pagination, source replacement, restart, vector/lexical/hybrid search, score semantics, installability, and client ownership.

docs.title: Qdrant compatibility details
docs.text:
• Client construction (src/holodeck/lib/vector_store.py, removed in T16) created an async client explicitly because SK otherwise closes a client across collection contexts.
  • Filtered reads (src/holodeck/lib/retrieval/adapters/sk_bridge.py, formerly lib/collection_filter.py; removed in T16) used native paginated scroll and omit vectors.
  • Hierarchical ingestion derives UUIDv5 IDs from tool/chunk identity. It creates keyword indexes for section/definition/source fields and a WORD full-text index for searchable_text, with lowercase tokens and lengths 2–20.
  • Searchable text includes contextual body, ancestry and section ID twice, the defined term three times, cross references, and filename.
  • Hybrid retrieval uses dense vector embedding plus tokenized MatchText OR filters, candidate count max(4 * top_k, 20), and RRF fusion. Empty token queries use dense-only candidates. Payload decoding supplies source/context without loading the full corpus.
  • Native-hybrid providers skip unused fallback BM25/OpenSearch setup and full-corpus loading.

A connector default that introduces sparse embeddings, renames vectors, nests payload metadata differently, or reassigns IDs changes this contract. It needs a deliberate migration and retrieval-quality evidence.

docs.title: Parsing and persistence evidence
docs.text:
The three record families in vector_store.py carry plain, structured, and hierarchical documents. Dynamic metadata, source keys, dimensions, score interpretation, and JSON-string relationship fields need explicit conversion rules. Current vector results clamp similarity to [0, 1]; a replacement must distinguish distances from similarities before normalization.

TextChunker wraps SK and currently ignores accepted overlap/separator options. StructuredChunker is already HoloDeck code using tiktoken. It must not be replaced merely because LlamaIndex has a splitter.

FileProcessor serves ingestion and multimodal inputs, including selected pages, Excel sheet/range processing, headings, URLs, and caching. A generic reader listing is not evidence that those extraction semantics are preserved. Reader selection needs format fixtures and license/optional-dependency review.

docs.title: Text splitting
docs.text:
lib/text_chunker.py is the only non-storage SK import. SK's splitter counts tokens as len(text) // 4, and HoloDeck's wrapper accepts overlap and separator options that it ignores.

Candidate Version Weight Finding In-house splitter on tiktoken n/a No new package; tiktoken is already required Estimated 80–120 lines plus tests. Honours size, overlap and separators. semantic-text-splitter 0.33.1 No dependencies (Rust wheel) Cannot honour custom separators. chonkie 1.7.0 6 required packages Workable; more than the need. langchain-text-splitters, llama-index-core current Pull their framework core Not justified for one function.

Any replacement that counts real tokens changes chunk boundaries. FR-022 and FR-023 apply: new pipeline fingerprint and controlled reindexing.

docs.title: Document parsing
docs.text: Candidate Version Finding markitdown 0.1.9 (2026-10-21), stable Granular extras exist (pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, xls, outlook, audio and others). The base package still requires magika, which pulls onnxruntime. [all] requires a package that has only prereleases. docling current Pulls torch. Too heavy for the base host. unstructured 0.27.x Requires Python <3.14. pymupdf4llm current AGPL. kreuzberg, LiteParse current Light and permissively licensed. Not evaluated against fixtures; watch only.

docs.title: NLP metrics and sparse search
docs.text:
• evaluate 0.4.6 has had no release since 2025-09. Only ROUGE and METEOR go through it; evaluate.load fetches metric scripts from the Hugging Face Hub at first use. BLEU already calls sacrebleu directly.
  • Direct calls reproduce the wrappers: rouge_scorer.RougeScorer(...).score(...) and NLTK single_meteor_score(alpha=0.9, beta=3, gamma=0.5). Score equality on HoloDeck fixtures is not yet proven.
  • rouge-score 0.1.2 (2022) requires NLTK, so NLTK and its scoped security exception stay. No NLTK-free METEOR was found.
  • rank-bm25 0.2.2 (2022) still works on Python 3.14. bm25s 0.3.16 is active, but no mode reproduces BM25Okapi's idf floor (epsilon times average idf), so rankings change.
  • DeepEval 4.3.3 still requires pytest, four pytest plugins and posthog at run time and has no slim extra.

docs.title: Recommendation and decision
docs.text:
Ranked options for replacing SK storage:

  1. Native adapters behind a HoloDeck-owned interface. Build qdrant, postgres, chromadb and in-memory first; most of that code exists. Add pinecone (which unlocks client 10), then weaviate, azure-ai-search and azure-cosmos-nosql. Decide separately whether faiss, sql-server and azure-cosmos-mongo are kept: none has an install extra, a sample or a live test today.
  2. Microsoft Agent Framework vector stores. Revisit when the API leaves experimental status and chroma, pinecone and weaviate connectors exist. The HoloDeck interface from option 1 keeps this open.
  3. LlamaIndex. Heaviest core, a second workflow runtime in the graph, a resolver conflict on Postgres, and no connector that meets the enumeration requirement.
  4. LangChain or Haystack. Same pin lag as SK, plus a second document contract or pipeline runtime.

Supporting selections: an in-house tiktoken splitter; MarkItDown with selective extras; direct ROUGE/METEOR calls without evaluate; keep rank-bm25.

Evidence that would change the ranking: Agent Framework vector stores reaching general availability with the missing connectors; a LlamaIndex release that adds paged enumeration and drops the workflows requirement; measured adapter cost far above the estimates here.

Decision (2026-11-10): option 1 is adopted. The spec's objective, working assumptions, section 3, FR-019, FR-021, FR-022 and open-decision table were revised to match. Provider scope for faiss, sql-server and azure-cosmos-mongo remains open.

docs.title: Required next evidence
docs.text:
• A maintainer decision on provider scope for faiss, sql-server and azure-cosmos-mongo (FR-014).
  • The operation matrix for each kept store, with live tests.
  • Frozen retrieval, parser and metric fixtures before any replacement.
  • Installed-profile measurements (packages, bytes, import time) for old and new graphs (FR-008).
  • A stored-data migration and rollback design (FR-023).

This record does not authorize installing dependencies or migrating production data.

docs.text:
Complete, runnable HoloDeck agents live in their own repository:

👉 github.com/justinbarias/holodeck-samples

Each sample ships for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and Anthropic (Claude), so you can see the same agent run on either backend.

docs.text: Sample What it shows Ticket Routing Structured output, classification, confidence scoring Customer Support RAG, conversation memory, escalation workflows Content Moderation Multi-category classification, policy enforcement Legal Summarization Document analysis, clause extraction, risk identification Legal Assistant Hierarchical document search, hybrid search, structured citations Financial Assistant Hierarchical document search, Qdrant native hybrid search, code graders, multi-turn test cases

docs.title: In-repo sample
docs.text: sample/openai-agents-full is a single agent that exercises every shipped OpenAI Agents backend capability: function tools, vectorstore and hierarchical-document RAG, an MCP server, subagents (handoffs), inline and SKILL.md skills, disallowed tools, reasoning effort, budget cap, fallback model, tracing, and tool-asserting test cases. docs.title: Run one
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/justinbarias/holodeck-samples
cd holodeck-samples/financial-assistant/openai   # or /claude, /azure
cp .env.sample .env        # fill in your credentials
holodeck test run agent.yaml

The OpenAI/Azure samples need the openai-agents extra; RAG samples also need a vector-store extra (e.g. qdrant).

H-031 The pre-commit job on PR #442 fails on MyPy errors in scripts/verify/profile_probe.py (VectorstoreTool and DatabaseConfig calls, and a None passed to NumericProposer.begin). make verify-fast type-checks only src, so it did not catch them. mypy scripts/verify/profile_probe.py run alone passes, so the hook's MyPy settings differ; reproduce with pre-commit run mypy --all-files. Azure OpenAI, Ollama and a Temporal server were also not part of make verify-live (AC-03). Verify-suite maintainers Fix the probe so the hook passes; add scripts to the MyPy run in verify-fast; run the live loop on Azure OpenAI and Ollama when credentials exist. Partly resolved 2026-11-10 (PR #442): the probe is fixed and the hook passes. Open: scripts in the verify-fast MyPy run, and an Azure OpenAI live run. The 035 completion plan schedules H-009 and retains H-008 as a separate decommission effort. The 035 reconciliation audits the 035 portion of H-001. Other feature inventories remain outside this audit.

docs.title: Test audit, 2026-11
docs.text: Audit date: 2026-11-09. Base: d382992 on main. Scope: tests/ and the coverage of src/holodeck. The audit itself only reported findings. With maintainer approval, H1–H5 were then fixed in test code only, on branch claude/test-audit-bd1afc. See Resolution of H1–H5.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The procedure adapts the OpenClaw test-audit skill (SKILL.md, CAMPAIGN.md, and references/audit.md from the same directory). The skill was written for a TypeScript/Vitest repository. This audit translated its checks to pytest as follows.

Skill check Python/pytest translation used here Assertion-free probes, self-comparisons, constant asserts AST scan of every test_* function: no assert, pytest.raises/warns, or mock.assert_*; x == x; assert True Subject-generated expected values, mocks that supply asserted behavior AST scan for tests that never reference a holodeck import, plus assert result is mock_x.return_value greps, then manual reading Negative controls that pass on an unrelated guard Manual reading of error-path tests, permissive exit_code in (...) asserts, and RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... never awaited lines in the run log Names that promise behavior the test never exercises Manual reading of every flagged test Test-only exports and production seams Grep of src/holodeck for reset/for-test helpers, then caller search Duplicate contracts and repeated layers Duplicate test names across files and per-command copies Campaign step 1 (baseline) Full suite run with branch coverage and durations Retention bar Applied before listing a finding. Retained false positives are listed at the end.

Skipped skill steps:

  • Campaign steps 3 to 8 (per-lane ledgers, cutover, mutation proof, PR handoff). They edit code, and this task is report-only.
  • OpenClaw-only tooling: pnpm deadcode:*, scripts/check-changed.mjs, the Vitest proof policy in openclaw-testing/SKILL.md, and docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md. These do not exist in this repository.
  • Commit, push, and land steps. They are outside this task's authority.

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text:
Command (Python 3.10.18, the CI version; uv sync --all-extras --frozen):

uv run pytest -n auto -q --cov --cov-branch --durations=40
Measure Value Result 6,032 passed, 66 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0 Wall time 133.8 s (10 macOS workers) Collected test functions (static) 5,362 in 285 files Test LOC / production LOC 114,947 / 62,595 Coverage (line + branch, src/holodeck, dashboard omitted) 91.0 %; branches 4,622 / 5,460 Warnings 1,557, including 80 PytestCollectionWarning, 11 RuntimeWarning (never-awaited coroutines), 2 PytestUnknownMarkWarning

All 66 skips come from live-credential gates or missing optional clients. None is a failure. Note: a fresh worktree without UV_PYTHON resolves to Python 3.14, and onnxruntime==1.20.1 has no 3.14 wheel, so uv run fails before tests start.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Severity: High means a test cannot detect the regression its name describes. Medium means a real gap in proof or enforcement. Low means cost, coupling, or hygiene.

docs.title: H1. The retry cap test cannot fail when the cap is removed, and it sleeps 17 s (resolved)
docs.text:
• Evidence: test_base.py:183-203 asserts only elapsed_time >= 16.0. With max_delay removed, the delays are 1+2+4+8+16 = 31 s, which still passes. It is the slowest test in the suite (17.01 s). test_azure_ai.py:488-518 (6.0 s; file removed in 042 T18) and test_base.py:174 use the same lower-bound timing pattern.
  • Contract: BaseEvaluator._calculate_delay returns min(base * exp**attempt, max_delay) (base.py:171-194).
  • Fix: patch holodeck.lib.evaluators.base.asyncio.sleep with a recorder. Assert the exact delays [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 5.0, 5.0]. This adds the missing upper bound and removes about 25 s of real sleep.

docs.title: H2. The chat error-path tests pass for the wrong reason (resolved)
docs.text:
• Evidence: test_chat_errors.py:335-368 sets process_message to raise ExecutionError. The chat loop calls process_message_streaming (chat.py:381). On an AsyncMock that call returns a coroutine, so async for raises TypeError. The generic handler at chat.py:432 catches it. The baseline log shows RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited at chat.py:381 and chat.py:438 for exactly these tests. The assertion result.exit_code in (0, 1, 2) or "Error" in result.output accepts almost every outcome, and error_msg is never checked. test_chat_errors.py:280 and :314 use the same permissive or assertions.
  • Effect: the successful streaming path in chat.py:384-430 is not covered (chat.py is at 75.2 %).
  • Fix: mock process_message_streaming as an async generator that raises ExecutionError(error_msg). Assert error_msg in result.output and exit_code == 0. Add one streaming happy-path test.

docs.title: H3. Middleware logging assertions can never fail (resolved)
docs.text:
• Evidence: test_middleware.py:131-139, :152-160, and :488-495 loop over mock_logger.info.call_args_list and run assert True; break on a match. If no call matches, the loop ends and the test passes. The tests claim to prove session-ID extraction from the query, header priority, and 500-status logging.
  • Fix: assert any(c.kwargs.get("extra", {}).get("session_id") == "query-session-456" for c in mock_logger.info.call_args_list). Use the same pattern for the other two tests.

docs.title: H4. Hierarchical document tool tests that run no code (resolved)
docs.text:
• Evidence, test_hierarchical_document_tool.py:
  • test_contextual_embeddings_when_enabled (:2126-2171) builds mocks and patches, then runs pass with the comment "Skip the actual test since chunker is None".
  • test_contextual_embeddings_disabled_reason_logged (:2174-2190) never calls the tool. Its name promises a log check.
  • test_ingest_logs_warning_no_files (:2019-2038) patches the private _discover_files and asserts nothing. Its name promises a warning.
  • Fix: delete the first two, or rewrite them through _ingest_documents with caplog. Add a caplog assertion to the third.

docs.title: H5. Observability tests that test Python, not HoloDeck (resolved)
docs.text:
• Evidence, test_logging_coordination.py:
  • test_observability_config_enabled_check (:20) asserts Pydantic field defaults.
  • test_observability_enabled_check_pattern (:32) asserts the short-circuit behavior of Python and on MagicMock.
  • test_otel_replaces_setup_logging_when_enabled (:61) and test_setup_logging_used_when_otel_disabled (:75) define the decision function inside the test and assert on it. No production code runs.
  • test_otel_shutdown_flushes_logs (:107) has no assertion.
  • test_otel_logger_provider_initialized (:93) initializes real global OTel providers and never shuts them down. The baseline log contains repeated ValueError: I/O operation on closed file tracebacks from the OTel log export thread. This shows provider state leaking past the test.
  • The real contract (CLI commands choose OTel or setup_logging) already has owners in test_{chat,test,optimize}_observability.py and serve/test_server_observability.py.
  • Fix: delete the four tautological tests. Add a shutdown, or a fixture that resets OTel global providers, to the two tests that initialize real providers. Give test_otel_shutdown_flushes_logs an observable check (for example, an in-memory exporter that receives the flushed record).

docs.title: M1. The Docker build integration tests cannot fail, and --strict-markers is not enforced
docs.text:
• Evidence: test_build_image.py:153-168 asserts only inside if result.exit_code == 0:. :170-184 accepts exit_code in (0, 3), where 3 is the Docker-error code. @pytest.mark.docker is not registered in pyproject.toml. addopts includes --strict-markers, but pytest 9.0.3 only warns (PytestUnknownMarkWarning, 2 occurrences) and the file passes. test_cli_help.py:95-109 has the same shape for holodeck --version: it accepts exit 2 ("option not found") and asserts only inside if result.exit_code == 0.
  • Fix: register docker. Gate with skipif(no docker daemon) and assert exit_code == 0 when the test runs. Assert exit_code == 0 and a version pattern for --version. Find out why --strict-markers does not reject unknown marks under pytest 9. One option to evaluate is the strict_markers = true ini key.

docs.title: M2. The "dual-backend" integration test exercises neither backend
docs.text:
• Evidence: the docstring of test_multi_turn_dual_backend.py:1-14 says HOLODECK_IT_OPENAI=1 and HOLODECK_IT_ANTHROPIC=1 run live backends. The code at :101-130 skips when those variables are set (pytest.skip("TODO: wire real ... session")). Otherwise it runs a Mock backend with a spoofed __class__.__name__. So the live path does not exist, and the default path proves only class-name dispatch plus token summation.
  • Fix: rename and move it to tests/unit as a dispatch test, or implement the live variant behind a live marker (see M5).

docs.title: M3. Modules with little or no default-suite proof
docs.text:
Module Coverage Cause cli/commands/test_view.py 27.4 % No test references it services/mcp_registry.py 29.0 % Only the live tests in test_mcp_registry_client.py exercise it. SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS defaults to true, so all 19 are skipped. CLI tests mock the client. lib/logging_utils.py 39.7 % No test references it cli/commands/chat.py 75.2 % See H2 lib/collection_filter.py (removed in 042 T4) 79.8 % The TestWeaviate class (test_collection_filter.py:294, removed with the module) skips because weaviate-client is not part of --all-extras. The same is true in CI. serve/protocols/agui.py 81.7 % Lines 834-865 are not covered
  • Fix: add httpx.MockTransport tests for the mcp_registry HTTP and error mapping. Add a CliRunner test for holodeck test view against a fixture run file. Either add weaviate-client to a test extra or accept the gap in writing.

docs.title: M4. The 80 % coverage target is not enforced by the CI job
docs.text:
• Evidence: ci.yml:59 runs pytest --cov without --cov-fail-under. The Makefile ci-github target has --cov-fail-under=$(MIN_COVERAGE), but ci.yml does not call it. codecov.yml sets an 80 % status target with require_ci_to_pass: false. This audit did not check whether branch protection requires that Codecov status. The constitution target is restated in QUALITY_SCORE.md, but no gate enforces it.
  • Risk is low today (91 %). Fix: add fail_under = 80 to [tool.coverage.report].

docs.title: M5. Tier markers are inconsistent, and live gates are copied per file
docs.text:
• Evidence: 130 of 241 unit files carry unit. 37 of 43 integration files carry integration. test_pdf_heading_detection.py marks integration inside tests/unit. Twelve files define their own skip_if_no_claude_oauth / skip_if_no_openai / skip_if_no_azure / skip_if_no_ollama (for example test_chat_executor_claude.py:31 and test_claude_instrumentation.py:98). No live marker exists.
  • Effect: a verify-fast / verify-live split cannot select tiers with -m. It must rely on paths and environment variables.
  • Fix: register live (and docker). Move the credential gates into a shared conftest helper that applies live together with the skipif. Optionally, add a pytest_collection_modifyitems hook that marks tests by directory.

docs.title: L1. A test-only production seam
docs.text: openai_agents_tracing.py:179 _reset_tracing_router() says "test isolation only". Its only callers are test_openai_agents_tracing.py:283,289 and test_openai_agents_fallback_runner.py:231,236. Fix: a fixture that uses monkeypatch.setattr to replace _registry and _router. Then delete the function.

docs.title: L2. Implementation-coupled unit suites
docs.text:
File Private attribute assignments patch.object(..., "_x") calls test_hierarchical_document_tool.py 136 27 test_claude_backend.py 65 0 test_vectorstore_tool.py 37 0 test_file_processor.py 0 31

Renaming a private helper breaks these tests. That conflicts with the skill rule that behavior-preserving refactors must not break tests. Fix (campaign-sized): drive the tools through initialize() / search() with a fake embedding service and an in-memory store. Do this one lane at a time.

docs.title: L3. Ownership and layout drift
docs.text:
• tests/unit/agent/test_executor_coverage.py (949 lines) has the docstring "Additional coverage tests for chat/executor.py". It tests holodeck.chat.executor, but tests/unit/chat/ exists. The file name shows it was written to raise coverage, not to own a contract.
  • tests/unit/test_vectorstore_tool.py (2,494 lines) is at the unit root, but its siblings are in tests/unit/tools/.
  • Fix: move these files to the owner directories during the next change in each area.

docs.title: L4. Per-command observability tests duplicate copied wiring
docs.text: initialize_observability setup is copied into serve.py:126, optimize.py:227, chat.py:190, and test.py:219. Four test files (1,072 lines) re-prove it with call-shape asserts. Thirty-seven tests discard the runner.invoke(...) result. Most are in these files and in test_chat.py / test_test.py. A crash after initialization still passes. Fix: assert result.exit_code where the result is discarded. Longer term, extracting one shared context manager (a production change, so ask first) would allow one owner test plus one smoke test per command.

docs.title: L5. Dead or slow test fragments
docs.text:
• test_file_processor.py:1261 is unconditionally pytest.skip(...). Delete it.
  • test_runs_fingerprint.py:61,89 uses time.sleep(1.1) twice to bump the mtime. Use os.utime instead.
  • Exporter tests leave PeriodicExportingMetricReader ticker threads running without a provider. After H5, 16 Cannot call collect on a MetricReader until it is registered tracebacks still appear per full run (the OTel log-export leak is gone). Shut the readers down in teardown.
  • 80 PytestCollectionWarnings come from production classes TestCaseModel, TestExecutor, TestReport, and TestResult that are imported into tests. Set __test__ = False on those classes, or filter the warning.

docs.title: Retained false positives
docs.text:
These matched a junk pattern but pass the retention bar:

  • test_tool_hooks.py:232 session.tool_events is session.tool_events checks that the property is memoized. It fails if the property builds a new queue on each access.
  • test_feel_conformance.py never imports holodeck. It pins the behavior of the bkflow-feel dependency, which is an independent dependency contract.
  • warnings.simplefilter("error") tests with no assert in test_claude_config.py (:451, :458, :590-645) are valid negative controls with paired positive tests.
  • Assertion-free validator tests in test_validators.py, test_feel.py, and test_sandbox_safety.py prove "does not raise", and a sibling test proves the raise.
  • 34 assert x is mock_y identity assertions, for example in test_selector.py, prove dispatch and routing contracts.
  • Temporal subprocess and sandbox tests that never import holodeck in the test body run production code in a child process.

docs.title: Relation to QUALITY_SCORE.md
docs.text:
QUALITY_SCORE.md (2026-09-06) grades most areas B with "not rerun here". This audit adds:

  • New (not in QUALITY_SCORE or the tech-debt tracker): H1-H5, M1, M2, the M3 module list, M4, M5, and L1-L5.
  • Known, now measured: the "80 % coverage target, measure explicitly" policy. Measured at 91.0 %, but not gated (M4).
  • Known, unchanged: "Live stores require service-specific verification" (Tools) and "Cloud behavior requires authorized end-to-end validation" (Serving). The skip list confirms these paths are covered only by credential-gated tests. M5 is the tooling gap that makes them hard to run as a tier.
  • Known, not re-reported: global import-layer enforcement (C) and spec freshness (C).

This audit does not change any QUALITY_SCORE row.

docs.title: Suggested order
docs.text:
1. ~~H1-H5~~: done. See below.
  2. M5 and M1: register live / docker markers and fix strict-marker enforcement before the tiered verify suite depends on markers.
  3. M3 and M4: add the missing owner tests, then add fail_under.
  4. L1-L5 opportunistically. Treat L2 as a separate per-lane campaign.

docs.title: Resolution of H1–H5
docs.text:
Fixed on 2026-11-09 on branch claude/test-audit-bd1afc. Only test code changed: no change to src/, pyproject.toml, or uv.lock.

Proof method: for each fix, one deliberate change to the production owner made the fixed test fail. Every source file was then restored with git checkout and verified clean. For H2, H3, and H5, the HEAD versions of the tests ran against the same mutants and passed, which shows the old tests were blind to them.

Finding Change Mutant (production change) New tests HEAD tests H1 test_base.py: a recorded_sleeps fixture replaces asyncio.sleep in holodeck.lib.evaluators.base. Exact delays are asserted: [1.0, 2.0] and [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 5.0, 5.0]. test_azure_ai.py (removed in 042 T18) asserted [2.0, 4.0] the same way. _calculate_delay returns delay (cap removed) test_max_delay_cap fails: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] != [1, 2, 4, 5, 5] By arithmetic, the old elapsed >= 16.0 also holds at 31 s H1 as above delay × 1.5 3 tests fail — H2 test_chat_errors.py: a _streaming_session helper streams chunks or raises from process_message_streaming. The error tests assert exit_code == 0, Error: <msg>, and a successful next turn. New test_streaming_reply_is_displayed covers the happy path. The Ctrl+C tests patch click.prompt to raise KeyboardInterrupt and assert exit 130, terminate awaited, and Goodbye!. The empty-line test asserts the session is never called. The REPL except Exception re-raises instead of logging 3 fail 5 passed H2 as above composer.write_text(chunk) removed 4 fail — H2 as above sys.exit(130) → sys.exit(0) 1 fails — H2 as above session_manager.terminate() removed 3 fail — H2 as above Empty-input continue removed 1 fails — H3 test_middleware.py: an _info_extras helper asserts the exact extra of the "Request started" and "Request completed" log calls. This replaces the five loops that could pass with zero matches. "status_code": 200 in the completion log test_middleware_order_matters fails 2 passed H3 as above Query-parameter session ID ignored 1 fails 10 passed H3 as above session_id dropped from the start log, then from the completion log 3 fail each time — H3 as above Query parameter checked before the header 1 fails — H4 test_hierarchical_document_tool.py: both no-op tests now drive _ingest_documents and capture the chunks passed to _embed_chunks. The enabled test asserts the generated context lands in contextualized_content. The disabled test is parametrized over both log reasons. The no-files test uses the real _discover_files with caplog and asserts ingested == 0. No-files warning downgraded to info 1 fails Old test had no assertion H4 as above Context output ignored, reason text swapped, fallback content blanked, or contextual_embeddings flag ignored 1–2 fail for each mutant Old tests ran no production code H5 test_logging_coordination.py: the four tautological tests are deleted. The provider test asserts the global LoggerProvider and a single root LoggingHandler. The flush test exports through InMemoryLogRecordExporter and asserts nothing is exported before shutdown and that flush me is exported after it. New conftest.py isolated_otel fixture: it resets the set-once OTel globals, shuts down the created context, and restores root logger handlers and level. It is also applied to TestInitializeObservability in test_providers.py. shutdown_observability returns early flush test fails 6 passed H5 as above set_logger_provider removed 1 fails — H5 as above Root addHandler(otel_handler) removed 2 fail —

H3 also exposed a wrong test premise. test_middleware_order_matters added the middlewares in the reverse of the production order (server.py:422-423). In that order LoggingMiddleware never logs the 500, and the old loop hid this. The test now uses the server's order and explains why the order matters.

H2 also rewrote the two TestValidationErrors tests, which had the same defect. One mocked the unused process_message. The other sent an empty line, which the CLI skips before it reaches the session.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Check Result Changed test files, 3 parallel runs 337 passed each run Full suite (uv run pytest -n auto, Python 3.10) 6,030 passed, 66 skipped, exit 0, 100.7 s (baseline: 6,032 passed, 133.8 s). Delta: −4 deleted tautologies, +1 streaming test, +1 parametrized case. RuntimeWarning never-awaited coroutines at chat.py 0 (baseline 2) OTel log-export I/O operation on closed file tracebacks 0. The 17 that remain come from metric-reader tickers (16) and OpenAI tracing (1); see L5. ruff check, black --check on changed files Pass mypy on changed files tests/ is excluded from the mypy gate in pre-commit. Error counts are at or below HEAD: test_chat_errors.py 10 → 5, other files unchanged, new conftest.py 0. make harness-check Pass

The isolated_otel fixture replaces private OTel module globals (_TRACER_PROVIDER, _*_SET_ONCE, and their log and metric equivalents). These names exist in the locked opentelemetry-sdk 1.39.1. Recheck them when the OTel SDK upgrade (1.45) lands.

docs.text: Bring the Claude Agent SDK backend to full serve/deploy parity with the Semantic Kernel backend. The protocol-level abstraction (AgentBackend/AgentSession) is already backend-agnostic — this feature addresses the practical gaps: serve pre-flight validation, Dockerfile Node.js injection, container entrypoint fixes, backend-aware health checks, subprocess lifecycle management, and integration test coverage.

docs.title: Phase 1: Serve Pre-Flight Validation (FR-001, FR-006, FR-008, FR-012, FR-013)
docs.text:
serve.py → _run_server() → AgentServer.start()
                              ↓
                    NEW: _validate_backend_prerequisites()
                              ↓
                    Detect provider from agent_config.model.provider
                              ↓
              ┌── ANTHROPIC ──────────────────────┐
              │  validate_nodejs()  ← enhanced    │
              │  validate_credentials(model)      │
              │  validate_embedding_provider()    │
              │  validate_response_format()       │
              └──────────────────────────────────┘
                              ↓
                    Pass → state = RUNNING → uvicorn starts
                    Fail → log error → sys.exit(1)

Key decision: Validation runs in AgentServer.start() before RUNNING state. On failure, the server exits with a clear error message — it never transitions to RUNNING.

FR-006 (env var pass-through): Proxy and credential env vars (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY) are provided by the operator at docker run time and inherited by child processes. No explicit forwarding code is needed. However, verify that ClaudeAgentOptions.env (constructed in build_options() at claude_backend.py:272) merges with rather than replaces the inherited environment — add a unit test to confirm proxy env vars reach the SDK subprocess.

FR-013 (OTel instrumentation): GenAI semantic convention instrumentation activates automatically via ClaudeBackend.initialize() → _activate_instrumentation(). This works in serve mode because AgentExecutor calls BackendSelector.select() which triggers initialize(). Add an integration test to verify OTel spans are emitted when serving Claude agents.

docs.title: Phase 4: Entrypoint Fixes (FR-004, FR-011)
docs.text:
Two entrypoints exist in the codebase — they serve different purposes:

Inline entrypoint (deploy.py _prepare_build_context(), lines 642-650): - Used by holodeck deploy build output — this is what deployed containers actually run - Already correct: uses positional arg (holodeck serve /app/agent.yaml) - Add Claude validation: check node --version and credential env vars before exec holodeck serve

docker/entrypoint.sh (base image, line 111): - Used only when running the base Docker image directly (not via deploy build) - Has --config bug: passes --config ${HOLODECK_AGENT_CONFIG} but holodeck serve uses @click.argument (positional), not --config option - Fix: change to positional arg holodeck serve ${HOLODECK_AGENT_CONFIG} --port ... --protocol ... - Add validate_claude_requirements() function for Node.js + credentials

docs.title: Phase 5: Session Cap & Crash Handling (FR-014, EC-2)
docs.text:
AgentServer.__init__()
    ↓
Read claude.max_concurrent_sessions from agent_config
    ↓
Pass to SessionStore(max_sessions=cap)
    ↓
SessionStore.create() checks len(sessions) < max_sessions
    ↓
Exceeded → raise RuntimeError → endpoint returns 503

Key detail: The existing SessionStore.max_sessions (default 1000) is repurposed. When provider: anthropic, it's overridden by claude.max_concurrent_sessions (default 10). Non-Claude backends keep the 1000 default.

Crash handling: When ClaudeSession.send() raises BackendSessionError (subprocess crash), the protocol handlers (serve/protocols/rest.py, serve/protocols/agui.py) must catch this and return the contract-defined 502 response with {"error": "backend_error", "retriable": true}. The crashed session is removed from SessionStore, freeing the slot.

docs.title: Edge Case Mitigations
docs.text:
• EC-3 (tmpfs fills up): Mitigated by operator-configurable tmpfs size at docker run time (e.g., --tmpfs /tmp:size=500m). Not a code concern — document in deployment guide.
  • EC-4 (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL unreachable): The Claude SDK raises CLIConnectionError which propagates through existing BackendSessionError handling. No new code needed — the error surfaces through standard error paths.

docs.title: Tasks: User Story 1 — Serve a Claude-Backed Agent via REST/AG-UI
docs.text:
Feature: 024-claude-serve-deploy | Story: US1 | Date: 2026-03-20 Spec: spec.md | Plan: plan.md | Data Model: data-model.md

User Story: A platform operator configures an agent with provider: anthropic and runs holodeck serve agent.yaml. The server starts, performs pre-flight validation (Node.js availability, API credentials), and begins accepting requests. Clients interact with the agent through REST or AG-UI protocol endpoints identically to how they would with an OpenAI-backed agent.

Acceptance Scenarios: 1. Given agent config with provider: anthropic and Node.js installed, When operator runs holodeck serve agent.yaml, Then server starts successfully and health endpoint reports ready. 2. Given running Claude-backed server, When client sends message to REST endpoint, Then server returns ExecutionResult-compatible response. 3. Given running Claude-backed server, When client opens streaming session, Then text chunks delivered progressively. 4. Given agent config with provider: anthropic but no Node.js, When operator runs holodeck serve, Then server fails fast with clear error. 5. Given agent config with provider: anthropic but no credentials, When operator runs holodeck serve, Then server fails fast with clear error.

FR Coverage: FR-001, FR-006, FR-008, FR-012, FR-013, FR-014

Add NODEJS_MIN_VERSION: int = 18 at module level after the existing env var candidate tuples. This constant is used by the enhanced validate_nodejs() (T005) and health check validators.

docs.title: Phase 2: Foundational — Blocking Prerequisites
docs.text:
These tasks implement the core validation logic, error mapping, and server lifecycle changes that must exist before the serve path works end-to-end.

  • T004 [US1] Enhance validate_nodejs() in /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/lib/backends/validators.py to verify Node.js version >= 18 (FR-012). After the existing shutil.which("node") check passes, run subprocess.run(["node", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5). Parse the output (format: v22.1.0) — strip the v prefix, split on ., extract the major version as int. If major < NODEJS_MIN_VERSION, raise ConfigError("nodejs", f"Node.js version {version} found but >= {NODEJS_MIN_VERSION} is required by Claude Agent SDK. ..."). Handle subprocess.TimeoutExpired and subprocess.CalledProcessError by raising ConfigError with an actionable message. Import subprocess at the top of the file.

  • T005 [US1] Add _validate_backend_prerequisites() method to AgentServer in /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/server.py (FR-001, FR-008). Implement async def _validate_backend_prerequisites(self) -> None that: (a) checks self.agent_config.model.provider == ProviderEnum.ANTHROPIC, (b) if Anthropic, calls validate_nodejs() and validate_credentials(self.agent_config.model) from holodeck.lib.backends.validators, (c) on ConfigError, raises BackendInitError with the error message. The CLI layer (serve command) catches this and exits. (d) for non-Anthropic providers, returns immediately (no-op). Import BackendInitError from holodeck.lib.backends, ProviderEnum from holodeck.models.llm, and the validator functions.

  • T006 [US1] Integrate _validate_backend_prerequisites() into the server startup lifecycle in /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/server.py. Locate the point where the server transitions to RUNNING state (currently in create_app() which sets READY, then uvicorn starts). Add a call to await self._validate_backend_prerequisites() in the start() method (or the appropriate startup hook) BEFORE the state transitions to RUNNING. The startup lifecycle catches BackendInitError from _validate_backend_prerequisites(), logs the error with logger.error(), and exits. If validation fails, the server never reaches RUNNING state. Log a success message on success: "Backend prerequisites validated for {provider} provider".

  • T007 [US1] Pass Claude session cap to SessionStore in /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/server.py (FR-014). In AgentServer.__init__(), detect if self.agent_config.model.provider == ProviderEnum.ANTHROPIC and self.agent_config.claude is not None. If so, read self.agent_config.claude.max_concurrent_sessions and pass it to SessionStore(max_sessions=cap) instead of the default 1000. Non-Anthropic providers keep the existing 1000 default. Import ProviderEnum from holodeck.models.llm.

  • T008 [US1] Map BackendSessionError to HTTP 502 in REST protocol at /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/protocols/rest.py (FR-014, crash handling). In the chat endpoint handler(s), wrap the AgentExecutor invocation with a try/except that catches BackendSessionError (import from holodeck.lib.backends). When caught, return a JSONResponse with status 502 and body: {"error": "backend_error", "message": "Claude Agent SDK subprocess terminated unexpectedly. Start a new session to retry.", "retriable": true}. Remove the crashed session from the session store.

  • T009 [US1] Map capacity exceeded to HTTP 503 in REST protocol at /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/protocols/rest.py (FR-014, session cap). When SessionStore.create() raises RuntimeError due to max sessions exceeded, catch it and return a JSONResponse with status 503, Retry-After: 5 header, and body matching the session-cap contract: {"error": "capacity_exceeded", "message": "Maximum concurrent Claude sessions ({max}) reached. Retry after existing sessions complete.", "active_sessions": N, "max_sessions": N}.

  • T010 [US1] Map BackendSessionError to SSE error event in AG-UI protocol at /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/protocols/agui.py (FR-014, crash handling). In the AG-UI endpoint handler, wrap the AgentExecutor invocation with a try/except that catches BackendSessionError (import from holodeck.lib.backends). When caught, emit an SSE error event: event: error\ndata: {"type": "backend_error", "message": "Claude Agent SDK subprocess terminated unexpectedly.", "retriable": true}. Remove the crashed session from the session store.

  • T011 [US1] Map capacity exceeded to SSE error event in AG-UI protocol at /Users/justinbarias/Documents/Git/python/agentlab/src/holodeck/serve/protocols/agui.py (FR-014, session cap). When SessionStore.create() raises RuntimeError due to max sessions exceeded, catch it and emit an SSE error event: event: error\ndata: {"type": "capacity_exceeded", "message": "Maximum concurrent Claude sessions ({max}) reached."}.
