docs.title: LLM-provider credentials (read in src/holodeck/lib/backends/validators.py:146-234)
docs.text: auth_provider Env vars on the SDK subprocess today Endpoint hit P3 disposition api_key ANTHROPIC_API_KEY api.anthropic.com Moved to sidecar. Envoy injects x-api-key. oauth_token CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN claude.ai backend (api.anthropic.com) Moved to sidecar. Envoy injects authorization: Bearer … (header name confirmed by SDK source — Task 2 verification step). custom ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Operator-supplied Token moved to sidecar; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL re-pointed at localhost. Sidecar's upstream is the operator's original endpoint, derived from agent.model.endpoint. bedrock CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1, AWS_REGION (+ AWS access key/secret from outside HoloDeck) bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com Rejected by hardened profile in v1. SigV4 signing happens inside the AWS SDK client; not transparently proxiable. Task 8 emits a load-time error. vertex CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1, CLOUD_ML_REGION, ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID (+ ADC credentials) <region>.aiplatform.googleapis.com Rejected by hardened profile in v1. Same reason. Task 8 emits a load-time error. foundry CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1, ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE or ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL Operator-supplied Foundry endpoint Rejected by hardened profile in v1. Foundry credential context is opaque. Task 8 emits a load-time error.

docs.title: Embedding-provider credentials (read by Semantic Kernel AgentFactory, injected via set_embedding_service on vectorstore tools)
docs.text:
Provider Env vars on the serve process today Endpoint hit P3 disposition openai (embeddings) OPENAI_API_KEY api.openai.com/v1/embeddings Moved to sidecar. Envoy injects authorization: Bearer …. Upstream domain added to allowlist. azure_openai (embeddings) AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY + endpoint from agent.yaml <resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/... Moved to sidecar. Envoy injects api-key: …. Upstream domain (<resource>.openai.azure.com) derived from agent.embedding_provider.endpoint and added to allowlist.

Embedding tool implementations read these via the SK service, which makes the same HTTP call we need to intercept. The intercept happens at the SK service's base URL — we set the SK service's base URL to http://localhost:7000 and let Envoy route by :authority / path. Concrete code path to investigate in Task 5: how the SK service base URL is configured at construction time. If the SK service does not respect a base-URL override, fall back to setting OPENAI_BASE_URL / AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT env vars (Task 5 spike).

docs.title: Vector-store credentials
docs.text:
Backend Where credentials live today P3 disposition Qdrant Cloud connection_string field on agent.tools[*].database (SecretStr in YAML) — embedded URL with API key Sidecar terminates; Envoy injects api-key header on https://<cluster>.qdrant.tech. Connection string is parsed in _resolve_database_config() (base_tool.py:83) but the parsed URL+key are then handed to the Qdrant client which makes the actual HTTPS call. Task 5 spike: confirm Qdrant Python client supports a base-URL override that points at localhost; if not, document Qdrant as out-of-scope for hardened-profile v1. Pinecone api_key in connection params Same risk as Qdrant — client may not respect a generic proxy. Task 5 spike. PostgreSQL (pgvector) postgresql://user:pass@host/db Out of scope. P3 is HTTP-only; pgvector uses the postgres protocol. Document in Task 15. Azure AI Search connection_string with admin key Sidecar terminates; Envoy injects api-key header. Same SDK-override question as Qdrant — Task 5 spike. ChromaDB connection_string (HTTP URL) or persist_directory (local) Local: no creds, no proxy needed. Remote HTTP: Task 5 spike. In-memory None N/A OpenSearch connection_string w/ user:pass Same shape as pgvector if not HTTP; if HTTP, same shape as Qdrant. Task 5 spike.

v1 ground rule: P3 supports vector-store backends only where (a) the wire protocol is HTTPS and (b) the Python client lets us override the base URL. Backends that fail either test are explicitly rejected in hardened mode with a load-time error pointing the operator at the default profile or at the custom-tool pattern. Spec 034 §"What … does not fix" already permits this scope.

docs.title: MCP-server credentials
docs.text: Transport How creds reach today P3 disposition stdio (the only one HoloDeck routes today — see mcp_bridge.py:51-95) tool.env + tool.env_file, passed to subprocess via McpStdioServerConfig.env Unchanged. Stdio MCPs run inside the agent container; their HTTPS egress (e.g. a Brave Search MCP calling api.search.brave.com) goes through the agent's HTTP stack. To route them through the sidecar: Task 7 sets HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:7000 on the agent container, so any well-behaved Python/Node MCP that respects proxy env vars uses Envoy. The MCP's own API keys still live in its declared env (no way to move them to the sidecar without per-MCP custom filters). This is documented as a known boundary in Task 15: the SDK subprocess (Claude Code CLI) and its stdio MCP children inherit the agent's env, so their creds are inside the agent's blast radius. The sidecar protects the destination of their egress but not their per-MCP API keys. http / sse MCP headers dict on the tool config (already in agent.yaml). Today build_claude_mcp_configs logs a warning and skips them. Out of scope in P3. Document.

docs.title: OTEL credentials
docs.text: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is typically internal (Aspire dashboard, OTLP collector inside the same cluster) and not a credential. Optional OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS could carry an auth token; P3 leaves it on the agent container — it's a telemetry path, not an LLM credential path, and routing it through Envoy adds a moving part with no clear win. Documented in Task 15.

docs.title: Task 2: Spike — verify base-URL override paths
docs.text:
This task does not write production code. It produces a 1–2 page memo (docs/product-specs/034-production-hardening/2026-05-24-spec-034-p3-baseurl-spike.md) that confirms or rejects three assumptions the rest of the plan depends on.

Questions to answer (with code references, not opinions):

  • Anthropic API via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Does the claude-agent-sdk (and the underlying Claude Code CLI) actually route through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for both api_key and oauth_token auth, including for the OAuth refresh flow? Cite the SDK source or the upstream CLI source. If OAuth refresh hits a hard-coded URL, that's a P3 blocker for oauth_token — document.
  • Anthropic auth header. For oauth_token, confirm the header name the SDK actually sends (authorization: Bearer … vs. something OAuth-specific). The Envoy Lua filter has to know what header to inject; getting this wrong silently fails closed.
  • OpenAI / Azure OpenAI base-URL overrides. Does the Semantic Kernel OpenAITextEmbedding accept a constructor arg (or env var) that we can use to redirect to http://localhost:7000? Same for AzureTextEmbedding. Cite the SK constructor signatures and whether HoloDeck currently exposes them.
  • Qdrant / Azure AI Search clients. Do their Python clients accept a base-URL override that survives the connection_string parser? If not, can we override connection_string at deploy time to point at https://localhost:7000 with SNI-rewriting? (Probably no — SNI to localhost won't match the upstream cert.) The honest answer here is likely: vector stores stay outside the sidecar in v1, and we document that.

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Memo committed under docs/product-specs/034-production-hardening/. - [ ] Each question has a yes/no answer with a file:line citation. - [ ] For every "no" answer, the memo lists which provider/backend it removes from hardened-profile v1.

Verification: Human review of the memo — this is a research task, not an implementable contract.

Dependencies: None (can run in parallel with Task 1). Estimated scope: M — investigation across two SDKs and 2–3 vector-store clients. Budget 1–2 days.

docs.title: Task 3: Implement build_envoy_bootstrap
docs.text:
Files: - Create: src/holodeck/deploy/envoy.py - Create: tests/unit/deploy/test_envoy_generator.py

Design: - [ ] build_envoy_bootstrap(agent: Agent) -> str returns the full bootstrap.yaml content as a string. Pure function. No I/O. - [ ] Listener on 0.0.0.0:7000, HTTP/1.1 + HTTP/2. - [ ] One route_config per allowlisted upstream domain. Each route matches by :authority header (so requests with Host: api.anthropic.com route to the anthropic upstream; everything else falls through to the catch-all direct_response with status 403 and an application/problem+json body matching spec 034 §"Backpressure 429" shape). - [ ] Per-route http_filters chain: one Lua filter that reads /var/run/secrets/envoy/<credname> synchronously at filter init (Envoy hot-restarts pick up new secret values; this is fine) and adds the appropriate header. Header name per route (anthropic → x-api-key, openai → authorization: Bearer, azure openai → api-key). - [ ] Upstream clusters declared with transport_socket of type tls so Envoy terminates the TLS upstream-side with the system trust store. - [ ] Access log to stdout with the route name, response code, and response_time so an operator can kubectl logs (or ACA az containerapp logs show) and see what got allowed/denied.

Allowlist derivation (this is the load-bearing logic): - [ ] api.anthropic.com is always present when agent.model.provider == anthropic and auth_provider in {api_key, oauth_token}. - [ ] When auth_provider == custom, the upstream is the host of agent.model.endpoint. - [ ] When the agent has any tool with embedding_provider set, the embedding provider's endpoint host is added. - [ ] When the agent has any vectorstore/hierarchical_document tool with a connection_string whose scheme is https, the connection_string's host is added (Task 5 may downgrade this). - [ ] No other domains are added.

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Given the financial-assistant sample's agent.yaml, build_envoy_bootstrap returns a YAML that includes upstream clusters for api.anthropic.com and the configured <resource>.openai.azure.com and the Qdrant cluster, in that order, and nothing else. - [ ] Catch-all returns 403 with a problem+json body whose type matches https://holodeck.dev/errors/egress-denied. - [ ] Generated YAML parses cleanly with PyYAML's safe loader. - [ ] Generated YAML is byte-stable across calls (deterministic ordering of clusters → reproducible builds).

Verification: - [ ] pytest tests/unit/deploy/test_envoy_generator.py -n auto -v covers: api_key path, oauth_token path, custom path, embedding-only agent, no-tool agent, agent with multiple vectorstores. - [ ] echo "$(holodeck-internal: dump-envoy-config sample/financial-assistant/claude)" | docker run --rm -i envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31-latest envoy --mode validate -c - returns exit 0 (config validates against real Envoy). Bash helper script lives in scripts/validate_envoy.sh; not a CLI command.

Dependencies: Task 1 (security_profile field), Task 2 (auth-header confirmation). Estimated scope: M — single module, one test file. The bulk of the cost is in getting the Envoy YAML right; allow 1–2 days plus the spike feedback.

docs.title: Task 4: Lua credential-injector filter
docs.text:
Subtask of Task 3, called out separately because it's the source of subtle bugs.

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Lua filter reads /var/run/secrets/envoy/<credname> once on filter init (not per request) and caches in envoy.streamInfo-adjacent state. - [ ] If the file is missing or empty, the filter responds with 500 + application/problem+json body. The agent sees the failure as an upstream error; it does not fall back to direct upstream. - [ ] The injected header replaces (not appends to) any header of the same name from the agent, so a compromised agent can't override the auth header with its own. - [ ] The filter strips Authorization / x-api-key / api-key from the request before injection, regardless of upstream — defense against a leak from the agent.

Verification: - [ ] Unit test the Lua via Envoy's test scaffold (docker run --rm envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31-latest envoy --mode validate) for the bootstrap, then a runtime test in Task 13. - [ ] Test that a request with a forged x-api-key header from the agent is stripped before reaching upstream (visible in access log: stripped count = 1).

Dependencies: Task 3 (same file). Estimated scope: S — small Lua snippet, three test cases.

Remove any of {ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, AWS_*, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, QDRANT_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN} from the agent's env-var list before passing to the deployer. - [ ] The builder reads credential env vars from the operator's host environment (the same surface holodeck deploy run reads today) and constructs the secret list. Once the secret list is built, the local copies are zeroed in env_credentials and not retained in process memory longer than necessary — best-effort, not a guarantee against a debugger.

docs.title: Task 13: Integration test — live ACA deploy under hardened profile
docs.text:
Files: - Create: tests/integration/security/test_hardened_profile_e2e.py

This is the smoke test that exercises the full machinery against a real ACA. Marked @pytest.mark.slow and @pytest.mark.integration; not part of make test by default. Run it via the manual deploy validation loop in CLAUDE.md.

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Test deploys sample/financial-assistant/claude/agent.hardened.yaml to a known ACA environment. - [ ] After /ready returns 200, the test: 1. Hits the AG-UI endpoint with a known-good ConvFinQA query and confirms a 200 with sensible content. 2. Uses az containerapp exec (or equivalent) to printenv inside the agent container and asserts none of the credential env vars are present. 3. Sends a request through the AG-UI surface that would trigger a (hypothetical) tool call to a non-allowlisted domain (e.g. by injecting via a malicious prompt). Confirms the request is rejected by Envoy with a 403 + problem+json body. 4. Confirms the agent's response stream surfaces the upstream 403 cleanly (not a crash).

Verification: - [ ] pytest tests/integration/security/test_hardened_profile_e2e.py -m slow -n auto against a deployed ACA passes.

Dependencies: All P3 tasks. Estimated scope: L — full E2E. The setup cost is real; budget half a sprint for the first green run.

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Names the problem: SigV4 and GCP-auth don't proxy transparently. - [ ] Names three candidate paths: (a) sidecar re-signs requests using its own AWS/GCP credentials (requires the agent's SDK to talk plain HTTP+JSON to the sidecar, which means a new transport mode in claude-agent-sdk — coordinate with upstream); (b) cloud-native workload identity (IRSA on EKS, Workload Identity on GKE, Azure Managed Identity on AKS — none apply to ACA); (c) require operators to use the custom-tool pattern for non-Anthropic Anthropic-routed access. - [ ] Calls out that ACA-specific deployments cannot use option (b), so options (a) and (c) are the realistic ones for HoloDeck's primary deployer.

docs.title: Checkpoint structure
docs.text:
Tasks 1, 2          (parallel)        → SPIKE GATE
Tasks 3, 5           (parallel after 1, 2) → ENVOY + VALIDATOR GATE
Tasks 4, 6           (parallel after 3)    → SIDECAR/DEPLOYER GATE
Tasks 7, 8           (after 4 + 6)         → INTEGRATION GATE
Tasks 9, 10, 11      (parallel after 7+8)  → CLI/SAMPLE GATE
Task 12, 15          (after 11)            → DOCS GATE
Task 13              (after 12)            → E2E GATE (slow)
Tasks 14, 16         (after 13)            → CLOSE

Checkpoints (run between phases):

  • After Task 2 (SPIKE GATE): Open questions resolved or scope narrowed. If the spike reveals oauth_token can't be proxied, drop it from v1 and update Task 5's supported-providers set before any production code lands.
  • After Tasks 3+5 (ENVOY GATE): Pure-function generator unit-tests green; validator rejects all unsupported combos. No deployer changes yet — the whole P3 design is provable against unit tests at this point.
  • After Tasks 6+7 (DEPLOYER GATE): Deployer unit tests green; the financial-assistant sample produces a believable two-container ContainerApp model object. Manual eyeball of the YAML the deployer would emit.
  • After Task 8 (INTEGRATION GATE): Backend fails closed locally with HOLODECK_HARDENED=1 and one credential env var present. This is the proof that the boot guard works before the deployer ever runs.
  • After Tasks 9–11 (CLI GATE): holodeck deploy run produces correct CLI output. Resolution block matches the spec.
  • After Task 13 (E2E GATE): Live ACA deploy passes the three smoke checks. This is the only point at which P3 is mergeable.

docs.title: Risks and mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Task 2 spike discovers oauth_token can't route through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for refresh Drop oauth_token from hardened-profile v1; document in Task 15; revisit when SDK adds proxy support Task 2 spike discovers no vector-store client supports a base-URL override Vector-store creds remain on the agent container; Envoy enforces destination domain via HTTPS_PROXY; document Envoy bootstrap drift across v1.31 minor versions Pin envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31.x to a specific patch; revalidate when bumping ACA Secrets propagation lag (creates → not yet projected when sidecar starts) Sidecar's Lua filter reads on first request, not init; if file missing, returns 500 (visible failure, not silent) — and we already have ACA's normal revision-readiness gating The agent loops on the 403 from Envoy, racking up tokens Already mitigated by max_turns default (P1a) at 20; document the failure mode in Task 12 An operator's host env happens to have a stray OPENAI_API_KEY that the deployer reads and stuffs into ACA Secrets unintentionally Task 7 only reads env vars that match credential patterns and that the agent.yaml's tool/embedding/auth config actually declares a need for. Unread vars are never copied. Lua filter caches a credential file at filter init; subsequent secret rotation requires Envoy hot-restart Document. ACA revision update triggers a fresh container, which re-inits the filter, which picks up the new secret. This is the supported rotation path. Agent code path bypasses ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. a tool that directly imports anthropic client without honoring the env var) Task 8's boot guard makes this loud: any direct call without going through the SDK fails because the agent has no credentials. The 403 from Envoy is a secondary safety net. HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:7000 breaks stdio MCP servers that don't honor proxy env vars (e.g. a Node MCP using a non-proxy-aware fetch lib) Document. Operator opts that MCP out of the sidecar by setting a NO_PROXY entry on the agent container — but then the MCP's egress is direct from the container. Acceptable trade-off; the sidecar protects the LLM credential boundary, not every outbound packet.

docs.title: Open questions resolved before implementation
docs.text:
1. Should the bootstrap be in a secret or a config-map style mount? Decided: secret. ACA does not expose ConfigMap; this is the only file-projection primitive available.
  2. Should P3 ship on GCP Cloud Run and AWS App Runner deployers too? No — v1 is ACA only. The other deployers have their own credential-mount surfaces (Cloud Run Secret Manager, App Runner secrets) and would each be their own task train. Documented as follow-ups in Task 16.
  3. Should the agent container's HOLODECK_HARDENED env var be a name an attacker could spoof to bypass checks? No — the env var only gates additional checks; the absence of credentials in the agent's env is the real invariant. An attacker who unsets HOLODECK_HARDENED doesn't gain credentials they don't already have.
  4. Should we ship a deny-by-default DNS resolver in the sidecar? No — Envoy's allowlist by :authority is sufficient. Adding a CoreDNS sidecar would couple two infrastructure concerns; out of scope.
  5. Where do credentials in P3 actually live? Azure Container App Secrets, mounted via Volume(storage_type=SECRET) only to the sidecar. Not in the image, not in the agent container env, not in any other Azure secret store.

docs.title: v1 contract
docs.text:
• One new schema field: deployment.security_profile: default | hardened.
  • Default profile: zero behavior change.
  • Hardened profile: ACA only, auth providers api_key and oauth_token (and custom when the operator's endpoint is plain Anthropic-shaped), vector stores limited to HTTPS-overridable backends.
  • Credentials in the agent container under hardened profile: zero. Asserted at boot.
  • Allowlist derived from agent.yaml. No silent fallback. Non-allowlisted egress: 403.
  • Sidecar holds credentials; agent fails closed if it sees any.
  • Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry deferred to follow-up spec; rejected with a clear error.
  • TLS interception, pgvector, HTTP/SSE MCP routing, GCP/AWS deployers: documented as out of v1.

docs.text: Status: In progress; T0–T3 complete (4/12 tasks). docs.title: Objective and observable acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Finish the agreed 035 parity scope and close its outstanding acceptance gaps. An OpenAI or Azure agent must support the declared tools, hooks, handoffs, serving, deployment, and telemetry behavior. Claude behavior and provider-neutral execution contracts must remain intact.

Completion requires all twelve tasks below, with linked evidence for each acceptance gate. Every functional requirement and success criterion must have a disposition: verified, superseded by a recorded decision, or explicitly deferred with an owner and exit criterion. A missing credential, skipped test, implemented adapter, or checked historical task does not prove acceptance. The original specification contains superseded requirements. This plan does not claim that its deferred sandbox and hardened-profile scope is delivered.

docs.title: Canonical records and scope
docs.text:
This file is the active execution checklist for completing 035. The full plan remains the detailed design reference for tasks A–K. The old TODO and reconciliation report retain the audited baseline and historical counts. Do not maintain another parallel completion checklist in those records. Update this plan with implementation decisions, test commands, results, and remaining blockers after each task.

In scope:

  • Remaining full-parity tasks D, E, G, I, J, K and the partial F4/H1 acceptance work.
  • Baseline acceptance for implemented A, B, C, F and the MVP/SK cleanup gates.
  • Open LiteLLM migration acceptance in its task record, including H-009.
  • Documentation corrections in the documentation plan.
  • Requirement reconciliation, reproducible fixtures, final verification, and archival of completed records.

Existing deferrals remain separate: P3/Envoy, sandbox mode, computer-use, interactive human approval, MCP-server tool guardrails, modify, prompt-tool execution, and namespace unification. Final Semantic Kernel decommission remains H-008 in the debt tracker. This plan closes the native-backend migration and its inference acceptance. It does not replace the eleven vector-store connectors or remove the SK package. T0 must give each deferred item a durable destination. A deferral must not be labelled implemented.

docs.title: Constraints and decisions
docs.text:
• Use BackendSelector and the contracts in src/holodeck/lib/backends/base.py.
  • Preserve current routing: OpenAI/Azure use OpenAI Agents; Anthropic/Ollama use Claude.
  • Keep the openai: namespace and the Azure /openai/v1 Responses mapping established by #338.
  • Use typed boundary adapters and validated Pydantic configuration. Do not bypass known types with Any or getattr.
  • Preserve multimodal execution, evaluation-model overrides, tool events, and GenAI instrumentation.
  • Keep network calls and blocking I/O outside Temporal workflow execution and async event loops respectively.
  • Verify SDK integration points against the installed, locked SDK before implementation. Do not copy obsolete SDK assumptions from the draft spec.
  • Do not change unrelated working-tree edits or add a repository-wide import linter as part of this feature.
  • The user authorized plan creation and T0 contract reconciliation. Future live deployment validation follows the explicit target-authorization rule in Reliability.

docs.title: Ordered work and verification
docs.text: Task checkboxes mean all listed acceptance and verification criteria are satisfied, not just that source code exists. Dependencies require upstream implementation and local gates to be ready. They do not require live gates assigned to T10 to finish first. Record “implementation ready; live acceptance pending” in progress when that distinction applies. T10 evidence then closes the upstream live gates. Proposed new test files are labelled as additions. Other file paths below are repository-relative.

docs.title: T0 — Establish the final requirement contract
docs.text:
Dependencies: None. Owner: Backend maintainers.

  • T0 complete.

Create acceptance-matrix.md beside this plan, with one row per FR-001–FR-111 identifier actually present and SC-001–SC-013. Each row records scope, owning task, required test/observable result, decision reference, and evidence status. Resolve the known specification drift in place: backend enumeration/AF/ADK assumptions, openai: naming, Azure client construction, effort max → xhigh, hooks, hosted-tool count, and tracing suppression. Preserve the original requirement identifiers and record why each changed requirement was superseded. Map P3 and sandbox criteria to explicit deferrals instead of silently deleting their success criteria. Give each deferred item a debt/spec link, owner, and observable exit criterion; H-008 already covers final SK removal.

Gate: Every requirement has a destination. No mandatory in-scope behavior disappears into a generic “follow-up.” Run make harness-check; review the matrix against the complete spec and all six reconciled records.

docs.title: T1 — Prove and correct fallback and tracing behavior
docs.text:
Dependencies: T0. Owner: Backend/observability maintainers. Old tasks: F4, H1.

  • T1 complete (local gates; live provider/dashboard evidence is T10).

Inspect openai_agents_fallback.py, openai_agents_backend.py, and openai_agents_tracing.py under src/holodeck/lib/backends/. Exercise fallback through the SDK Runner, including retry exhaustion, retryable/non-retryable errors, streaming before/after the first event, and both-attempt traces. Define one bounded retry order and correct the wrapper if its internal catch bypasses that order. Test OpenAI/Azure and provider-upload overrides with observability enabled and disabled, repeated initialization, and mixed-provider initialization in both orders. Resolve SDK process-global processor ownership so configuration isolation is explicit and safe. Do not fix mixed-provider behavior by silently ignoring later agents.

Gate: Deterministic Runner-level tests demonstrate ordering, no duplicate streamed output, and provider-upload suppression without starving permitted OTel spans. Extend existing fallback/backend/tracing tests. Record the process-global tracing policy in the spec and guide.

Result (2026-09-06): Decisions D13 (per-backend tracing-policy router owning the SDK processor list) and D14 (primary client retries, then one fallback, no Runner repeat) recorded in the spec; guides and changelog updated. The first-initialization flag was replaced: register_tracing_policy / unregister_tracing_policy and active_tracing_policy in openai_agents_tracing.py; every run tags RunConfig.trace_metadata["holodeck.tracing_policy"]. Evidence E5 in the matrix.

docs.title: T2 — Complete LiteLLM inference acceptance
docs.text:
Dependencies: T0. Owner: Retrieval/observability maintainers. Old tasks: LiteLLM T2/T3/T6/T8; H-009.

  • T2 complete (local gates; live three-provider and collector evidence is T10).

Resolve the shared embedding service versus per-tool dimensions contract in tool_initializer.py and litellm_support.py. Test factory-to-provider dimension forwarding and mismatch handling, including tools with different configured dimensions. Choose and document the provider-error boundary, then test propagation or wrapping without losing useful causes. Resolve semantic-convention stability against the installed integration. Verify emitted embedding/chat spans through an in-memory exporter, including token attributes, redaction, and capture disabled. Preserve LLMContextGenerator retry, truncation, and concurrency behavior and the Claude context-generator selection path.

Gate: Focused tests cover the resolved contracts. T10 supplies the live grounded/query and contextual-ingest evidence required to close H-009. No rollback flag or SK inference path is reintroduced.

Result (2026-09-06): Decision D15 recorded in the spec: per-tool embedding_dimensions builds a dedicated LiteLLMEmbeddingService that sends dimensions to the provider; EmbeddingServiceError (cause chained) is the provider-error boundary and both tools propagate it instead of storing placeholder vectors; semantic conventions are not pinned, the default LiteLLM shape is documented, and the opt-in is documented and tested. LLMContextGenerator and Claude context-generator selection are unchanged. Guides, changelog, and the LiteLLM plan record updated. Evidence E6 in the matrix.

docs.title: T3 — Deliver subagents, skill tools, and handoff events
docs.text:
Dependencies: T0. Owner: Backend/model maintainers. Old tasks: D1–D3.

  • T3 complete (local gates; live handoff and skill routes verified on Azure OpenAI, E8; the plain OpenAI run remains T10).

Add validated openai.agents configuration, SDK subagent construction, parent-tool inheritance, explicit tool restrictions, model inheritance, and Claude-literal rejection. Add SkillTool to the tool union, with inline and SKILL.md forms, following the full plan's contracts. Emit handoff/parent-link events through the existing backend and AG-UI contracts. Preserve ordinary tool start/end/error events as well as thinking events. Record how the recommended handoff prefix and its opt-out work. Define the portable setting_sources warning required by FR-071.

Gate: Unit and session integration tests prove tool/model inheritance, restricted skills, invalid configuration, and ordered AG-UI events. Generate schemas and verify schema synchronization. Add bounded fixture-based handoff tests; T10 covers a live handoff.

Result (2026-09-06): Decision D16 recorded in the spec: openai.agents entries (OpenAISubagentSpec) and the net-new SkillTool (type: skill, inline or SKILL.md, YAML-only allowed_tools) become SDK handoff-target agents built from the parent's built tool surface by openai_agents_subagents.py (inherit-all, explicit restriction by config name, unknown/disallowed names fail load, inherit model reuse, Claude literals rejected at config load, prefix once with opt-out, skills verbatim). openai_agents_events.py maps SDK run items and stream events onto the existing ToolEvent contract (start/end/parent_link/subagent_message/thinking), the session exposes tool_events, and handoffs are recorded in ExecutionResult. FR-071 logs setting_sources is a Claude-only concept; ignored on openai. once per load. Schema regenerated. sample/openai-agents-full/ is a runnable agent exercising every shipped backend surface (function, RAG, MCP, subagents, skills, disallowed tools, effort, budget, fallback, tracing, tests). Live run on 2026-09-06 (Azure OpenAI gpt-5-mini, agent.azure.yaml): 7/7 cases pass across five consecutive runs, in-memory and with both RAG tools on Qdrant; see E8 in the matrix for the three harness bugs it exposed and fixed on the same branch. Guides (OpenAI backend, Tools), examples index, changelog, and the full plan updated. Evidence E7 in the matrix.

docs.title: T4 — Deliver hosted tools and safety gates
docs.text:

Add validated hosted-tool configuration and the five factories retained by the full plan. Cover web search, file search, code interpreter, image generation, and hosted MCP. docs.title: T5 — Implement default credential boundaries

Attach default output redaction to HoloDeck-built tools and preserve the recorded opt-out warnings. Test the model-visible result and exported spans using synthetic credential-shaped values, without using real credentials. Implement child-process environment scrubbing for HoloDeck-managed MCP and function subprocess paths, with explicit opt-out behavior. Do not mutate the process-wide environment during concurrent requests. Document the limits for arbitrary Python tools that spawn children outside managed paths. Keep hosted and MCP-server guardrail limitations visible and distinguish them from OTel redaction.

docs.title: T6 — Complete YAML hooks and rejection semantics
docs.text:
Dependencies: T3, T4, T5. Owner: Backend/model maintainers. Old tasks: E1–E2.

  • T6 complete.

Implement validated hook configuration and the event/action mappings in the full plan. Cover log/notify/script observation, session start, stop, tool success/failure, and unreachable matchers. Run internal tracking/redaction before user hooks and preserve declaration order and terminal-action behavior. Function-tool rejection must continue the run with the rejection result; input rejection must abort with the specified message. Reject unsupported MCP-server guardrail configuration at load. Implement the agreed hosted-MCP rejection path without introducing the deferred interactive approval loop. Treat modify as the documented inert warning, not silent mutation.

Gate: Tests cover each event/action pairing, failure wrappers, ordering, script lifecycle, function/input rejection, hosted rejection, and unsupported MCP configuration. Ensure hook scripts use the credential boundary from T5. Generate and validate schemas.

docs.title: T7 — Complete serving lifecycle and capacity
docs.text:
Dependencies: T0, T1; final integration after T3–T6. Owner: Serving/backend maintainers. Old task: I1.

Extend src/holodeck/serve/server.py and shared validation for OpenAI/Azure startup credential preflight, readiness, and configuration echo. Implement active-turn capacity with explicit override or the D11 formula: full finite cgroup MiB divided by the configured estimate (default 100), with an assumed 1024-MiB fallback and an actionable error below one. Do not subtract Claude's subprocess reserve. Idle sessions must not consume active-turn slots. Release slots on success, error, timeout, cancellation, disconnect, and streaming-generator closure. Return the agreed 429 problem response and Retry-After; verify tool-init endpoints and non-init-tool errors.

docs.title: T10 — Establish complete acceptance evidence
docs.text:
Dependencies: T1–T9 implementation and local gates ready; upstream live-acceptance checkboxes can remain open. Owner: Backend maintainers coordinating service owners. Old tasks: K2, all open checkpoints.

  • T10 complete.

docs.title: T11 — Close and archive feature records
docs.text:
Dependencies: T10. Owner: Backend/harness maintainers. Old task: K checkpoint and historical plan closure.

Run final repository checks listed below on the assembled candidate and resolve introduced failures. Review the final diff, acceptance matrix, and actual runtime scope together. docs.title: Dependencies and suggested PR boundaries
docs.text:
T0 precedes implementation. T1, T2, T3, and T4 can proceed independently after that contract is settled. T5 starts after T1 and integrates T3 adapters. T6 follows T3–T5. T7 can develop in parallel with tool work, then integrates it. T8 follows T7. T9 prepares fixtures early and completes after runtime behavior stabilizes. T10 and T11 are final gates.

Prefer one reviewable PR per task, splitting schema/adapters from integration only when each intermediate change remains usable. A task stays open until all dependent acceptance is satisfied. Merge order follows the dependencies above. For delegated work, assign disjoint files. Sequence edits to shared models, the selector, backend initialization, schemas, and tests.

docs.title: Verification commands and evidence format
docs.text:
For each Python change, run focused Black, Ruff, MyPy, and relevant pytest tests through uv run. Run pytest with -n auto. Use the existing quality map to select consumers of shared contracts. After model changes, run make schema and make schema-check. At final integration, preserve CI/pre-commit requirements and run:

uv run pre-commit run --all-files
uv run pytest -n auto --cov --cov-branch --cov-report=xml
make security
make schema-check
make harness-check
uv run mkdocs build --strict

Keep live service tests separately identifiable. Record skips and unavailable services, rather than treating a green summary as complete live acceptance. Do not rerun broad suites after they pass unless the candidate changes or a new concern warrants it.

Each task records: commit/configuration identity, changed behavior, command, result/count, artifact reference, and remaining limitation. Do not store credentials or raw sensitive traces in the evidence.

docs.title: Progress and decisions
docs.text:
• 2026-09-06: Created this execution plan from the six reconciled records. No implementation tasks were completed by plan creation.
  • The earlier audit recorded 324 focused test passes plus harness and strict MkDocs passes. Those results cover the audited baseline only.
  • T0 records decisions D01–D12 and all 69 requirement dispositions in the spec/matrix. Deferred scope has owners and observable exit criteria in H-008 and H-011–H-022; H-009 remains mandatory migration acceptance.
  • /ready remains canonical but must gain prerequisite/tool-state gating and HTTP 503 semantics. D11 corrects the invalid ACA 1-CPU / 1-GiB proposal to supported 1-CPU / 2-GiB while preserving the local ten-turn target and adding the cloud twenty-turn gate.
  • 2026-09-06 (T1): the fallback wrapper's internal catch was found to sit inside the SDK Runner's retry loop, so runner-managed retries would repeat the primary-then-fallback pair; D14 pins the order to the OpenAI client's provider-managed retries followed by one fallback, with HoloDeck never enabling ModelSettings.retry. The process-global mirror flag silently skipped later agents (an Azure agent after an OpenAI agent inherited upload; observability-disabled Azure still uploaded); D13 replaces it with a router that applies each backend's policy per trace. Only traces and spans with no HoloDeck identity keep SDK default behaviour; events for a torn-down backend are dropped immediately. An independent Codex review of the first T1 draft reproduced escapes across two rounds (span under a caller-owned outer trace started before the run, span finished outside its scope or after its trace ended or after trace-map eviction, in-flight trace after unregister) and the SDK's conversation_locked compatibility retry; span identity is now pinned at span start, withdrawal is immediate, and the retry bound is documented in D14, each with regression tests. Codex's reproduction script yields zero uploads on the committed revision.

docs.text:
Plan-only validation: make harness-check and git diff --check passed on 2026-09-06. Independent coverage review identified a live-acceptance dependency cycle and missing explicit LiteLLM live checks. Both were corrected. The review covered task scope, dependencies, authorization boundaries, and completion criteria. T0 verification on 2026-09-06: all original 56 FR and 13 SC identifiers preserved exactly; 69 matrix rows have every required field. All 181 local fragment links across the spec and active records resolve. make harness-check, git diff --check, and uv run mkdocs build --strict passed. Independent contract review covered the full spec and six reconciled records; its two matrix gaps (first-event fallback boundary and trace run/capture identity) were corrected.

T1 verification on 2026-09-06: uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/backends tests/unit/serve tests/integration/test_multi_turn_dual_backend.py -n auto -q — 946 passed (6 new Runner-level fallback tests, 23 router tests, 18 policy/lifecycle/capture tests); Black, Ruff, and MyPy clean on the three changed source modules; make harness-check and uv run mkdocs build --strict passed. Test files remain outside the repository's MyPy gate. Remaining T1 limitation: real OpenAI dashboard and collector observation for FR-100–FR-102/SC-011 and live 429 fallback behaviour are T10 evidence.

T2 verification on 2026-09-06: uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/test_litellm_support.py tests/unit/lib/test_tool_initializer.py tests/unit/test_vectorstore_tool.py tests/unit/tools tests/unit/lib/backends/test_otel_redaction.py tests/unit/lib/observability tests/unit/lib/test_llm_context_generator.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_claude_backend.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_tracing.py tests/integration/test_multi_turn_dual_backend.py -n auto -q — 699 passed (7 dimension/boundary initializer tests, 4 shim boundary tests, 9 exporter-level LiteLLM span tests, tool propagation and failure-telemetry redaction tests); independent adversarial review found six issues (Azure deployment-alias dimensions guard, unredacted error.*/exception-event telemetry, LiteLLM callback_list fixture leak, two documentation claims, an untyped helper), all fixed before commit; tests/integration/test_litellm_rag_integration.py skipped without credentials (8 skipped); Black, Ruff, and MyPy clean on the six changed source modules; make harness-check and uv run mkdocs build --strict passed.

T3 verification on 2026-09-06: uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_subagents.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_events.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_backend.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_tool_adapters.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_validators.py tests/unit/models/test_skill_tool.py tests/unit/models/test_openai_config.py tests/unit/models/test_agent.py tests/unit/lib/test_skills.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_claude_backend.py tests/unit/chat tests/unit/serve -n auto -q — see the recorded count below; make schema and make schema-check pass; Black, Ruff, and MyPy clean on the changed source modules; make harness-check and uv run mkdocs build --strict passed. Remaining T2 limitation: live OpenAI/Azure/Ollama grounded ingest/query, contextual ingest, and collector observation are T10 evidence.

T3 live follow-up on 2026-09-06 (same branch, PR #380): cd sample/openai-agents-full && uv run holodeck test run agent.azure.yaml against Azure OpenAI (gpt-5-mini deployment, text-embedding-3-small) — 7/7 passed on four consecutive runs; handoff to researcher, handoff to analyst with inherited tools, and skill route exercised real handoffs with inherited and restricted tools (analyst called get_inventory + reserve_stock after transfer_to_analyst; researcher and summarise skill called knowledge_base_search). The run exposed and fixed three harness defects: (1) retrieval_context never built on this backend because the test runner matched only SK/Claude tool names — faithfulness and contextual_* were silently skipped (d21a14c; faithfulness now scores 1.0 on the four retrieval cases); (2) vectorstore ingest failed on Qdrant with 400 Bad Request (readable point IDs) and search failed on qdrant-client 1.18 (AsyncQdrantClient.search removed) — fixed with UUIDv5 IDs and a query_points shim (5879801, 3bdecb0; H-010 tracks structured-key preservation); (3) the loader has no ${VAR:-default} syntax, so sample env references were literal. Sample-level fixes: G-Eval compares with expected_output; subagent prompts assert ownership of the request at low reasoning effort. Independent adversarial review of the Qdrant fix found two issues (native UUID IDs re-hashed; structured business key lost), both fixed. Plain provider: openai run still pending (no credits on the available key) and remains T10 with the OpenAI dashboard/collector checks.

Serve follow-up on 2026-09-06 (E9, same branch): holodeck serve with the same sample validated by raw AG-UI SSE requests and a CopilotKit browser flow. It exposed a serve defect on this backend — turn 2 on a thread returned empty because the backend and its stdio MCP servers were initialised in turn 1's HTTP request task — fixed by running every serve session's backend inside its actor task and surfacing is_error results in the chat executor. This is the validation loop now recorded in AGENTS.md: live sample run, raw serve requests, then user-driven CopilotKit validation.

Apart from the Azure OpenAI sample run above, live-provider, container, and cloud acceptance have not run under this plan. Access to provider credentials, a collector, Docker, and an authorized ACA target will be needed for the corresponding T10 evidence.

docs.title: Reading the matrix
docs.text: There are 56 functional requirements and 13 success criteria: one row for each identifier actually declared in the spec. Retained preserves the requirement. Revised replaces a superseded assumption with the cited decision; the replacement still requires verification. Deferred preserves a requirement outside retained 035 scope, with a durable debt destination and future acceptance. No runtime row is certified complete by this documentation task. Update evidence only from named tests or recorded observations. Task owners are defined in the completion plan; deferred owners and exit criteria are defined in the linked debt entries. T10 supplies candidate/live acceptance. T11 checks coverage and final status across all retained rows.

docs.text:
• E1: The reconciliation records 128 focused backend/adapter/selector tests passing on the audited baseline. Files: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_backend.py, test_openai_agents_tool_adapters.py, and test_selector.py.
  • E2: The same report records 196 tests covering LiteLLM, tool initialization, context generation, tracing, output, cost, fallback, MCP, permissions, and OTel redaction. These are focused baseline tests, not full/live acceptance.
  • E3: src/holodeck/models/openai_config.py, models/agent.py, lib/backends/validators.py, and their model/validator tests were inspected. Configuration presence does not prove serve enforcement.
  • E5 (T1, 2026-09-06): Runner-level fallback acceptance in tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_fallback_runner.py (6 tests) drives the real SDK Runner over real OpenAIResponsesModel instances against an in-process httpx.MockTransport: primary client retries exhaust (1 + max_retries requests) before one fallback attempt; no third attempt after a fallback failure; non-retryable 401 never reaches the fallback; streamed fallback before response.created with deltas delivered once; no restart after the first event; the SDK conversation_locked compatibility re-run bounded to four primary/fallback pairs; both response spans (first with error) reach the OTel mirror under one trace via the router. Tracing-policy router acceptance in test_openai_agents_tracing.py (TestTraceRouter*, 23 tests) and test_openai_agents_backend.py (TestTracingPolicyFor, TestBackendTracingPolicyLifecycle, TestRunConfigCapturePolicy, 18 tests) covers the routing matrix, mixed providers in both orders, repeated registration, observability-disabled Azure, spans under a caller-owned outer trace opened before the run, spans finished outside their scope, after trace end, or after trace-map eviction, immediate withdrawal of in-flight traces, bounded trace map, untagged traces, per-run tagging, teardown withdrawal, and the env-default capture override. Command: uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/backends tests/unit/serve tests/integration/test_multi_turn_dual_backend.py -n auto -q — 946 passed at the T1 revision (later reruns are listed in the completion plan). Live dashboard/collector observation remains T10.
  • E6 (T2, 2026-09-06): LiteLLM inference contracts (D15). tests/unit/lib/test_tool_initializer.py::TestEmbeddingDimensionsForwarding (7 tests) proves factory-to-provider dimension forwarding into litellm.aembedding, distinct services for tools with different embedding_dimensions, one shared service otherwise, single-tool init forwarding, a provider size mismatch aborting init with the ValueError cause, and a provider failure aborting init with EmbeddingServiceError → original exception chained. tests/unit/lib/test_litellm_support.py::TestEmbeddingServiceErrorBoundary (4 tests) pins the boundary; vectorstore/hierarchical tool tests pin propagation (no placeholder fallback with a service). tests/unit/lib/observability/test_litellm_spans.py (9 tests) reads real embedding and LLMContextGenerator chat spans from an in-memory exporter behind RedactingSpanProcessor: default span shape and token attributes, no content and no raw-response span under NO_CONTENT, redacted prompt/completion/raw payload under SPAN_ONLY, the OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental shape with and without capture (no raw span under the opt-in), and a provider failure span whose error.* attributes and exception event carry no credential. test_otel_redaction.py pins the raw-response, error.*, and event scrubbing. TestLiteLLMEmbeddingService pins the Azure deployment-alias allowed_openai_params allow-list for dimensions. Existing test_llm_context_generator.py retry/truncation/concurrency and TestResolveContextGenerator Claude-selection tests pass unchanged. Command: uv run pytest tests/unit/lib/test_litellm_support.py tests/unit/lib/test_tool_initializer.py tests/unit/test_vectorstore_tool.py tests/unit/tools tests/unit/lib/backends/test_otel_redaction.py tests/unit/lib/observability tests/unit/lib/test_llm_context_generator.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_claude_backend.py tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_tracing.py tests/integration/test_multi_turn_dual_backend.py -n auto -q — 699 passed after an independent adversarial review (six findings: Azure alias dimensions guard, unredacted failure telemetry, LiteLLM callback_list fixture leak, token-row wording, opt-in raw-span claim, untyped helper — all fixed). Live OpenAI/Azure/Ollama grounded and contextual ingest and collector observation remain T10.
  • E7 (T3, 2026-09-06): Subagents, skills, and handoff events (D16). tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_subagents.py (25 tests) builds real SDK Agent/FunctionTool objects and pins: three subagents become three handoffs in order with prefixed instructions and descriptions; tools: null inherits the parent's tools and MCP servers (same SDK objects); explicit lists restrict by config name, can grant an MCP server, an empty list grants nothing, unknown or disallowed names raise ConfigError naming the entry; inherit/omitted reuse the parent model object and explicit ids go through the provider resolver; inline and SKILL.md skills yield identical instructions, description, tools, and model; skills carry no prefix, get no tools without allowed_tools, are dropped when disallowed, and collide-fail against openai.agents keys. tests/unit/models/test_skill_tool.py (19 tests) and tests/unit/lib/test_skills.py (13 tests) pin SkillTool validation (naming, inline/path exclusivity, frontmatter fallback, base-dir resolution, missing directory/file/field failures) and the allowed_tools cross-check on Agent. tests/unit/models/test_openai_config.py::TestOpenAISubagentSpec (13 tests) pins prompt/prompt_file rules and Claude-literal rejection. tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_events.py (10 tests) pins the ToolEvent mapping and drives the real SDK Runner through OpenAIAgentsSession with a scripted model (entry → transfer_to_researcher → inherited lookup → answer): both send_streaming and send deliver start/end(transfer_to_researcher), subagent_message, start/parent_link/end(lookup), subagent_message in that order, and ExecutionResult records the handoff call and handoff:researcher result. test_openai_agents_backend.py::TestHandoffWiring/TestResolveSubagentModel pin initialize() passing handoffs to the SDK agent, unknown subagent tools failing initialize, and the Azure deployment model resolver. test_validators.py::TestSettingSourcesWarning pins FR-071. Schema regenerated (make schema, make schema-check). An independent adversarial review found ten issues, all fixed before commit: SDK tool-name collisions (kb + kb_search) now fail load; load_agent_yaml sets agent_base_dir before validation (also fixes stale-context claude.agents.prompt_file resolution); handoff targets carry the parent's output_type and model settings; normalised transfer_to_ name collisions fail load; indented --- inside SKILL.md block scalars is content; the handoff end is deferred to run completion so the panel nests children; a mid-stream failure closes open calls with error; the event queue is bounded; FR-071 logs once per load. sample/openai-agents-full exercises every surface (loads and builds five handoff targets offline); its live run is E8.
  • E4: src/holodeck/serve/server.py, serve/tool_init_manager.py, deploy/deployers/azure_containerapps.py, models/deployment.py, and existing serve/deploy tests were inspected. Current /ready only proves lifecycle state and always returns 200. ACA probes already use /ready.

Paths in this catalog are repository-relative. Proposed additional tests belong to the corresponding T1–T10 tasks, not fictitious existing files. - E8 (T3 live follow-up, 2026-09-06): sample/openai-agents-full/agent.azure.yaml run against Azure OpenAI (gpt-5-mini deployment, text-embedding-3-small embeddings, MCP filesystem server over npx, knowledge_base and the handbook hierarchical index on Qdrant 1.17, collections documents_dim512 and hierarchical_docs_handbook_dim1536): 7/7 test cases pass on five consecutive runs (holodeck test run). Live handoffs: transfer_to_researcher → knowledge_base_search/handbook_search (restricted tools), transfer_to_analyst → get_inventory + reserve_stock (inherited tools), transfer_to_summarise (inline skill) → knowledge_base_search; purge_inventory never offered. Evaluators: G-Eval against expected_output on all cases and faithfulness (RAG) scoring 1.0 on the four retrieval cases and skipped on the rest. Defects found and fixed on the same branch: the test runner did not recognise OpenAI-backend tool names (<name>_search) when building retrieval_context, so RAG metrics were silently skipped on openai/azure_openai (tests/unit/lib/test_runner/test_executor.py now pins all three naming schemes); vectorstore on Qdrant failed ingest (400, non-UUID point IDs) and search (AsyncQdrantClient.search removed in qdrant-client 1.13+) — deterministic UUIDv5 IDs with native UUID/int IDs preserved, plus a query_points shim in create_qdrant_client (tests/unit/tools/test_vectorstore_source_keys.py::TestQdrantRecordIds, tests/unit/lib/test_vector_store.py::TestCreateQdrantClientSearchCompat; H-010 tracks structured business-key preservation). Not covered: plain provider: openai (no credits on the available key), OpenAI dashboard trace upload, collector observation — T10. - E9 (T3 serve follow-up, 2026-09-06): holodeck serve sample/openai-agents-full/agent.azure.yaml --port 8765 validated with raw AG-UI SSE requests (curl -N POST /awp, two threads, two turns each) and then a CopilotKit browser flow (sample/copilotkit, HOLODECK_BACKEND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/awp, user-driven plus scripted turns). Events observed in order: RUN_STARTED, REASONING_*, TOOL_CALL_START(transfer_to_analyst) with nested get_inventory/reserve_stock (parentMessageId chain), TOOL_CALL_RESULT "Handoff to 'analyst' completed.", TEXT_MESSAGE_*, RUN_FINISHED; the researcher thread showed transfer_to_researcher → handbook_search/knowledge_base_search. Defect found and fixed: turn 2 on any thread returned an empty reply with RUN_FINISHED — the backend (and its stdio MCP servers) was initialised in turn 1's HTTP request task, whose anyio streams died with it (ClosedResourceError on list_tools), and the chat executor ignored the is_error result. Fixes: serve enables the task-bound actor for every provider and the actor now builds, prepares, closes, and tears the backend down inside its own task (tests/unit/agent/test_executor_coverage.py::TestTaskBoundSessionOwnership); execute_turn raises BackendSessionError on content-less error results and returns partial content otherwise (TestExecuteTurnErrorResults); the backend logs swallowed run failures. After the fix: four requests, zero errors, follow-up turns answered from session history (Reservation ID: R-1000, Bay H.). CopilotKit rendered the reasoning block and the three nested tool cards as Complete. AG-UI HTTP acceptance for FR-006 is therefore live on Azure; REST protocol and holodeck deploy remain T7/T10.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The MVP proved one vertical slice: a provider: openai / azure_openai agent runs the OpenAI Agents SDK Runner loop, calls Python function tools, and streams under holodeck chat, with default routing flipped and the SK agent path removed. This plan delivers the rest of the backend's parity surface:

  • the remaining HoloDeck tool types: vectorstore, hierarchical_document, MCP — plus skill tools, whose SkillTool model is net-new (the spec presumes it exists; it does not — see reconciliations);
  • subagents (handoffs) and YAML hooks;
  • the spec-026 config mappings (effort, max_budget_usd, fallback_model, disallowed_tools);
  • hosted tools (type: hosted);
  • structured output + thinking parity (FR-004);
  • RunConfig plumbing (trace sensitivity, workflow naming);
  • tracing dual-write;
  • serve/deploy parity and the spec-034 hardening phases P1a/P1b/P2a/P2b.

It is organised as vertical, feature-complete slices (model + adapter + backend wiring + tests per slice) so each phase leaves holodeck chat/test/serve working.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
Confirmed with user 2026-06-09 (1–4) and 2026-06-10 (3 revised; 5–7 added after the SDK review):

  1. Namespacing → a new top-level openai: block. Hooks, subagents, permissions, and all backend knobs for this backend live under openai: (sibling to claude:). claude.hooks / claude.agents stay Claude-only — they are NOT read by this backend. Cross-backend portability is achieved by declaring the relevant block per backend, not by sharing claude.*. (This supersedes spec Open Question 1 — neither option (a) "reuse claude.*" nor the openai_agents: name; the block is literally openai:.)
  2. P3 hardened profile (Envoy sidecar, deployment.security_profile, egress allowlist, base-URL rewriting) → deferred to a separate cross-backend spec. It exists for no backend today (Claude included); building it here would be net-new shared infra with backend-specific divergence. FR-090…FR-093 are out of this plan. P1a/P1b/P2a/P2b stay in.
  3. US8 sandbox mode (agent_mode: sandbox) → deferred to a follow-up spec, as a scoping decision. (Rationale corrected 2026-06-10: the first draft claimed UnixLocalSandboxClient does not exist in 0.17.4 — that is false; it exists at agents.sandbox.sandboxes.unix_local and imports on non-Windows platforms.) The honest reason for deferral: sandbox mode is a large, security-sensitive surface (manifests, sandbox runtimes, lifecycle management) that deserves its own spec and threat model rather than riding along in a parity plan. FR-094…FR-099 are out of this plan. The openai.i_understand_this_is_unsafe gate still ships (it gates CodeInterpreterTool).
  4. Hosted tools allowed on Azure, runtime-gated. The MVP put Azure on the Responses API (/openai/v1), so the spec's blanket config-load block (US5 scenario 3) is relaxed: hosted tools are accepted on azure_openai; if a specific tool isn't available on the resource, the SDK surfaces a runtime error that HoloDeck propagates verbatim with a clear hint. (The spec's risk table cites FR-091 for this block — a mis-citation; FR-091 is the P3 egress-allowlist FR, deferred under Decision 2.)
  5. reject + credential redaction → native per-tool guardrails, scoped to HoloDeck-built tools. The SDK's FunctionTool.tool_input_guardrails / tool_output_guardrails (ToolGuardrailFunctionOutput.reject_content(message)) are the implementation for hook reject actions and for default credential redaction — synchronous, message-bearing, run continues. Coverage is function/vectorstore/hier-doc/skill tools only: hosted tools execute server-side, and MCP-server tools become SDK-built FunctionTools HoloDeck never touches (see reconciliations). The first draft's needs_approval synthesis is dropped: needs_approval interrupts the run (RunState.approve()/.reject() + re-run), which is a human-in-the-loop feature, not an auto-reject — deferred to a follow-up spec if wanted.
  6. modify hook action stays inert in v1 (load warning, no runtime effect) to keep hook semantics symmetric with the Claude backend. Note for later: SDK output guardrails can replace the model-visible tool output, so modify-on-output is implementable when both backends are ready to support it.
  7. ComputerTool rejected at config load, computer-use deferred. ComputerTool requires a live Python Computer/AsyncComputer implementation (tool.py — required computer: field); it cannot be constructed from YAML params. type: hosted, name: ComputerTool fails load with a clear "requires a computer harness — not yet supported" error. Computer-use gets its own follow-up spec (likely alongside sandbox).

docs.title: Spec ↔ reality reconciliations (verified against installed 0.17.4 source + this repo)
docs.text:
These differ from the spec text and/or earlier drafts; the plan follows reality:

  • No Backend enum / no backend: override / no agent_framework backend exist. Routing is purely by model.provider in BackendSelector (src/holodeck/lib/backends/selector.py), and the openai/azure_openai → openai_agents flip already shipped in the MVP. → FR-001 and FR-007 are already satisfied; US1 scenario 4 (explicit AF opt-out) is dropped (no AF backend in this repo).
  • SkillTool does not exist in the codebase. The spec (line 37, FR-070, SC-001) presumes an "existing HoloDeck SkillTool (spec 023)", but ToolUnion (models/tool.py) is VectorstoreTool | FunctionTool | MCPTool | PromptTool | HierarchicalDocumentToolConfig. D2 therefore creates the SkillTool model (+ schema regen) before translating it.
  • PromptTool (type: prompt) has no runtime adapter in any backend — it is defined in models/tool.py and referenced nowhere else in src/. The spec's tool list excludes it. This plan keeps it out of scope but downgrades the openai adapter's unsupported-type ConfigError for prompt to a skip-with-warning (B1), so switching providers on an agent that declares one matches the de-facto status quo instead of hard-failing.
  • MCP-server tools are SDK-built FunctionTools HoloDeck never sees. agents/mcp/util.py (to_function_tool) converts each MCP tool to a FunctionTool inside the SDK, per run, with tool_input_guardrails=None / tool_output_guardrails=None. HoloDeck only passes Agent(mcp_servers=[...]). Consequence: guardrail-based reject (E2), credential redaction (J1), and adapter-wrapper failure detection (E1) cannot cover MCP tools in v1 — documented per task and in the K3 matrix.
  • Directly constructed FunctionTools have no default failure handling. The SDK's error-string-to-model behavior lives in the function_tool factory's failure-handling invoker (tool.py _build_wrapped_function_tool); HoloDeck constructs FunctionTool directly, so an uncaught tool exception propagates and fails the whole run (run_internal/tool_execution.py → UserError). E1's adapter wrapper must catch exceptions itself, fire PostToolUseFailure, and return an error string to the model (mirroring the factory's default).
  • Run-level InputGuardrail is tripwire-only. GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered) halts execution via InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered (guardrail.py, run_internal/guardrails.py) — there is no message-and-continue option at the run-input level. Input-matched reject hooks therefore abort the turn (HoloDeck catches the exception and surfaces the configured message); only tool-matched rejects continue the run.
  • The shipped MVP already calls set_tracing_disabled(True) on the Azure path (openai_agents_backend.py _build_model) — which makes the trace provider return NoOpTrace/NoOpSpan (tracing/provider.py) and would starve the H1 OTel mirror. H1 removes that call; A2's preflight refactor keeps _build_model's credential checks side-effect-free (no set_tracing_disabled / set_default_openai_key during validation).
  • MCPServerStdio / MCPServerSse / MCPServerStreamableHttp live under agents.mcp.*, not at the agents top level. Confirmed present in 0.17.4, plus create_static_tool_filter.
  • needs_approval is an interrupt, not a synchronous reject (tool.py: "the run will be interrupted and the tool call will need to be approved using RunState.approve() or rejected using RunState.reject()"). Auto-reject maps to tool_input_guardrails instead (Decision 5). This also covers the MCP server classes' require_approval (it resolves into the generated tool's needs_approval) — so MCP reject cannot be implemented that way without HITL.
  • on_tool_start/on_tool_end fire for local tools only (lifecycle docstrings; invocation sites are in run_internal/tool_execution.py / tool_actions.py). Hosted tools execute server-side and never trigger AgentHooks/RunHooks tool events or guardrails.
  • ReasoningEffort accepts "none" | "minimal" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" in the installed client. Spec FR-030/031's "clamp max to high" was written against an older value set; this plan maps max → "xhigh" (documented deviation).
  • Reasoning summaries must be requested. ReasoningItems carry summaries only when Reasoning(summary=...) is set on the request; effort alone yields empty summaries. F5 sets summary="auto" for reasoning models so thinking has content.
  • AgentOutputSchemaBase is abstract and the SDK's only concrete implementation (AgentOutputSchema) requires a Python type. JSON-schema-dict-driven output (HoloDeck's response_format) needs a small HoloDeck subclass (F5 writes it).
  • RunConfig.trace_include_sensitive_data defaults to True (env-derived), uploading raw tool inputs/outputs with provider traces. A security-focused plan must set it explicitly (Task A3 ties it to observability.traces.capture_content).
  • CodeInterpreterTool / ImageGenerationTool / HostedMCPTool require structured tool_config objects (openai-types CodeInterpreter / ImageGeneration / Mcp), not flat kwargs — G1 factories build the nested objects from YAML params.
  • HostedMCPTool approval requires require_approval in its Mcp tool_config — the on_approval_request callback only fires for tools the provider was told need approval. E2's hosted-MCP reject mapping must set both halves.
  • The SDK has runner-managed retry (ModelSettings.retry: ModelRetrySettings(max_retries, backoff, policy)) that fires on the same 429/5xx class as F4's fallback — F4 must define the ordering (retries exhaust first, then fallback).
  • FR-084 reinterpreted. The FR says function tools' needs_approval gates are never weakened; v1 ships no needs_approval at all (Decision 5), so the FR is satisfied vacuously, and the enforced invariant becomes: default guardrail gates (J1 redaction, E2 rejects) are never weakened by hosted-tool or permission config.
  • RedactingSpanProcessor is already backend-agnostic (otel_redaction.py) — P2b OTel redaction (FR-088) needs verification only, no new code.
  • security_profile / Envoy infra does not exist → see Decision 2.

docs.title: Architecture decisions
docs.text:
• One openai: config model (src/holodeck/models/openai_config.py, OpenAIConfig) mirrors the role ClaudeConfig plays for Claude. It carries sizing (max_concurrent_sessions, session_memory_estimate_mib), max_turns, safety (i_understand_this_is_unsafe), hook/redaction opt-outs, permissions, the spec-026 fields (effort, max_budget_usd, fallback_model, disallowed_tools), plus hooks and agents sub-blocks.
  • Lazy import gate preserved. Every import agents / import openai stays inside functions/methods of the openai_agents_* modules (SC-005). Pydantic models in models/openai_config.py never import the SDK.
  • Tool adapters extend the existing build_sdk_tools in openai_agents_tool_adapters.py. At the MVP baseline it raised ConfigError for every non-function type; each phase below removes one type from that error path and returns the right SDK object. Returns become a tuple (tools, mcp_servers, handoffs) so MCP servers and skill/subagent handoffs flow into Agent(...).
  • Reuse the live RAG factories. Vectorstore / hierarchical_document adapters wrap the existing tool .search() callables (same objects the Claude adapter wraps in lib/backends/tool_adapters.py), reusing tool_initializer.create_embedding_service. No new embedding code.
  • One guardrail module (openai_agents_guardrails.py) owns both hook-reject input guardrails (E2) and the default credential-redaction output guardrail (J1) — same mechanism, one attachment point at FunctionTool build time, for HoloDeck-built tools only (see reconciliations for the MCP gap). Observation hooks (log/notify/script) use AgentHooks/RunHooks; failure detection lives in the adapter wrapper.
  • Cost accountant price table = bundled versioned constant + unknown-model warning (spec Open Question 3 → v1). Lives in openai_agents_cost.py.
  • Unit tests mock the SDK (no network, no key); creds-gated integration smokes exercise live Azure.

docs.title: Task E1: openai.hooks model + observation actions + failure path
docs.text: Reconciled status: Pending / acceptance not established. Description: Add hooks to OpenAIConfig (event + matcher + action shape mirroring spec 028). New openai_agents_hooks.py builds AgentHooks/RunHooks from the config: PreToolUse / PostToolUse with log|notify|script → on_tool_start/on_tool_end (observation-only — local tools only, and MCP-server tools are observable here but not wrappable); PostToolUseFailure → HoloDeck's adapter wrapper around the on_invoke callables it builds catches tool exceptions itself, fires the configured action, and returns an error string to the model (directly constructed FunctionTools have no SDK default failure handling — an uncaught exception fails the whole run; see reconciliations). PostToolUseFailure does not fire for MCP-server tools (SDK builds their invokers) — load warning when a failure matcher targets MCP tool names. Stop → on_end; Notification → on_llm_start/on_llm_end; SessionStart → invoked at create_session(). Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Each event fires its log/notify/script action at the mapped lifecycle point (mocked). - [ ] A raising function tool fires PostToolUseFailure and the model receives an error string; the run does not abort. - [ ] Hook chain ordering: internal hooks (tool tracking, redaction) before user hooks; declaration order preserved (FR-051). - [ ] A hook matcher that can only match hosted tools (or a failure matcher on MCP tool names) loads with a "will never fire" warning. Verification: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_hooks.py. Dependencies: A1 Files: src/holodeck/models/openai_config.py, src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_hooks.py, src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_backend.py Scope: M

docs.title: Task E2: reject (→ tool guardrails) + modify (inert)
docs.text: Reconciled status: Pending / acceptance not established. Description: New openai_agents_guardrails.py. Reject mapping by target: - HoloDeck-built function/local tool (function, vectorstore, hier-doc, skill) → attach a tool_input_guardrail returning ToolGuardrailFunctionOutput.reject_content(<configured message>) — synchronous, the run continues, the model sees the rejection message. (The guardrail context exposes tool_name/tool_arguments — sufficient for spec-028 matchers.) - HostedMCPTool → set require_approval for the matched tool names inside the Mcp tool_config and wire on_approval_request to return a rejection with the configured message (both halves required — the callback only fires for tools flagged as needing approval). - MCP-server tools (agents.mcp.*) → fail load with a clear error: HoloDeck cannot attach guardrails (SDK builds those FunctionTools internally), and the server classes' require_approval resolves into needs_approval interrupts — i.e. HITL, excluded by Decision 5. - Other hosted tools (WebSearch/FileSearch/CodeInterpreter/ImageGeneration — server-side, no guardrail path) → fail load with a clear error. - Input-matched rejects → entry-agent InputGuardrail. This is tripwire-only: the turn aborts via InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered; the backend catches it and surfaces the configured message as the turn's error result. Distinct semantics from tool rejects (run does NOT continue) — documented in the K3 matrix. action: modify → load succeeds with a not yet supported on openai_agents warning (inert, Decision 6). Phase ordering note: the function-tool and input paths land with E1/B1; the hosted-tool paths require G1 and are verified at Checkpoint G. Acceptance criteria: - [ ] A reject on a function tool blocks the call via input guardrail; the model receives the configured message; the run continues (no interrupt). - [ ] An input-matched reject aborts the turn with the configured message as the error result. - [ ] A reject on an MCP-server tool fails load with a clear error. - [ ] (After G1) A reject on a HostedMCPTool sets require_approval + rejects via on_approval_request; a reject on WebSearchTool (et al.) fails load. - [ ] A modify action loads with a warning and has no runtime effect. Verification: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_guardrails.py (reject paths), test_openai_agents_hooks.py (modify warning). Dependencies: E1 (function/input/MCP-error paths); G1 (hosted-tool paths only) Files: src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_guardrails.py, src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_hooks.py Scope: M

docs.title: Task H1: OTel-mirroring TracingProcessor + processor-list management
docs.text: Reconciled status: Partial; see reconciled register for remaining acceptance. Description: New openai_agents_tracing.py: a TracingProcessor that mirrors SDK trace events into the OTel pipeline. Remove the MVP's set_tracing_disabled(True) call in _build_model (Azure path) — it makes the provider return NoOpTrace/NoOpSpan and starves every processor, including the mirror. Processor configuration happens once at backend initialize(), before any run emits spans (the default platform exporter is lazily registered and set_trace_processors does not flush what the replaced processor already queued): provider: openai → agents.add_trace_processor(mirror) (default platform.openai.com exporter retained alongside the mirror); provider: azure_openai → agents.set_trace_processors([mirror]) (replaces the default exporter — spans keep flowing, nothing uploads). Add observability.disable_provider_tracing: bool (default False): when true, use set_trace_processors([mirror]) regardless of provider. Sensitive-payload inclusion in uploaded traces is governed by A3 (trace_include_sensitive_data). Verify RedactingSpanProcessor scrubs the mirrored spans (FR-088 — expected no code). Acceptance criteria: - [ ] The set_tracing_disabled(True) call is gone; Azure runs deliver spans to the mirror (regression test against the NoOp failure mode). - [ ] provider: openai → OTel mirror receives spans AND upload retained (unless override). - [ ] provider: azure_openai → OTel mirror receives spans; no default exporter registered. - [ ] disable_provider_tracing: true suppresses upload for either provider — mirror still receives spans. - [ ] A credential-shaped tool.output.* span attribute is redacted before export. Verification: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_tracing.py. Dependencies: A1, A3 Files: src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_tracing.py, src/holodeck/models/observability.py, openai_agents_backend.py Scope: M

docs.title: Phase I — Serve / deploy parity + P1a / P2a hardening (US2 / US6)
Task I1: Serve active-turn cap, 429, readiness, config echo
docs.text: Reconciled status: Pending / acceptance not established. Description: In serve/server.py, derive an active-turn semaphore for openai_agents from openai.max_concurrent_sessions (explicit) or floor(memory_mib / session_memory_estimate_mib) (default 100). Overflow → 429 + Retry-After + problem+json type: …/session-cap-exceeded (FR-081). /ready exists but currently returns lifecycle-only HTTP 200. Require HTTP 503 until backend prerequisites and required tool initialization succeed, then HTTP 200; include shutdown and verified existing tool data (spec D10). Add backend credential preflight to serve startup; add an "OpenAI Agents" resolved-config echo section. Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Concurrent in-flight turns are capped at the resolved value; overflow → 429 + Retry-After. - [ ] Idle sessions do not consume slots (cap is on active turns, FR-014). - [ ] Startup echoes the resolved cap + derivation; missing creds exit non-zero at startup (FR-012). Verification: tests/unit/serve/test_session_semaphore_openai_agents.py; serve smoke. Dependencies: A2 Files: src/holodeck/serve/server.py, src/holodeck/cli/commands/serve.py Scope: M

docs.title: Phase J — P2b credential redaction + subprocess scrub (US6)
Task J1: Default credential-redaction output guardrail
docs.text: Reconciled status: Pending / acceptance not established. Description: In openai_agents_guardrails.py (shared with E2), attach a default-on tool_output_guardrail to every HoloDeck-built FunctionTool (function, vectorstore, hier-doc, skill) that scrubs the 5 credential patterns (anthropic key, AWS access key, GitHub token, JWT, Bearer) from tool output before the model sees it: clean output → allow(); pattern found → reject_content(<redacted text>) (the SDK replaces the model-visible tool result with the message, and the redacted value is also what lands in the span output). Reuse redact_credentials() from claude_hooks.py. Opt-out: openai.disable_default_hooks: true with the loud warning. Coverage note (documented + tested): hosted tools execute server-side, and MCP-server tool outputs flow through SDK-built FunctionTools HoloDeck cannot wrap — both bypass this redaction (K3 matrix; SC-009 scope is HoloDeck-built tools; J2's OTel-layer redaction still covers MCP/hosted span attributes). Acceptance criteria: - [ ] A tool returning sk-ant-api03-… is seen by the model as [REDACTED:anthropic-key] (via the output guardrail, not return-value mutation). - [ ] Clean outputs pass through unmodified (allow() path). - [ ] Opt-out disables it with a warning; OTel redaction (J2) still runs. Verification: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_guardrails.py (redaction + opt-out). Dependencies: B1, E2 (shared guardrail module) Files: src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_guardrails.py, src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_tool_adapters.py Scope: M

Acceptance criteria: - [ ] A spawned MCP stdio child does not inherit the scrubbed credential vars. - [ ] An openai_agents span's tool.output.* credential value is redacted (regression test). Verification: tests/unit/lib/backends/test_openai_agents_hooks.py; tests/unit/lib/backends/test_otel_redaction.py (add openai case). Dependencies: C1 Files: src/holodeck/lib/backends/openai_agents_hooks.py (or a small subprocess wrapper) Scope: S
