docs.text:
• Agent Configuration — tool usage in context
  • Vector Stores — RAG provider setup
  • MCP CLI — discovering and managing MCP servers
  • File References — path resolution
  • Examples — complete tool usage

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.7.x to 0.8
docs.text:
HoloDeck 0.8 removes Semantic Kernel, splits the install into feature extras, and moves vector stores onto HoloDeck's own adapters. This guide lists what to check, in the order to check it. Each step says what changed, how to find out if it affects you, and what to do.

The full list of changes is in the changelog.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
For most projects, these three commands cover the upgrade. Run them in the project folder, then read the steps for anything they report.

pip install --upgrade "holodeck-ai[all]"      # everything installed as before
holodeck test run agent.yaml                  # a retired metric or provider fails here, before any model call
holodeck vectorstore inspect agent.yaml       # read-only: do your collections need a rebuild?

Expected: the test run either starts, or stops at once with a message that names the metric, provider or extra to change.

docs.title: Step 1: Check your install extras
docs.text:
pip install holodeck-ai now installs less. These features moved into extras:

You use Install DeepEval metrics (type: geval, rag, and other LLM-judged metrics) or NLP metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR) pip install "holodeck-ai[eval,nlp]" holodeck test optimize pip install "holodeck-ai[optimizer]" (add eval,nlp for its metrics) An OpenSearch keyword index pip install "holodeck-ai[opensearch]" A vector store pip install "holodeck-ai[qdrant]", chromadb, postgres, pinecone, weaviate, azure-ai-search or azure-cosmos; vectorstores installs all of them Everything as before pip install "holodeck-ai[all]"

all installs every runtime extra. MkDocs Material and Twine are now in the dev extra only.

A command that needs a missing extra stops early and prints the install command. For example, holodeck test run stops before any agent or model call when a metric needs eval and it is not installed. Commands that do not need the extra still start.

docs.title: Step 2: Update retired metric names
docs.text:
The Azure AI evaluation metrics are removed, together with the azure-ai-evaluation package. An agent.yaml that names one fails when the configuration loads, before any agent or model call. The error names the replacement. HoloDeck does not translate the old configuration, and the new scores are not equivalent to the old ones. Run the suite again and set new thresholds.

Removed metric Use instead (DeepEval) groundedness type: rag, metric_type: faithfulness relevance type: rag, metric_type: answer_relevancy coherence type: geval with coherence criteria fluency type: geval with fluency criteria similarity type: geval with evaluation_params: [actual_output, expected_output] safety type: geval with safety criteria

Results stored by earlier runs that used these metrics still open in the dashboard. See Removed Azure AI metrics for a before and after example.

METEOR also changed. It no longer downloads NLTK data the first time it runs. If the data is missing, METEOR stops with an error that names the command. Run it once on each machine that scores METEOR:

python -m nltk.downloader wordnet punkt_tab omw-1.4

docs.title: Step 3: Update retired vector store providers
docs.text:
Three providers are retired. They had no install extra, sample or live test, and could not run from a documented install. An agent.yaml or config.yaml that names one fails at config load with a migration message, before any model call.

Retired provider Use instead faiss chromadb (embedded, local files) or in-memory sql-server postgres (pgvector) azure-cosmos-mongo azure-cosmos-nosql

HoloDeck does not copy data between providers. Point the tool at the new provider and start the agent. It ingests the source again. See Vector Stores for each provider's settings.

Two more changes affect vector store tools:

  • A missing client library is an error. Before, a vectorstore tool whose client was not installed logged a warning and stored data in memory. Now it fails and prints the install command (Step 1). A failure while the store adapter is created still falls back to memory. A client that connects on first use (Qdrant, for example) raises its connection error; it does not fall back.
  • Chroma scores changed. Chroma returned a distance that HoloDeck used as the score, so results ranked worst-first. The score is now 1 - distance, and the best match comes first. If you tuned min_similarity_score against the old behavior, check it.

docs.title: Step 4: Check your vector collections
docs.text:
HoloDeck now records the pipeline that wrote a collection: the embedding model and dimensions, the parser and splitter, the record layout and the retrieval mode. The record lives in a companion collection named holodeck_manifest in the same store. Your collection layout is unchanged.

Plain text chunking also changed. The splitter now counts real tokens (tiktoken cl100k_base), honors chunk_size as a hard limit and applies chunk_overlap. Chunk boundaries differ from 0.7, so a collection written by 0.7 holds different chunks than 0.8 would write.

Run the read-only check:

holodeck vectorstore inspect agent.yaml

It reports each collection, its record count, whether it matches the current pipeline, and what a rebuild would embed. It does not change anything and calls no model.

  • A collection created before 0.8 is marked legacy. It stays readable and writable, and keeps its old chunks until you re-ingest.
  • A collection written by a different pipeline stays searchable, but a write to it fails and lists the inputs that differ. This protects you from mixing old and new chunks in one collection.

To rebuild a collection with the current pipeline:

holodeck vectorstore migrate agent.yaml --tool NAME   # builds a new collection, verifies it, then switches; resumable
holodeck vectorstore rollback agent.yaml --tool NAME  # switch back to the old collection
holodeck vectorstore prune agent.yaml --tool NAME --yes  # delete the old collection when you are sure

migrate calls the embedding model and keeps the old collection until you run prune. Details are in Pipeline fingerprint and migration.

docs.title: Step 5: Rebuild deployment images
docs.text:
Images are now pinned. holodeck deploy build and the base image install one exact HoloDeck version, with dependency versions taken from that release's lock file. They no longer use --prerelease. Each build writes a manifest to .holodeck/builds/<tag>.json with the version, extras, base image digest and package list.

  • Rebuild your images with the 0.8 CLI. The build uses holodeck-base:<version> of the same release.
  • A development version that is not on PyPI needs --wheel dist/<wheel>.
  • Serving images carry only the extras the agent needs. They never carry eval, nlp or optimizer.

See Reproducible images.

docs.title: For Python code that imports HoloDeck
docs.text:
If your code imports HoloDeck modules, note these removals:

  • semantic-kernel is no longer installed by any profile. Remove any import of it that relied on HoloDeck bringing it in.
  • The holodeck.lib.vector_store module is gone. QueryResult and StructuredQueryResult now live in holodeck.lib.retrieval.
  • holodeck.lib.observability.enable_semantic_kernel_telemetry and the SK_OTEL_* constants are gone.
  • The default of observability.logs.filter_namespaces is now an empty list. It was ["semantic_kernel"].
  • mcp 2 is allowed (>=1.30.0,<3).

docs.title: Other breaking changes in 0.8
docs.text:
These do not come from the dependency work. See the changelog for each one:

  • Python 3.11 or later is required.
  • The tool_filtering agent field is removed. Delete the block.
  • The Claude backend isolates settings by default. Add setting_sources to the claude: block if your agent relied on host Claude configuration.
  • NotebookEdit and WebSearch need a declaration on the Claude backend.

docs.title: Vector Stores Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to set up and configure vector stores for semantic search (RAG) in HoloDeck agents.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Run a local Qdrant, point one vectorstore tool at a folder of documents, and chat with your agent. HoloDeck ingests the source on first run and answers from it.

# 1. Start a local Qdrant
docker run -d --name qdrant -p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant

# agent.yaml
name: knowledge-agent
model:
  provider: openai          # also works on provider: anthropic
  name: gpt-4o
instructions:
  inline: Search the knowledge base before answering.
tools:
  - name: search-kb
    type: vectorstore
    description: Search the knowledge base
    source: knowledge_base/  # folder of docs to ingest
    database:
      provider: qdrant
      connection_string: http://localhost:6333

holodeck chat   # ingests knowledge_base/ on first run, then answers from it

Expected: the agent calls search-kb, retrieves matching chunks, and grounds its reply in your documents.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: A vectorstore tool embeds your source documents into chunks and stores them in a vector database, then retrieves the most semantically similar chunks at query time to ground the agent's answer (RAG). Embeddings work across providers, and vectorstore (and hierarchical_document) RAG tools run on both the Claude and OpenAI backends. Each provider runs on a HoloDeck adapter that uses the store's own client library behind one contract, so every provider offers the same operations or says clearly which it lacks (see What each provider supports). See the OpenAI backend and Claude backend guides for backend specifics, and the Tools Guide for the full tool schema.

docs.title: Installing vector store providers
docs.text:
HoloDeck uses optional dependencies for vector database providers. Install only what you need:

uv add holodeck-ai[qdrant]        # Qdrant
uv add holodeck-ai[postgres]      # PostgreSQL with pgvector
uv add holodeck-ai[chromadb]      # ChromaDB
uv add holodeck-ai[pinecone]      # Pinecone
uv add holodeck-ai[weaviate]      # Weaviate
uv add holodeck-ai[azure-ai-search]  # Azure AI Search
uv add holodeck-ai[azure-cosmos]  # Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL
uv add holodeck-ai[vectorstores]  # all of the above

The same extras work with pip install holodeck-ai[<extra>].

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text:
Provider Best for Setup complexity qdrant High-performance production, hybrid search Medium chromadb Lightweight development, Python-native Low postgres Existing PostgreSQL infrastructure Medium pinecone Serverless, managed cloud Low weaviate Self-hosted or cloud, native hybrid search Medium azure-ai-search Azure-hosted search, native hybrid Medium azure-cosmos-nosql Existing Azure Cosmos DB accounts Medium in-memory Testing and prototyping None

See the Tools Guide for the complete list.

docs.title: What each provider supports
docs.text:
Every provider supports the core operations: upsert, get and delete by ID, exact metadata filtering, paginated listing, delete by metadata filter, record count and vector search. Lexical and hybrid search differ. Where a store has no native support, HoloDeck runs its own BM25 index and fuses the results, so the tool still works. An operation a provider cannot do fails before ingestion; it never returns empty results.

Provider Lexical search Hybrid search in-memory, chromadb, pinecone HoloDeck BM25 HoloDeck fusion qdrant Not offered alone (use hybrid) Native (dense plus full-text, RRF) postgres Native HoloDeck fusion weaviate, azure-ai-search Native Native azure-cosmos-nosql HoloDeck BM25 Native with full_text_search: true, otherwise HoloDeck fusion

Not every provider has been run against its hosted service. Pinecone and Azure AI Search ran on local emulators or fakes only, and Cosmos DB hybrid search ran on a fake. See Quality score.

docs.title: Removed vector store providers
docs.text:
HoloDeck 0.8.0 removed three providers. An agent.yaml or config.yaml that names one fails at config load with the migration advice below.

Removed Use instead faiss chromadb (embedded, local files) or in-memory for local development sql-server postgres (pgvector) for a SQL database azure-cosmos-mongo azure-cosmos-nosql

docs.title: Configuring vector stores
docs.text: You can configure a store inline (as in the Quick start) or define it once in global config and reference it by name.

docs.title: Global configuration (config.yaml)
docs.text:
Define reusable vector store connections, then reference them from any agent:

# config.yaml (project root or ~/.holodeck/config.yaml)
vectorstores:
  my-qdrant-store:
    provider: qdrant
    url: http://localhost:6333
  my-chroma-store:
    provider: chromadb
    connection_string: http://localhost:8000
  my-postgres-store:
    provider: postgres
    connection_string: ${DATABASE_URL}

# agent.yaml
tools:
  - name: search-kb
    type: vectorstore
    description: Search the knowledge base
    source: knowledge_base/
    database: my-qdrant-store   # reference to config.yaml

docs.title: Tuning ingestion and embeddings
docs.text:
Set embedding model and chunking on the tool. The embedding model is provider-neutral — pick one your configured model provider exposes:

tools:
  - name: search-kb
    type: vectorstore
    description: Search the knowledge base
    source: knowledge_base/
    database: my-qdrant-store
    embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small
    chunk_size: 512
    chunk_overlap: 50

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Store sensitive connection details in environment variables and reference them with ${VAR}:

# .env file (DO NOT commit to version control)
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb
QDRANT_API_KEY=your-api-key

Security: Always use ${VAR_NAME} for passwords, API keys, and sensitive connection details. Never commit plaintext credentials to version control.

docs.title: Running a vector database
docs.text: All providers below run locally in a container. You need a container runtime — Docker (recommended) or Podman. Podman commands are Docker-compatible; replace docker with podman in the examples.

docs.title: Qdrant
docs.text:
Qdrant is a high-performance vector database designed for production workloads. It supports HTTP and gRPC, and native hybrid (dense + sparse) search.

docker run -d \
  --name qdrant \
  -p 6333:6333 \
  -p 6334:6334 \
  -v $(pwd)/qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage:z \
  qdrant/qdrant

Exposes port 6333 (HTTP API) and 6334 (gRPC). Verify:

curl http://localhost:6333/healthz

Docker Compose:

services:
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    container_name: holodeck-qdrant
    ports:
      - "6333:6333"
      - "6334:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant-data:/qdrant/storage
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  qdrant-data:

For production, enable API key auth with QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY=${QDRANT_API_KEY}, and pin a version (e.g. qdrant/qdrant:v1.9.0) instead of latest.

Record IDs. A UUID record ID is the point ID. Any other ID becomes a stable UUIDv5 and the original is kept in the holodeck_id payload field. Two different IDs can never share a point: a write that would give two IDs of one call the same point ID (invoice-7 and the text of its own UUID), or overwrite a point that holds another ID, fails with a SchemaError. The stored layout does not change.

docs.title: ChromaDB
docs.text:
ChromaDB is a lightweight, Python-native embedding database that's ideal for development.

docker run -d \
  --name chromadb \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v ./chroma-data:/chroma/chroma \
  -e IS_PERSISTENT=TRUE \
  -e ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=FALSE \
  chromadb/chroma:latest

Exposes port 8000 (HTTP API). Verify:

curl http://localhost:8000/api/v2/heartbeat
Variable Description Default IS_PERSISTENT Enable data persistence FALSE PERSIST_DIRECTORY Path for persistent storage /chroma/chroma ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY Send anonymous usage data TRUE

Security Advisory: chromadb is currently affected by CVE-2026-45829 / GHSA-f4j7-r4q5-qw2c, a pre-authentication code injection issue in ChromaDB server versions 1.0.0 and later when the server accepts a malicious model repository with trust_remote_code=true. As of this documentation update, upstream has not published a fixed chromadb release. Until a fix is available, run ChromaDB only on trusted networks, do not expose it directly to the public internet, and treat model repository inputs as trusted administrative data.

docs.title: PostgreSQL with pgvector
docs.text:
PostgreSQL with pgvector provides production-grade vector storage with full SQL capabilities — ideal if you already run PostgreSQL.

docker run -d \
  --name postgres \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} \
  -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  pgvector/pgvector:pg17

Exposes port 5432. Verify:

docker exec -it postgres psql -U postgres -c "SELECT 1;"
Variable Description Default POSTGRES_PASSWORD Database password (required) - POSTGRES_USER Database user postgres POSTGRES_DB Default database name postgres

docs.title: Pinecone
docs.text:
Pinecone is a fully managed, serverless vector database. HoloDeck uses the pinecone client 10.x (holodeck-ai[pinecone]) over asyncio and creates one serverless, cosine index per collection:

database:
  provider: pinecone
  api_key: ${PINECONE_API_KEY}
  namespace: my-namespace  # optional
  cloud: aws               # optional, for a new index
  region: us-east-1        # optional, for a new index
Setting Meaning api_key, connection_string API key, or pinecone://key[@namespace]. PINECONE_API_KEY is the fallback. namespace Namespace of the records. Default: the default namespace. cloud, region Where a new serverless index runs. Default aws, us-east-1. index_name Index name instead of the collection name. host, index_host Control plane and data plane URLs, for a gateway or private endpoint.

Pinecone index names are lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 45 characters. A name that is already valid is used unchanged. Otherwise HoloDeck lower-cases it, turns other characters into hyphens and adds a short hash of the original name, so documents_dim1536 becomes documents-dim1536-<hash> and a_b and a-b never share an index. Set index_name or collection_name to a valid name to choose the index name yourself.

Record IDs must be ASCII (at most 512 characters). A source file with a non-ASCII path is rejected at ingestion with a clear error. Pinecone reads are eventually consistent, so a search right after ingestion can briefly miss new chunks.

A HoloDeck collection on Pinecone is the pair (index, namespace):

  • With the default namespace the collection is the whole index. Deleting the collection (holodeck vectorstore prune) deletes the index.
  • With a named namespace the collection is that namespace only. Deleting it deletes every record in the namespace and keeps the index, which other namespaces can share. Record counts and "exists" checks read the namespace. Pinecone has no empty namespaces, so a named namespace with no records reads as absent.

The pipeline manifest (see Pipeline fingerprint and migration) is one more small serverless index, holodeck-manifest-<hash>, per project and API key. Set manifest: false in the database settings if you cannot afford the extra index; fingerprint protection and holodeck vectorstore migrate are then off.

Note: Pinecone Local reached end of life on 2026-10-07. The last emulator image (ghcr.io/pinecone-io/pinecone-local:latest, 1.0.0-rc0) speaks the pre-10 control plane, so the 10.x client cannot create indexes on it. HoloDeck's own tests use it with a small test-only control plane. For local development use the cloud service, or the in-memory, Qdrant or ChromaDB providers.

docs.title: Weaviate
docs.text:
Weaviate is an open-source vector database with a managed cloud. HoloDeck uses the weaviate-client 4.x asynchronous client (holodeck-ai[weaviate]) and supports every retrieval operation, including Weaviate's own hybrid search (vector plus BM25), so a hybrid tool does not build an in-process keyword index.

# A server, for example Docker on this machine
database:
  provider: weaviate
  local_host: localhost
  local_port: 8080        # optional, default 8080
  local_grpc_port: 50051  # optional, default 50051

# Weaviate Cloud
database:
  provider: weaviate
  url: https://my-cluster.weaviate.cloud
  api_key: ${WEAVIATE_API_KEY}
### Azure AI Search

[Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/) is Azure's managed search service. HoloDeck uses the `azure-search-documents` 12.0 asyncio clients (`holodeck-ai[azure-ai-search]`, which also installs `azure-identity`) and keeps one index per collection:

```yaml
database:
  provider: azure-ai-search
  connection_string: https://my-service.search.windows.net
  api_key: ${AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY}   # omit to use Microsoft Entra ID
### Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL

HoloDeck uses the `azure-cosmos` async client (`holodeck-ai[azure-cosmos]`) and stores each collection in one container of a Cosmos DB for NoSQL account. The provider name is `azure-cosmos-nosql`:

```yaml
database:
  provider: azure-cosmos-nosql
  url: https://my-account.documents.azure.com:443/
  key: ${COSMOS_KEY}
  database_name: holodeck
  create_database: true   # optional
Setting Meaning url, api_key Weaviate Cloud cluster (https:// URL or host name) and its API key. The key is required. local_host, local_port, local_grpc_port A server over plain HTTP and gRPC. Set api_key too when the server uses API key authentication. connection_string https://<cluster> for Weaviate Cloud, or http://host[:port] for a server. Explicit settings win. collection_name Collection name instead of the default.

WEAVIATE_URL, WEAVIATE_LOCAL_HOST, WEAVIATE_LOCAL_PORT, WEAVIATE_LOCAL_GRPC_PORT and WEAVIATE_API_KEY are used when the settings name no server. Set exactly one of a cloud url and local_host; unknown settings are an error. The embedded Weaviate mode that Semantic Kernel offered (use_embed) is not supported; run a server.

To start a local server:

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -p 50051:50051 \
  -e AUTHENTICATION_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=true \
  -e PERSISTENCE_DATA_PATH=/var/lib/weaviate \
  -e DEFAULT_VECTORIZER_MODULE=none \
  cr.weaviate.io/semitechnologies/weaviate:1.40.4

Stored layout. One Weaviate collection per HoloDeck collection. Weaviate names start with an upper-case letter and use only A-Z a-z 0-9 _. A name that already fits is used unchanged. Any other name is cleaned (the first letter is upper-cased, every other character becomes _) and gets _ plus a short hash of the original name, so documents_dim1536 becomes Documents_dim1536_<hash> and docs, Docs and a-b/a_b never share a collection. Set collection_name to a name that fits to choose the collection name yourself. It holds one self-provided named vector embedding (cosine, flat index), one property per data field, and a holodeck_id text property. The record ID is the object UUID: a UUID is stored as it is, any other ID (chunk IDs are free text) becomes a stable UUIDv5 of the collection and the ID, and the original goes into holodeck_id. Two different IDs can never share an object: a write that would give two IDs of one call the same UUID (invoice-7 and the text of its own UUID), or overwrite an object that holds another ID, fails with a SchemaError. Fields marked indexed get a filter index, and string fields use field tokenization, so a filter such as source_path matches the whole value exactly and case-sensitively; other fields have no index, and a filter on one is an error. This is the layout Semantic Kernel's Weaviate connector writes, apart from the property indexes, holodeck_id and the field tokenization.

Limits to know:

  • Semantic Kernel's Weaviate path never worked against a server (its cosine setting was rejected and it could not store free-text IDs), so there are no earlier HoloDeck Weaviate collections to migrate.
  • Weaviate returns at most QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS (10,000 by default) results for one query. HoloDeck pages with the filter on the server while it stays under that limit. For a source with more chunks it reads the whole collection by cursor and applies the filter itself, so find, delete_where and replacing a large source still work, more slowly.
  • An existing collection must have the embedding named vector with cosine distance, matching property types and field tokenization on the string properties that tools filter on, or HoloDeck raises an IncompatibleCollectionError and leaves it alone. A collection that Semantic Kernel's connector creates uses word tokenization, which cannot match exactly, so it is refused. | connection_string, endpoint, search_endpoint | Service URL, https://<service>.search.windows.net. AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT is the fallback. | | api_key | Admin key. AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY is the fallback. With no key, DefaultAzureCredential (Microsoft Entra ID) signs in. | | index_name | Index name instead of the collection name. |

Unknown settings are an error. The index is created on first use with a key field id, one field per data field, and a vector field embedding with an HNSW cosine profile. Only fields that the tool filters on are filterable, and only the text field the keyword leg searches is searchable.

Search. All of vector, keyword and hybrid search run in the service. Hybrid mode is one request that carries the text query and the vector query, and the service fuses the two lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Keyword text is reduced to words first, so characters such as - or " in a question are not read as query operators. Vector scores are converted from Azure's 1 / (1 + distance) value to cosine similarity.

Record IDs and names. Azure keys allow only letters, digits, _, - and =, so an ID such as docs/policy.md_chunk_0 is stored as b64- plus its URL-safe Base64 text. An ID that is already a valid key is stored unchanged. An ID that starts with b64- is always encoded too, so a key that starts with b64- is always an encoding and the mapping is one to one. Index names are lowercase letters, digits, - and _. A name that already fits is used unchanged (documents_dim1536). Any other name is lower-cased, cleaned and gets - plus a short hash of the original name (Product Catalog.v2 becomes product-catalog-v2-<hash>), so a_b and a-b never share an index.

Existing indexes. An index that an earlier Semantic Kernel setup created has a key that cannot be sorted. Azure cannot change that on an existing index, so HoloDeck stops with an IncompatibleCollectionError. Delete the index or use another index_name. An index whose vector field compares vectors with another metric than cosine is refused in the same way.

Azure indexes documents asynchronously. After a delete, HoloDeck checks for up to 10 seconds that a search shows none of the deleted documents. After an upload it checks that a search shows every written document and that the last one has the written values and embedding. Then it continues, with a warning if the wait ran out. The document count is approximate while indexing runs.

Note: Azure AI Search has no local emulator, and this adapter has been verified only against an in-memory fake of the client and against the SDK's request shapes with a stubbed transport. It has not been run against the Azure service. Ordering of string keys in range filters, indexing delay, and score values are therefore unobserved. Treat the first run on a real service as a check, and report problems. | url (or endpoint), key | Account URL and key. The environment variables AZURE_COSMOS_DB_NO_SQL_URL and AZURE_COSMOS_DB_NO_SQL_KEY are the fallbacks. Token credentials cannot be set from YAML. | | connection_string | The portal form AccountEndpoint=...;AccountKey=...; instead of url and key. | | database_name | Database that holds the container. Fallback: AZURE_COSMOS_DB_NO_SQL_DATABASE_NAME. | | create_database | Create the database when it is missing. Default false: a missing database is an error. | | vector_index | flat, quantizedFlat or diskANN, for a container HoloDeck creates. Default: flat up to 505 dimensions, quantizedFlat above (4096 at most). | | full_text_search | true creates a full-text policy and index and uses the service's hybrid search (ORDER BY RANK RRF). Default false. See below. | | partition_key | Only id or /id. |

The account needs the vector search capability (EnableNoSQLVectorSearch). full_text_search also needs the full-text search capability. Unknown settings are an error.

Layout. The container has the collection's name and the partition key /id. A document is {id, <fields>, embedding}. The vector embedding policy is float32, cosine, with the collection's dimensions. Fields that are neither indexed nor full-text are excluded from the index, and so is the vector. This is the layout Semantic Kernel created, so containers created before the move keep working. HoloDeck never changes an existing container. It rejects one with other dimensions or another partition key (IncompatibleCollectionError).

Vector index. Semantic Kernel always used flat, which Cosmos DB limits to 505 dimensions, so it could not create a container for the default 1536-dimension embeddings. HoloDeck chooses quantizedFlat there. Cosmos DB cannot change a vector index in place, so set vector_index before the first run.

Record IDs. Cosmos DB rejects item IDs with /, \, ? or #, and HoloDeck chunk IDs often contain a file path. An ID that Cosmos DB accepts is stored unchanged. Any other ID is stored as ~hd~ plus the URL-safe base64 of the ID, and the original is kept in the holodeck_id field. HoloDeck decodes the ID on every read.

Hybrid search. With full_text_search: false (the default) HoloDeck fuses its own BM25 results with the vector results, as it does for Postgres. With true, the keyword leg runs in Cosmos DB. This needs a full-text index. Cosmos DB cannot add one to an existing container, and Semantic Kernel never created one. For a container from the old path, keep the default or use a new container (a new collection_name). HoloDeck reports a container without the index with IncompatibleCollectionError. The service does not return the fused score, so hybrid results carry a rank-based score: only their order means something.

What was verified where. The adapter passes the shared contract suite on the Linux Cosmos DB emulator (mcr.microsoft.com/cosmosdb/linux/azure-cosmos-emulator:vnext-preview, --protocol http) for every operation except hybrid search. It passes the whole suite, hybrid search included, on a test fake of the container API. The emulator accepts only the diskANN index, does not check the account key, does not report the vector embedding policy back, and does not support full-text search (FullTextScore, RRF): it drops the full-text policy and index. So full_text_search: true, the ORDER BY RANK RRF query, the flat and quantizedFlat indexes, key authentication and throttling have not run against a Cosmos DB service. The hybrid query text follows the service documentation and is checked by unit tests only.

docs.text:
my-agent-project/
├── config.yaml
├── agent.yaml
├── .env
├── knowledge_base/
│   ├── faq.json
│   └── docs.md

# config.yaml
providers:

    provider: openai
    name: gpt-4o
    api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}

vectorstores:
  knowledge-store:
    provider: qdrant
    url: http://localhost:6333

# agent.yaml
name: support-agent
description: Customer support agent with knowledge base search

model:
  provider: openai
  name: gpt-4o
  temperature: 0.7

instructions:
  inline: |
    You are a customer support specialist.
    Always search the knowledge base before answering questions.

tools:
  - name: search-kb
    description: Search knowledge base for answers to customer questions
    type: vectorstore
    source: knowledge_base/
    database: knowledge-store
    embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small
    chunk_size: 512
    chunk_overlap: 50

test_cases:

    input: "How do I reset my password?"
    expected_tools: [search-kb]

# docker-compose.yml
services:

    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    container_name: holodeck-qdrant
    ports:
      - "6333:6333"

volumes:

Run it:

docker compose up -d           # 1. Start Qdrant
curl http://localhost:6333/healthz   # 2. Verify it's up
holodeck test                  # 3. Run the agent (uses agent.yaml by default)

docs.title: Pipeline fingerprint and migration
docs.text: Records in a collection depend on more than its schema. HoloDeck records the pipeline that wrote a collection and refuses to mix records from two different pipelines in one collection.

docs.title: What is fingerprinted
docs.text:
The fingerprint is a SHA-256 hash of these inputs:

Input vectorstore tool hierarchical_document tool Embedding provider, model, dimensions provider, model, dimensions Parser markitdown/1 (structured-rows/1 for CSV/JSON rows) markitdown/1 Chunker plain-tiktoken-cl100k/1, chunk_size, chunk_overlap (rows: vector fields, field separator) structured-chunker/1, max_chunk_tokens, document_domain, max_subsection_depth Record layout field names, types and index flags, key and vector field, dimensions, distance same Retrieval none contextual embeddings on or off, searchable-text/1 recipe; when on, the context generator (litellm-context/1 or claude-sdk-context/1 recipe, its model, context_max_tokens, document truncation), context_model provider and name Structured rows vector fields, field_separator, id_field, delimiter, meta_fields -

Search settings such as top_k, min_similarity_score and the search mode are not part of the fingerprint: they do not change stored records.

docs.title: The manifest collection
docs.text:
HoloDeck does not add fields to your collections. It keeps its state in one extra collection per store connection, holodeck_manifest, which it creates through the same provider. The manifest holds:

  • one entry per collection: the fingerprint, the physical collection that currently serves the tool, and the collection kept for rollback;
  • one entry per ingested source file: the expected chunk count and a completion flag. A source is marked incomplete before its chunks are written and complete after the last write. A source whose ingestion stopped midway (a crash, a failed write) is ingested again on the next start.

A collection's manifest entry is keyed by its logical name: the name the provider is asked for, which is index_name when set, else collection_name, else the default (documents_dim<N>, the tool name for structured data, hierarchical_docs_<tool>_dim<N>). Two tools with the same logical name share one collection and one entry; two tools with different names have their own.

A provider that cannot hold the manifest logs one warning and works as before, without fingerprint protection. Settings that address one collection (collection_name, index_name, Pinecone index_host) do not apply to the manifest: it is stored in its own holodeck_manifest collection or index.

If the manifest collection does not exist and cannot be created (a quota, a missing permission, a provider error), HoloDeck logs one warning that names the cause and says fingerprint protection is off, and the tool works as before. If the manifest exists but cannot be read or written, an established pointer or fingerprint may be in it: searches still work and every write is refused until the store answers again.

Set manifest: false in a tool's database settings to turn the manifest off on purpose (no warning). Fingerprint protection, completion markers and the holodeck vectorstore migration commands are then off for that store.

database:
  provider: pinecone
  api_key: ${PINECONE_API_KEY}
  manifest: false

docs.title: Concurrent starts
docs.text:
Two processes that start at the same time can both find no manifest entry. Vector stores have no portable compare-and-set, so HoloDeck narrows the race this way:

  • every write of a collection entry carries a new random revision;
  • after writing the entry, a tool reads it back and writes data only if the stored revision is its own. Otherwise the other process's entry decides: the same fingerprint allows writes, a different one refuses them;
  • immediately before the first write of each source file, the tool reads the entry again (one read per file) and refuses to write if the fingerprint or the physical collection changed. If only the revision changed, the tool continues with the new entry once.

This narrows the race but cannot remove it on a store without transactions: two writers can still interleave between the last check and a write. Do not start agents with different pipelines against one collection at the same time. The manifest update on PostgreSQL uses the same read-back rule; it does not take a transaction or advisory lock.

docs.title: What happens at start-up
docs.text:
Situation Result New or empty collection The current fingerprint is recorded. Structured data (CSV, JSON, JSONL) The source file gets a completion marker with its row count. An unchanged file with a complete marker is not embedded again; a changed file is embedded again. Collection created before this release (no manifest entry) It stays readable. Unchanged files are not embedded again. A changed file is replaced as a whole. HoloDeck records the current pipeline marked legacy and logs that holodeck vectorstore migrate rebuilds the collection. Same fingerprint Normal incremental ingestion. Different fingerprint Searches read the existing records. Any write (a changed file, --force-ingest) fails with an error that lists the inputs that differ and names the commands below.

HoloDeck never deletes or recreates a collection on its own.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
# Read-only dry run: collection, record count, compatibility, the inputs that
# differ, and the files, chunks and estimated tokens a migration embeds.
holodeck vectorstore inspect agent.yaml [--tool NAME] [--json]

# Build a new collection <name>__<fingerprint prefix> with the current
# pipeline, verify it, then switch to it. --tool selects the collection; every
# tool of the agent that uses it is rebuilt. The old collection is kept.
holodeck vectorstore migrate agent.yaml --tool NAME [--yes] [--restart] [--drop-unlisted-sources]

# Switch back to the kept collection.
holodeck vectorstore rollback agent.yaml --tool NAME [--yes]

# Delete the kept collection. The only command that deletes a collection.
holodeck vectorstore prune agent.yaml --tool NAME --yes
  • inspect is strictly read-only: it downloads nothing, creates no file, directory, collection or manifest entry, and calls no model. It counts chunks by parsing and splitting local sources. A remote source (s3://, https://, ...) is listed as "remote source: not estimated". The token figure is an estimate: tiktoken cl100k_base tokens of the chunk text, without the text that contextual embeddings add.
  • migrate works on a collection. Several tools can share one (plain vectorstore tools share documents_dim<N> unless they set collection_name), so every tool of the agent bound to the selected tool's collection is rebuilt together, and the plan lists them. They must have the same pipeline; if not, migrate refuses and shows the inputs that differ.
  • migrate lists every source file before it embeds anything. A source that fails to parse, produces no chunks or does not finish fails the migration; nothing is skipped silently.
  • Before it switches, migrate checks that the old collection holds no source that the migration did not rebuild (for example, files written by a tool in another agent file). If it does, migrate lists them and does not switch. Pass --drop-unlisted-sources to switch without them.
  • migrate calls the embedding model. If it stops (for example, the embedding service fails), run it again: files that were completed are not embedded again. The tools keep using the old collection until every source of the new one is complete with its expected chunk count, the total record count matches, and it answers a vector search. A migration for a different pipeline that is still in progress blocks a new one; add --restart to abandon it. Run prune before a second migration if a collection is still kept from the first.
  • migrate, rollback and prune take a lock on the collection in the manifest while they run (a lock record with an owner, the command, and the time it was taken). A second command on the same collection reports who holds the lock and exits with an error. A lock that is not refreshed for two hours is stale and the next command takes it over; a running migration refreshes it every ten minutes.
  • rollback checks that the kept collection still exists, under the lock, immediately before it switches.
  • prune first removes the kept collection from the manifest (it is marked reserved for deletion), then deletes it. If the delete fails, run prune again to finish; rollback never points at a collection being deleted.
  • migrate, rollback and prune print what they will do and ask for confirmation unless you pass --yes.

docs.title: Cannot connect to the vector database
docs.text:
Error: Connection refused or Cannot connect to http://localhost:<port>

  1. Verify the container is running: docker ps | grep <name>
  2. Check logs: docker logs <name>
  3. Test connectivity (Qdrant: curl http://localhost:6333/healthz; ChromaDB: curl http://localhost:8000/api/v2/heartbeat)
  4. Ensure the port isn't blocked by a firewall

Error messages never contain the API key, password or connection string you configured: HoloDeck replaces them with ***. An API key or header value that contains a control character (a trailing newline from a file or environment variable, for example) is rejected when the adapter is created, with a message that names the setting but not its value.

docs.title: Data not persisting
docs.text: Mount a named volume for persistence — e.g. -v qdrant-data:/qdrant/storage (Qdrant) or -v chroma-data:/chroma/chroma -e IS_PERSISTENT=TRUE (ChromaDB).

docs.title: Container already exists
docs.text:
Error: container name "<name>" is already in use

Remove the existing container: docker rm -f <name>
